10.title: Property Location And Size
10.text:
SEC. S-10.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 10 is established on property generally bounded by Cedar Springs Road, Douglas Street, Hall Street, and Knight Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 10 is approximately 4.58 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Definitions And Interpretations
10.text:
SEC. S-10.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this division refer to articles, divisions, or sections of Chapter 51.

(c) Section 51-2.101, “Interpretations,” applies to this division.

(d) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this division and in Chapter 51 triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning subdistrict or district, and for purposes of interpreting the requirements of Division 51-4.800, this subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district.

(e) In the event that PD 193 ever ceases to exist and the Property is not rezoned at that time, all references in this division to uses and development standards in PD 193 mean those uses and development standards as they last were in that district. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Development/Landscape Plan
10.text:
SEC. S-10.104. DEVELOPMENT/LANDSCAPE PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development/landscape plan (Exhibit S-10A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and the development/landscape plan, the provisions of this division control. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Main Uses Permitted
10.text:
SEC. S-10.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only uses authorized by this PD subdistrict are:

(1) Retail uses.

(2) Library, art gallery, or museum uses. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Accessory Uses
10.text:
SEC. S-10.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
10.text:
SEC. S-10.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Building setbacks. Minimum required setback along Douglas Avenue is 10 feet. Required setbacks along Cedar Springs Road, Douglas Avenue, and Hall Street are as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(b) Height. No structure may exceed 25 feet in height, except that certain structures on top of a building as listed in Section 51P-193.123(a)(2)(A), including a parapet wall, may project a maximum additional height of six feet. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
10.text:
SEC. S-10.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Off-street parking and loading must be located as shown on the development/landscape plan. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Landscaping
10.text:
SEC. S-10.109. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Tree Preservation
10.text:
SEC. S-10.110. TREE PRESERVATION.

The tree preservation regulations contained in Division 51A-10.130 of Chapter 51A apply to this Property. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Sidewalks
10.text:
SEC. S-10.111. SIDEWALKS.

(a) Sidewalks with a minimum unobstructed width of six feet are required along Cedar Springs Road, Douglas Avenue, and Knight Street.

(b) The sidewalk along Hall Street is required to have a minimum unobstructed width of five feet. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Traffic-Related Improvements
10.text:
SEC. S-10.112. TRAFFIC-RELATED IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) The existing island and associated “free right turn” that exist at the intersection of Douglas Avenue and Cedar Springs Road must be removed and a new curb relocating the right turn movement into the intersection must be constructed, as shown on the development/landscape plan. The

existing traffic signal equipment at this island must be relocated as directed by the department of public works and transportation.

(b) The curb adjacent to the Property along Cedar Springs Road from Douglas Avenue to the proposed Cedar Springs driveway must be realigned as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(c) A separator island must be constructed in the Cedar Springs driveway to limit vehicular movement to right-in and right-out only, as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(d) All required traffic-related improvements to the Property and the adjacent street rights-of- way listed in Subsections (a), (b), and (c) above must be constructed before issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any retail use on the Property. Pavement markings, signs, traffic signals, and utility relocations associated with the traffic-related improvements must also be constructed before issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any retail use. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Signs
10.text:
SEC. S-10.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII, except that:

(1) Only one detached sign for all retail uses combined is permitted. The sign must be located as shown on the development/landscape plan. The sign may have a maximum height of five and one-half feet and a maximum length of 15 feet. No attached signs are permitted on building facades facing Douglas, Hall, and Knight Streets.

(2) Non-premise signs are prohibited. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: Other Oak Lawn Spd Requirements
10.text:
SEC. S-10.114. OTHER OAK LAWN SPD REQUIREMENTS.

Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the development/landscape plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

10.title: General Requirements
10.text:
SEC. S-10.115. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267; 26102)

10.title: Paving
10.text:
SEC. S-10.116. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267; 26102)

10.title: Compliance With Conditions
10.text:
SEC. S-10.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267; 26102)

10.title: Zoning Map
10.text:
SEC. S-10.118. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 10 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. Nos. 22411; 25267)

11.title: Legislative History
11.text:
SEC. S-11.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 11 was established by Ordinance No. 22477, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 28, 1995. Ordinance No. 22477 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 22477; 25267)

11.title: Property Location And Size
11.text:
SEC. S-11.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 11 is established on property generally located at the north corner of Lyte Street and Houston Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 11 is approximately 5.3038 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 28087)

11.title: Definitions And Interpretations
11.text:
SEC. S-11.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 apply.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Chapter 51.

(c) This subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267)

SEC. S-11.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-11A: Tract II development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-11B: tract boundary descriptions.

(3) Exhibit S-11C: landscape plan.

(4) Exhibit S-11D: Tract 1 development plan. (Ords. 28087; 29718)

11.title: Development Plan
11.text:
SEC. S-11.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Tract I. Development and use of the Property must comply with the Tract I development plan (Exhibit S11-D). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the Tract I development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) Tract II. Development and use of the Property must comply with the Tract II development plan (Exhibit S-11A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the Tract II development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 29718)

11.title: Main Uses Permitted
11.text:
SEC. S-11.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Commercial uses.

-- Attached non-premise sign. [SUP] [Tract I only.]

(b) Community service uses.

-- Child-care facility. [SUP] -- Community service center. [SUP]

(c) Recreation uses.

-- Public golf course. -- Public park or playground. -- Private recreation club or area.

(d) Residential uses.

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. -- Multiple-family. -- Single-family.

(e) Transportation uses.

-- Private street or alley.

(f) Utility and public service uses.

-- Electrical substation. [SUP] -- Local utilities. -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. [SUP]

(g) Wholesale, distribution, and storage uses.

-- Recycling drop-off container. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 28087)

11.title: Accessory Uses
11.text:
SEC. S-11.107. ACCESSORY USES.

The open storage accessory use is not permitted in this district. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267)

11.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
11.text:
SEC. S-11.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard. No minimum front yard setback.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) No minimum side or rear yard for single-family structures.

(2) Minimum side and rear yard for other permitted structures is as shown on the Tract I development plan and the Tract II development plan.

(c) Density. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(d) Floor area ratio. No maximum floor area ratio.

(e) Height and stories. Maximum structure height is 70 feet. No maximum number of stories.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent for residential structures and 100 percent for nonresidential structures.

(g) Lot size. Minimum lot area is 1,655 square feet. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 29718)

11.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
11.text:
SEC. S-11.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) For single-family uses, the following apply:

(1) A minimum of two off-street parking spaces are required per lot.

(2) Garages may not be enclosed into a living area unless provisions are made to provide required parking.

(3) A parking space must be at least 10 feet from the right-of-way line adjacent to a street or alley if the space is located in an enclosed structure and if the space faces upon or can be entered directly from the street or alley. This provision controls over any building line platted to a lesser setback and any other provision of this district.

(4) Any garage door setback less then 20 feet from the right-of-way adjacent to a street or alley must be equipped with electric automatic control. The controls must be maintained in working condition at all times.

(b) For all other uses, off-street parking and loading must be provided as shown on the Tract I development plan and the Tract II development plan.

(c) Except as provided in this section, off-street parking must be provided at or below ground level.

(d) Two levels of above-ground parking are permitted for Building J. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 29718)

11.title: Environmental Performance Standards
11.text:
SEC. S-11.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267)

11.title: Access
11.text:
SEC. S-11.111. ACCESS.

Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the Tract I development plan and Tract II development plan. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 29718)

11.title: Landscaping
11.text:
SEC. S-11.112. LANDSCAPING.

Landscaping must comply with the landscape plan (Exhibit S-11C). Landscaping must be served by an automatic underground irrigation system. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. The property owner or homeowners’ association is responsible for the proper maintenance of all landscaping on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267)

11.title: Screening
11.text:
SEC. S-11.113. SCREENING.

A minimum six-foot-high screening wall must be installed as shown on the Tract II development plan. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 29718)

11.title: Homeowner’S Association
11.text:
SEC. S-11.114. HOMEOWNER’S ASSOCIATION.

Prior to final plat approval, the owner(s) of the Property must execute an instrument creating a homeowners’ association for the maintenance of common areas, screening walls, landscape areas (including perimeter landscaping areas), private streets, and for other functions. This instrument must be approved as to form by the city attorney, approved by the city plan commission, and filed in the Dallas County Deed Records. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267)

11.title: General Requirements
11.text:
SEC. S-11.115. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 26102)

11.title: Paving
11.text:
SEC. S-11.116. PAVING.

Except for the right-of-way widths of the private streets shown on the Tract II development plan and which must be constructed as shown on that plan, all paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 26102; 29718)

11.title: Compliance With Conditions
11.text:
SEC. S-11.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22477; 25267; 26102)

12.title: Legislative History
12.text:
SEC. S-12.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 12 was established by Ordinance No. 22645, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 10, 1996. Ordinance No. 22645 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 22645; 25267)

12.title: Property Location And Size
12.text:
SEC. S-12.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 12 is established on property generally located along the southeast line of Inwood Road, northeast of the intersection of Inwood Road and Lemmon Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 12 is approximately 3.3833 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Definitions And Interpretations
12.text:
SEC. S-12.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Division S-12 is incorporated by reference into Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict, Division S-12 controls.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Part I of this article.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Part I of this article.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Development Plan
12.text:
SEC. S-12.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the site plan (Exhibit S-12A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and the site plan, the provisions of this division control. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Uses Permitted
12.text:
SEC. S-12.105. USES PERMITTED.

(a) The only use allowed on the Property is self-storage. For purposes of this subdistrict, a self-storage use is defined as a building or group of buildings containing one or more individual compartmentalized storage units for the inside storage of customers’ goods or wares, where no unit exceeds 500 square feet in floor area. Caretaker’s quarters are permitted on the Property. Caretaker’s quarters must be located in Building N as shown on the site plan.

(b) Sexually oriented businesses as defined in Chapter 41A of the Dallas City Code, as amended, are specifically prohibited. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
12.text:
SEC. S-12.106. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Setbacks. Buildings must be placed as shown on the site plan.

(b) Floor area. Maximum floor area permitted on the Property is 89,000 square feet.

(c) Height and stories. Maximum structure height and maximum stories permitted for each individual building identified on the site plan is as follows:

Building Maximum Height Maximum Stories

A and B 18 feet One D and J 30 feet Two N 28 feet Two All other buildings 11 feet One

(d) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 44 percent. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Off-Street Parking
12.text:
SEC. S-12.107. OFF-STREET PARKING.

Parking for self-storage uses must be provided at a ratio of one parking space for each 3,000 square feet of floor area. Parking must be provided in the location shown on the site plan. If the caretaker’s quarters are provided, two additional parking spaces must be provided in the location shown on the site plan. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Environmental Performance Standards
12.text:
SEC. S-12.108. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI of Chapter 51. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Landscaping
12.text:
SEC. S-12.109. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Before issuance of a certificate of occupancy for the first building developed on the Property, landscaping must be provided along that portion of the property line that adjoins the public alley as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-12B).

(b) All landscaping shown on the landscape plan, except landscaping described in Subsection
(a) above, must be installed within 18 months after January 10, 1996.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Screening
12.text:
SEC. S-12.110. SCREENING.

(a) Before issuance of a certificate of occupancy for the first building developed on the Property, a minimum six-foot-high solid screening wall must be provided along that portion of the property line that adjoins the public alley as shown on the site plan.

(b) The screening requirements of Subsection (a) may be satisfied as to any portion of the Property that adjoins the building by the construction of Buildings C, H, or L as shown on the site plan. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: Signs
12.text:
SEC. S-12.111. SIGNS.

(a) Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII of Chapter 51.

(b) One detached premise sign is permitted in the location shown on the site plan.

(c) Non-premise signs are not permitted.

(d) Signs are not permitted within the required visibility triangles. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

12.title: General Requirements
12.text:
SEC. S-12.112. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267; 26102)

12.title: Paving
12.text:
SEC. S-12.113. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267; 26102)

12.title: Compliance With Conditions
12.text:
SEC. S-12.114. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267; 26102)

12.title: Zoning Map
12.text:
SEC. S-12.115. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 12 is located on Zoning Map No. H-6. (Ord. Nos. 22645; 25267)

13.title: Legislative History
13.text:
SEC. S-13.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 13 was established by Ordinance No. 22721, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 10, 1996. Ordinance No. 22721 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 22721 was amended by Ordinance No. 22985, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 8, 1997. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 22721; 22985; 25267)

13.title: Property Location And Size
13.text:
SEC. S-13.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 130 is established on property generally located along the southeast line of Cole Avenue, between the northeast line of Hall Street and the southwest line of Lemmon Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 13 is approximately 2.1942 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Definitions And Interpretations
13.text:
SEC. S-13.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this division refer to articles, divisions, or sections of Chapter 51.

(c) Section 51-2.101, “Interpretations,” applies to this division.

(d) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this division and in Chapter 51 triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning subdistrict or district, and for purposes of interpreting the requirements of Division 51-4.800, this subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district.

(e) In the event that PD 193 ever ceases to exist and the Property is not rezoned at that time, all references in this division to sections and development standards in PD 193 mean those uses and development standards as they last were in that district. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Development Plan
13.text:
SEC. S-13.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-13A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and the development plan, the provisions of this division control. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Main Uses Permitted
13.text:
SEC. S-13.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in Subsections (b) and (c) below, the only uses permitted on the Property are those uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use

permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict by specific use permit (SUP) is only permitted in this PD subdistrict by SUP.

(b) In addition to those uses permitted in Subsection (a), uses permitted in the SC Shopping Center Subdistrict are permitted on the ground level.

(c) The commercial parking lot or garage use is permitted but limited to that portion of the Property identified on the development plan as the “parking structure.” (Ord. Nos. 22985; 25267)

13.title: Accessory Uses
13.text:
SEC. S-13.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
13.text:
SEC. S-13.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is three and one-half feet. Parking may be located in the front yard. Balcony ground supports, as shown on the development plan, are allowed in the required front yard.

(b) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is four feet. Parking may be located in the side or rear yard. Balcony ground supports, as shown on the development plan, are allowed in the required side and rear yard.

(c) Dwelling units. No maximum number of dwelling units on the ground level. On all levels above ground level, a maximum of 210 dwelling units are permitted.

(d) Floor area.

(1) Maximum floor area permitted on the Property is 176,500 square feet for all uses.

(2) Of the 176,500 square feet of floor area permitted for all uses, a maximum of 13,000 square feet of floor area is permitted on the ground level for nonresidential uses.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 55 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 75 percent for all structures. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
13.text:
SEC. S-13.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) For a residential use, parking must be provided at a minimum of one parking space per dwelling unit. Parking may be provided in the required yards.

(b) For all other permitted uses, off-street parking must be provided at a ratio of one parking space per 220 square feet of floor area. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Environmental Performance Standards
13.text:
SEC. S-13.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Landscaping
13.text:
SEC. S-13.110. LANDSCAPING.

All landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-13B), and completed in accordance with the landscaping requirements contained in Part I of this article. Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: Signs
13.text:
SEC. S-13.111. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

13.title: General Requirements
13.text:
SEC. S-13.112. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267; 26102)

13.title: Paving
13.text:
SEC. S-13.113. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267; 26102)

13.title: Compliance With Conditions
13.text:
SEC. S-13.114. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267; 26102)

13.title: Zoning Map
13.text:
SEC. S-13.115. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 13 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. Nos. 22721; 25267)

14.title: Legislative History
14.text:
SEC. S-14.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 14 was established by Ordinance No. 22871, passed by the Dallas City Council on September 11, 1996. Ordinance No. 22871 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 22871 was amended by Ordinance No. 24173, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 26, 2000. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 22871; 24173; 25267)

14.title: Property Location And Size
14.text:
SEC. S-14.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 14 is established on property generally located along the southwest line of Dickason Avenue, southeast of the southeast line of Welborn Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 14 is approximately 1.118 acres. (Ord. Nos. 22871; 25267)

Food is prepared in a central kitchen. Assisted living facilities must be licensed as Personal Care Facilities under Chapter 247 of the Texas Health and Safety Code. Nos. 10962; 21859; 22954; 25267; 28917)

16.title: Property Location And Size
16.text:
SEC. S-16.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 16 is established on property generally located on the east corner of Harwood Street and Wolf Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 16 is approximately .9968acres. (Ord. Nos. 22954; 22567; 28917)

SEC. S-16.102.1. PURPOSE STATEMENT.

The standards for this division complement the development pattern in the area and recognize the area’s unique identity as a gateway to downtown and a bridge between downtown and Oak Lawn. The objectives of these standards are as follows:

(1) To promote the health, safety, welfare, convenience, and enjoyment of the public.

(2) To achieve buildings more in urban form.

(3) To promote a pedestrian environment and provide public open space.

(4) To encourage development that complements nearby properties.

(5) To achieve buildings efficient in design and use of space while providing adequate view corridors, light, and air to nearby properties.

(6) To achieve buildings that reduce natural resources consumption, enhance occupant comfort and health, lower utility consumption, minimize strain on local infrastructures, and improve quality of life.

(7) To promote new sign construction and existing sign alterations that:

(A) enhance, preserve, and develop the unique character of the district;

(B) insure compatibility with the areas architectural character;

(C) do not obstruct significant architectural features; and

(D) promote the safety of pedestrians and motorists. (Ord. 28917)

16.title: Definitions And Interpretations
16.text:
SEC. S-16.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(b) In this division:

(1) CANOPY means a permanent, non-fabric architectural element projecting from the facade of a building.

(2) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord Nos. 22954; 25267; 28917)

SEC. S-16.103.1. EXHIBITS.

For example, a use permitted in the O-2 Office Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

16.text:
SEC. S-16.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the O-2 Office Subdistrict apply.

(b) Front yard.

(1) Minimum front yards are:

(A) 20 feet along McKinnon Street;

(B) No front yard is required along Wolf Street or Harwood Street.

(2) The following items are permitted in a front yard in the locations shown on the development plan:

(A) Water features.

(B) A monument sign.

(C) Bike racks.

(D) Trellises. [May not exceed 10 feet in height on McKinnon Street.]

(E) Landscape feature (solid panels).

(c) Side and rear yard. No minimum side or rear yard is required.

(d) Floor area.

(1) Maximum floor area is 174,000 square feet.

(2) Additional street level uses listed in Section 51P-193.110(c)(2) may not have a floor area greater than 3,000 square feet each.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 300 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 22954; 25267; 28917)

See Article VI. (Ord, Nos. 22954; 25267; 28917)

16.title: Parking Structures
16.text:
SEC. S-16.110. PARKING STRUCTURES.

(a) Parking structures must be underground or have a facade that is similar in appearance to the facade of the main structure.

(b) A minimum of 12 percent of the aboveground parking structure facade area, including openings, must have the same materials as are used on the first 24 feet of the main structure.

(c) Openings in an aboveground parking structure facade may not exceed 52 percent of the total aboveground parking structure facade area. (Ord. 28917)

16.text:
SEC. S-16.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscape plan. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-16B).

(b) Surface parking screening. Surface parking must be screened in accordance with the off- street parking and screening requirements in Section 51P-193.126(b)(3)(A)(iii).

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 22954; 25267; 28917)

16.title: Signs
16.text:
SEC. S-16.112. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Attached premise signs.

(1) The following are the only attached premise signs permitted on and between the seventh and 13th floors and at or above the 20th floor in this subdistrict:

(A) On the north main structure facade, one logo sign may be located at or above the 20th floor, as shown on the logo sign elevations (Exhibit S-16C), and may not exceed 24 feet in height. The logo sign may be illuminated.

(B) On the south main structure facade, one logo sign may be located at or above the 20th floor, as shown on the logo sign elevations, and may not exceed 24 feet in height. The logo sign may be illuminated.

(C) On the west main structure facade, one logo sign may be located between the 9th floor and 13th floor, as shown on the logo sign elevations, and may not exceed 45 feet in height. The logo sign may only be illuminated with LED light embedded glazing.

(D) On each of the north, south, and west garage screen structure facades, one attached premise sign may be located between the seventh and ninth floors. These attached premise signs may be illuminated.

(E) The maximum effective area for all signs on the north and south garage facades is 205 square feet per facade.

(F) The maximum effective area for all signs on the west garage facade is 50 square feet.

(2) Except as provided in this section, attached premise signs are permitted on or below the third floor.

(c) Canopy sign. On the east main structure facade, one logo sign may be located on a canopy, as shown on the logo sign elevations.

(d) Illuminated signs.

(1) Illuminated signage is prohibited on the east structure facade.

(2) No illuminated sign may have a luminance greater than 200 foot lamberts.

(3) No illuminated sign or any illuminated element of any sign may turn on or off more than two times per day.

(4) On the north and south facades, the luminance of a sign may not directly project at an angle greater than 150 degrees measured from the location on the facade of the building at which the sign is placed.

(5) Before the issuance of a sign permit for attached premise signs, an exhibit showing the angle of luminance of a sign must be provided to the building official.

(e) Movement. No sign or any part of a sign may move or rotate. (Ord. Nos. 22954; 25267; 28917; 29684)

16.text:

(a) In general.

(1) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(2) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(3) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article.

(b) Visibility triangles. The visibility triangles must be provided as shown on the development plan.

(c) Traffic improvements. Before the issuance of a certificate of occupancy on this Property, the following must occur:

(1) Two-and-one half feet of right-of-way must be dedicated along the Property boundary on Wolf Street.

(2) 36 feet of street pavement, measured back-of-curb to back-of-curb, must be provided on Wolf Street from McKinnon Street to Harwood Street.

(3) Traffic signal upgrades for a left turn lane and pavement widening must be installed on Wolf Street. (Ord. Nos. 22954; 25267; 26102; 28917)

16.title: Compliance With Conditions
16.text:
SEC. S-16.114. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 22954; 25267; 26102; 28917)

18.title: Rezoning Of Pd Subdistrict 18

20.title: Legislative History
20.text:
SEC. S-20.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 20 was established by Ordinance No. 23082, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 9, 1997. Ordinance No. 23082 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 23082 was amended by Ordinance No. 23522, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 27, 1998. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 23082; 23522; 25267)

20.title: Property Location And Size
20.text:
SEC. S-20.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 20 is established on property generally located on the east corner of Oak Lawn Avenue and Gillespie Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 20 is approximately 0.57 acres. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Establishment Of Phases
20.text:
SEC. S-20.103. ESTABLISHMENT OF PHASES.

The Property is divided into two phases: Phase I and Phase II. The property descriptions for Phase I and Phase II are labelled Exhibit S-20A. The development/landscape plan (Exhibit S-20B) shows the boundaries of Phase I and Phase II. In the event of a conflict between Exhibit S-20A and the development/landscape plan, Exhibit S-20A controls. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 23522; 25267)

20.title: Definitions And Interpretations
20.text:
SEC. S-20.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this division refer to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) Phase I of this subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. Phase II of this subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Development/Landscape Plan
20.text:
SEC. S-20.105. DEVELOPMENT/LANDSCAPE PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development/landscape plan. Phase I of this subdistrict consists of the areas described as Part A and Part B on the development/landscape plan. Phase II of this subdistrict consists of the area described as Part C on the development/landscape plan. In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and the development/landscape plan, the provisions of this division control. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 23522; 25267)

20.title: Main Uses Permitted
20.text:
SEC. S-20.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Uses permitted in Phase I are as follows:

-- Antique shop. -- Bakery or confectionary shop. -- Bar, lounge, or tavern. [SUP] -- Book and stationary store. -- Camera shop. -- Cigar, tobacco, and candy store. -- Clothing store. -- Custom cleaning shop. [Pick-up and drop-off window is prohibited.] -- Drug store. -- Feed store. -- Florist store. -- Furniture store. -- Hardware or sporting goods store. -- Home improvement center. -- Hobby and art supplies store. -- Office. -- Paint and wallpaper store. -- Pet shop. -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. -- Retail food store. [Convenience store as defined in Dallas City Code Chapter 12B is not permitted.] -- Retail store other than listed. -- Second hand store. -- Swimming pool sales and supply. -- Tailor, custom sewing, and millinery. [Pick-up and drop-off window is prohibited.]

(b) The only uses permitted in Phase II are single-family, handicapped group dwelling unit, and multiple-family uses. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 23522; 25267; 28121; 28613)

20.title: Accessory Uses
20.text:
SEC. S-20.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this subdistrict:

-- Private stable. -- Open storage. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
20.text:
SEC. S-20.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Setbacks. Setbacks must be provided as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(b) Dwelling units. Maximum number of dwelling units permitted on the Property is 12.

(c) Floor area.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no maximum floor area.

(2) For Phase I, the footprint of the existing building shown on the development/landscape plan approved on February 9, 2011 may not be expanded eastward.

(d) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(e) Maximum structure height and stories.

(1) Maximum structure height and number of stories in Phase I is 36 feet and two stories.

(2) Maximum structure height and number of stories in Phase II is 48 feet and four stories, except for the following:

(A) Structures described in Section 51P-193.123(a)(2)(A) may project an additional 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(B) Structures with a gable, hip, gambrel, or dome roof may project an additional 12 feet above the maximum structure height. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267; 28121)

20.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
20.text:
SEC. S-20.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Off-street parking and loading for Phase I must comply with the following regulations.

(1) Except as provided in this paragraph, Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Existing off-street parking shown on the development/landscape plan approved on February 9, 2011 may be located within the visibility triangle.

(2) All required off-street parking must be provided on the Property.

(b) Off-street parking and loading on Phase II must comply with the following regulations.

(1) A minimum of 1.5 off-street parking spaces must be provided for each dwelling unit in Phase II.

(2) Except as provided in this paragraph, a parking space in an enclosed structure must be at least 20 feet from the right-of-way line adjacent to a street or alley if the space faces upon or can be entered directly from the street or alley. A parking space in an enclosed structure may be within 20 feet of the right-of-way line adjacent to a street or alley if:

(A) the garage door has a remote automatic control installed that is maintained in working condition; and

(B) no portion of the garage door encroaches into the public right-of-way when it opens or closes.

This paragraph does not authorize the erection of a garage within a required front, side, or rear yard setback. This paragraph applies to the Property in lieu of the regulations contained in Section 51P- 193.113(a)(9).

(3) Off-street loading in Phase II must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 23522; 25267; 28121)

20.title: Environmental Performance Standards
20.text:
SEC. S-20.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Access
20.text:
SEC. S-20.111. ACCESS.

Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the development/landscape plan. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Landscaping
20.text:
SEC. S-20.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Plant materials used for screening must maintain a solid appearance at all times. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition in accordance with Section 51P-193.126.

(b) Phase I.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping must be provided as shown on the development/landscape plan.

(2) Within 12 months of the construction of the parking lot located in Part B as shown on the development/landscape plan, screening must be provided adjacent to the southeast line of the parking lot in accordance with Section 51P-193.126(b)(3)(A). For purposes of this condition, construction of the building located on Part C, as shown on the development/landscape plan, constitutes screening for that portion of the parking lot adjacent to the building.

(c) Phase II.

(1) Landscaping for Phase II must comply with Section 51P-193.126.

(2) For purposes of compliance with Section 51P-193.126, Phase II is a TH subdistrict. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 23522; 25267; 28121)

20.title: Tree Preservation
20.text:
SEC. S-20.113. TREE PRESERVATION.

Tree mitigation must comply with Article X. Trees provided in Phase I may be counted towards the mitigation requirements of Phase II. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: Signs
20.text:
SEC. S-20.114. SIGNS.

Signs in Phase I must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII. Signs in Phase II must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267)

20.title: General Requirements
20.text:
SEC. S-20.115. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the development/landscape plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267; 26102)

20.title: Paving
20.text:
SEC. S-20.116. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267; 26102)

20.title: Compliance With Conditions
20.text:
SEC. S-20.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 23082; 25267; 26102)

21.text:

21.text:
SEC. S-21.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) This division is incorporated by reference in Chapter 51. In the event of a conflict, this division controls.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this division refer to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267)

21.text:
SEC. S-21.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

21.title: Main Uses Permitted
21.text:
SEC. S-21.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in Subsection (b) below, the uses permitted in this subdistrict are all uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict by specific use permit (SUP) only is permitted in this PD subdistrict by SUP. A use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this PD subdistrict, etc.

(b) The following uses are permitted as indicated below:

-- Office. -- Temporary construction or sales office. -- Laundry or cleaning pickup and receiving station. -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. [SUP] -- Child-care facility. [SUP] -- Private club. (Ord. Nos. 23423; 25267)

21.title: Accessory Uses
21.text:
SEC. S-21.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article.

(b) The following accessory uses are permitted in this district:

-- Accessory community center (private).

21.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
21.text:
SEC. S-21.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Minimum front yards.

(1) Minimum front yard setback is 10 feet.

(2) Balconies and ground supports, staircases, awnings, and other architectural features may project or extend into the front yard.

(3) Off-street parking may be located in the required front yard.

(b) Minimum side and rear yards. No minimum side or rear yard setback.

(c) Floor area. Maximum floor area for all uses combined is 560,000 square feet. Maximum floor area for nonresidential uses is 5,000 square feet.

(d) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units permitted on the Property is 300.

(e) Height and stories. Maximum structure height and stories is as follows:

(1) Building A. Maximum structure height and stories is 270 feet and 24 stories, as shown on the development plan.

(2) Buildings B and C. Maximum structure height and stories is 55 feet and four stories, as shown on the development plan.

(3) Parking structures. Maximum structure height is 55 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 84 percent. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations. For purposes of this subsection, the entire subdistrict is considered one lot. (Ord. Nos. 23423; 25267)

21.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
21.text:
SEC. S-21.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult the use regulations in PD 193 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations in PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. For purposes of this section, the entire subdistrict is considered one lot. (Ord. Nos. 23423; 25267)

21.title: Environmental Performance Standards
21.text:
SEC. S-21.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267)

21.title: Landscaping
21.text:
SEC. S-21.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping plan. Landscaping must be provided in accordance with the development plan and completed in accordance with the landscaping requirements contained in Part I of this article. Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Sidewalks. Sidewalks must be located as shown on the development plan. (Ord. Nos. 23423; 25267)

21.title: Signs
21.text:
SEC. S-21.111. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267)

21.title: General Requirements
21.text:
SEC. S-21.112. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the development plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article.

(d) The regulations contained in this division regarding building heights and setbacks control over any building height and setback regulations contained in Ordinance No. 14874 (“the Turtle Creek Environmental Corridor”). (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267; 26102)

21.title: Paving
21.text:
SEC. S-21.113. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267; 26102)

(Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267; 26102)

PD Subdistrict 21 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. Nos. 23141; 25267)

26.title: Main Uses Permitted
26.text:
SEC. S-26.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display).

(b) Auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside).

(c) Steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery.

(d) Engine or motor repair shop.

(e) Bus or truck repair/parking garage.

(f) Except as provided in this section, the uses permitted in this subdistrict are all uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. 26.text:

Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51P-193.108, “Accessory Uses.” For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 23422; 25267)

26.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
26.text:
SEC. S-26.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard.

(1) For an automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display) use, an auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside) use, a steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery use, an engine or motor repair shop use, and a bus or truck repair/parking garage use, minimum front yard is as shown on the development plan.

(2) For all other permitted uses, minimum front yard requirements for the GR General Retail Subdistrict contained in Section 51P-193.118 apply.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) For an automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display) use, an auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside) use, a steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery use, an engine or motor repair shop use, and a bus or truck repair/parking garage use, minimum side and rear yards are as shown on the development plan.

(2) For all other permitted uses, minimum side and rear yard requirements for the GR General Retail Subdistrict contained in Sections 51P-193.119 and 51P-193.120 apply.

(c) Minimum lot area per dwelling unit. Minimum lot area per dwelling unit requirements for the GR General Retail Subdistrict contained in Section 51P-193.125 apply in this subdistrict.

(d) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio for all permitted uses is 2.0:1.

(e) Height.

(1) For an automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display) use, an auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside) use, a steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery use, an engine or motor repair shop use, and a bus or truck repair/parking garage use, maximum structure height is 30 feet as shown on the development plan.

(2) For all other permitted uses, maximum height for residential structures is 36 feet, and maximum height for nonresidential structures is 120 feet.

(f) Lot coverage.

(1) For an automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display) use, an auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside) use, a steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery use, an engine or motor repair shop use, and a bus or truck repair/parking garage use, maximum lot coverage is 91 percent.

(2) For all other permitted uses, maximum lot coverage is as follows:

(A) Except as provided in Subparagraph (B), maximum lot coverage is 80 percent.

(B) For institutional uses, maximum lot coverage is 60 percent.

(3) Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations. (Ord. Nos. 23422; 25267)

(b) For all other permitted uses, consult the use regulations (Section 51P-193.107) for the specific off-street parking and loading requirement for each use. (Ord. Nos. 23422; 25267)

(2) Five foot side yard and 10 foot rear yard for duplex structures.

(2) 3,000 square feet per dwelling unit for duplex structures;

(3) 800 square feet per dwelling unit for multiple-family dwelling units with no separate bedroom;

(4) 1,000 square feet per dwelling unit for multiple-family dwelling units with one bedroom;

(5) 1,200 square feet per dwelling unit for multiple-family dwelling units with two bedrooms; and

(6) an additional 150 square feet per dwelling unit to the 1,200 square feet required in (5) above for each bedroom over two.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent for residential structures and 50 percent for nonresidential structures. (Ord. Nos. 23748; 25267)

Ordinance No. 24204 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 10962; 21859; 24204; 25267)

37.title: Property Location And Size
37.text:
SEC. S-37.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 37 is established on property generally fronting on the southwest line of Hall Street between the southeast line of Hood Street and the northwest line of Sale Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 37 is approximately 1.5586 acres. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267)

37.title: Definitions And Interpretations
37.text:
SEC. S-37.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division:

(1) ASSISTED LIVING FACILITY means a permanent residential facility which furnishes (in single or multiple facilities) food, shelter, laundry, and other assistance in activities of daily living to five or more persons who are not related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the owner or proprietor of the establishment. Food is prepared in a central kitchen. Individual dwelling units do not have kitchen facilities (i.e., do not have cook tops, ranges, or full size appliances, but may contain bar sinks, small refrigerators, or microwave ovens). Assisted living facilities must be licensed as Assisted Living Facilities under Chapter 247 of the Texas Health and Safety Code. Assisted living facilities do not include other licensed health facilities under Subtitle B, “Licensing of Health Facilities,” of Title 4, “Health Facilities,” of the Texas Health and Safety Code, specifically nursing homes.

(2) INDEPENDENT LIVING FACILITY means retirement housing as set forth in PD 193, except that individual dwelling units or suites may contain kitchen facilities.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Chapter 51.

(c) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944)

37.title: Development Plan
37.text:
SEC. S-37.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a multiple-family use, an assisted living facility, or an independent living facility, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-37A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and the development plan, the provisions of this division control.

(b) For all other permitted uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944; 26463; 27233)

37.title: Main Uses Permitted
37.text:
SEC. S-37.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the main uses permitted are those uses permitted in the O-2 Office Subdistrict of PD 193, subject to the same conditions applicable in that subdistrict. For example, a use permitted in that subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this PD subdistrict by SUP only; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in that subdistrict is subject to DIR in this PD subdistrict, etc.

(b) Independent living facility (permitted by right).

(c) Assisted living facility (permitted by right).

(d) The following main uses are prohibited:

-- Bar, lounge, or tavern. -- Commercial wedding chapel. -- Dance hall. -- Drive-in restaurant. -- Drive-through restaurant. -- Inside commercial amusement. -- Liquor store. -- Private club. -- Restaurant without drive-through service. -- Retail food store. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944)

37.title: Accessory Uses
37.text:
SEC. S-37.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51P-193.108, “Accessory Uses.” For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article.

(b) The following accessory uses are permitted only in conjunction with an assisted living facility or an independent living facility, and must comply with the rules for limited uses:

-- Bar, lounge, or tavern. -- Barber and beauty shop. -- Community center (private). -- Drug store. -- Game court (private). -- Handcrafted art work studio. -- Health studio. -- Instructional art studio. -- Office. -- Private club.

-- Private recreation club or area. -- Retail food store. -- Retail stores other than listed. -- Swimming pool (private).

(c) Common dining facilities are permitted by right as an accessory use to an independent living facility or assisted living facility. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944)

37.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
37.text:
SEC. S-37.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in PD 193. In the event of a conflict between this section and PD 193, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard.

(1) For a multiple-family use, an assisted living facility, or an independent living facility, minimum front yard setback is as shown on the development plan. Structures and fences in the front yard are permitted in the locations shown on the development plan.

(2) For all other permitted uses, minimum front yard is the same as in the O-2 Office Subdistrict in PD 193.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) For a multiple-family use, an assisted living facility, or an independent living facility, minimum side and rear yard setbacks are as shown on the development plan. Structures and fences in the side and rear yard are permitted in the locations shown on the development plan.

(2) For all other permitted uses, minimum side and rear yard setbacks are the same as in the O-2 Office Subdistrict in PD 193.

(c) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units or suites is 210.

(d) Floor area. Maximum floor area ratio is the same as in the O-2 Office Subdistrict in PD 193.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 120 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944; 27233)

37.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
37.text:
SEC. S-37.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, off-street parking and loading must be provided in accordance with the requirements of PD 193, as amended.

(b) For an assisted living facility, off-street parking must be provided at the ratio of 0.30 spaces per dwelling unit or suite.

(c) For an independent living facility, off-street parking must be provided at the ratio of 1.2 spaces per dwelling unit or suite.

(d) For an assisted living facility and an independent living facility, a minimum of 133 off- street parking spaces must be provided on the property. (Ord. Nos. 24204; 25267; 25944; 27233)

37.title: Environmental Performance Standards
37.text:
SEC. S-37.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

37.text:
SEC. S-37.110. LANDSCAPING.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(2) For multiple-family uses, minimum rear yard is eight feet as shown on the development/ landscape plan.

(3) For all other uses, minimum side and rear yard is the same as in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict in PD 193.

45.title: Landscaping
45.text:
SEC. S-45.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For a public school use:

(1) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-45B).

(2) Within three months after issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any development within the area identified as "Buildable Area," a minimum of three trees, each a minimum of three-and-one-half caliper inches and a minimum of 14 feet in height, must be provided on the Property.

(b) For all other uses, landscaping must be provided in accordance with the landscape requirements contained in Part I of this article.

(c) Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 24353; 25267; 31151)

SEC. S-45.110.1. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a public school must comply with the traffic management plan (Exhibit S-45C).

(b) Queuing. Queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within the city rights-of-way.

(c) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director by November 1, 2020. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit updates of the traffic study to the director by March 1 of each even-numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick-up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(d) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using the minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3).

(2) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation; eliminate traffic hazards; or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. 31151)

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(d) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 24809; 25267; 26102; 28859)

SEC. S-50.112.1. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS FOR TRACT I.

(a) Applicability. This section only applies to a development in Tract I that contains multiple-family uses and exceeds 106,000 square feet of floor area.

(b) Residential tower setback. Any portion of a structure containing multiple-family dwelling units must be a minimum of 55 feet from the eastern boundary of Tract I. This subsection does not apply to portions of a structure that house aboveground parking.

(c) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum height for all structures is 200 feet measured from ground surface elevation at the northeastern corner of the property. Mechanical equipment, elevator overrides, parapet walls and related equipment and structures may extend an additional 15 feet in height above 200 feet.

(2) Maximum height of any parking structure or portion of a building containing parking is 66 feet measured from existing ground surface elevation at the northeastern corner of the property. Required safety rails and related structures may be located above 66 feet in height.

(d) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 180.

(e) Structured parking.

(1) Maximum number of parking spaces inside a structure is 540 spaces.

(2) Any portion of the eastern facade of a structure that contains parking that is located above a portion of a building that contains parking on Tract II must be fully enclosed with no openings.

(f) Screening of open space. Open space that is located on the rooftop above a parking structure must be screened from Tract II with evergreen plant materials that are a minimum of six feet in height upon maturity.

(g) Street level activating uses. A minimum of 6,000 square feet of floor area on the ground level of any building must contain some combination of the following uses:

(1) Bar and restaurant uses.

(2) Retail uses.

(3) Professional, personal service and custom craft uses, except office use.

(h) Balconies. A minimum of 80 percent of the multiple-family dwelling units must have balconies.

(i) Facade materials. A minimum of 60 percent of the exterior facade of any building must have some combination of the following materials:

(1) Glass.

(2) Metal.

(3) Masonry.

(4) Stone.

(5) Concrete.

(j) Ground level transparency. Street facing facades on the ground level of any building must have a minimum transparency of 50 percent. A minimum of 60 percent of the required minimum transparency area must allow views into the ground-story use to a minimum depth of four feet. Windows must be clear or unpainted, or, if treated, must be transparent or translucent. Spandrel glass and backpainted glass are not considered transparent for purposes of this requirement. This provision does not apply to parking structures.

(k) Minimum private open space. A minimum of 7,500 square feet of private open space must be located on Tract I. The private open space may be located on top of a parking structure.

(l) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical and related equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as not to be visible from any public right-of-way. (Ord. 28859).

52.title: Legislative History
52.text:
SEC. S-52.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

(a) PD Subdistrict 52 was established by Ordinance No. 25591, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 12, 2004. Ordinance No. 25591 amended Ordinance No. 21859, PD 193 (the Oak Lawn Special Purpose District), as amended, and Ordinance No. 10962, Chapter 51 of the Dallas City Code, as amended.

(b) This subdistrict was established in conjunction with PD Subdistrict 53, PD Subdistrict 54, deed restrictions adopted in Zoning Case No. Z034-181, and the property owner’s plan for development of the four tracts. The intent was to mitigate development impacts on the surrounding area by increasing the floor area of certain tracts and decreasing the floor area of certain tracts, while maintaining the combined total allowed floor area of the four tracts. Other goals included the preservation of a designated historic structure (St. Ann’s School) and requiring certified designation under the United States Green Building Council's Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design checklist. (Ord. 25591)

52.title: Property Location And Size
52.text:
SEC. S-52.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 52 is established on property generally bounded by North Pearl Street, Randall Street, McKinnon Street, and Wolf Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 52 is approximately 1.315 acres. (Ord. 25591)

52.title: Purpose
52.text:
SEC. S-52.103. PURPOSE.

The standards of this division complement the development pattern in the area and recognize the area’s unique identity as a gateway to downtown and a bridge between downtown and Oak Lawn. The objectives of these standards are as follows:

(1) To promote the health, safety, welfare, convenience, and enjoyment of the public.

(2) To achieve buildings more in urban form.

(3) To promote a pedestrian environment and provide public open space.

(4) To preserve landmark historic buildings and the city's cultural heritage.

(5) To encourage development that complements nearby properties.

(6) To achieve buildings efficient in design and utilization of space while providing adequate view corridors, light, and air to nearby properties.

(7) To achieve buildings that reduce natural resource consumption, enhance occupant comfort and health, lower utility consumption, minimize strain on local infrastructures, and improve quality of life. (Ord. 25591)

52.title: Definitions And Interpretations
52.text:
SEC. S-52.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division:

(1) MAYOR’S WAY HOMEOWNER ASSOCIATION means the homeowner’s association for the Mayor’s Way neighborhood generally bounded by Wolf Street, Bookhout Street, Randall Street, and North Pearl Street.

(2) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 25591)

52.text:

(b) Any amendment, minor or major, to the development plan must be submitted to the Mayor’s Way Homeowner Association at the same time it is submitted to the city plan commission. (Ord. 25591)

For example, a use permitted only by specific use permit (SUP) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is permitted only by SUP in this subdistrict; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict, etc. (Ord. 25591)

52.text:
SEC. S-52.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult PD 193.
