52.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
52.text:
SEC. S-52.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) Front, side, and rear yard. Minimum front, side, and rear yard is 10 feet.

(b) Dwelling unit density. Maximum dwelling unit density is 250 units per acre.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) For residential uses, maximum floor area ratio is 5.5.

(2) For all other uses, maximum floor area ratio is 5.0.

(d) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this section, maximum structure height is 350 feet.

(2) Maximum structure height for a parking structure is 36 feet.

(3) Structures located on a roof, such as chimneys, clerestories, communication towers, cooling towers, elevator penthouses or bulkheads, mechanical equipment rooms, plaza or terrace structures, pool structures, skylights, vent stacks, and visual screens that surround mechanical equipment are allowed to project up to 25 feet above the maximum structure height.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 85 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size. (Ord. 25591)

52.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
52.text:
SEC. S-52.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking/loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. (Ord. 25591)

SEC S-52.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI, “Environmental Performance Standards.”

(b) LEED certification.

(1) A United States Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) checklist, effective May 1, 2004, must be submitted with an application for a building permit for development on the Property, indicating how development of the Property will comply with a certified designation (26 to 32 project points). The development plans submitted for a building permit must be certified by a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of

development services. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, the building official shall determine that the project is consistent with the standards and criteria for a LEED certified designation.

(2) If during development of the Property, the developer is unable to achieve all of the green building rating system points identified on the checklist, the developer must replace any points not achieved with other green building rating system points acceptable under the United States Green Building Council’s LEED rating system.

(3) All supporting documentation and templates related to the points previously approved by the city for the LEED certified level designation must be submitted with an application for a certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy may not be issued until a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services certifies that the building complies with the LEED certified designation (26 to 32 project points). (Ord. 25591)

52.title: Landscaping
52.text:
SEC. S-52.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscape plan. A landscape plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of a building permit. The landscape plan must be submitted to the Mayor’s Way Homeowner Association at the same time it is submitted to the city plan commission. The landscape plan must comply with the landscape requirements of Part I of this article, with the following exceptions:

(1) Required street trees may be located within the sidewalk area abutting the curb.

(2) Any trees that would be required to be located in the Entry Plaza or deceleration lane from McKinnon Street may be provided at the Plaza.

(3) Replacement trees may be planted anywhere on the Property and within the public right-of-way.

(4) Credit for trees planted in an open space shall serve as a credit to offset the tree replacement requirements on the Property. “Open space” as used in this provision means a plaza, terrace, or outdoor area, whether public or private, located anywhere on the Property, including the roof of a structure.

(5) A minimum of 30 percent of the exposed parking garage roof must be planted with plant materials approved for use under Article X, “Landscape and Tree Preservation Regulations.”

(6) A minimum of 30 percent of all impervious areas must be shaded. If trees are used, they must be capable of achieving compliance with this section within three years of planting.

(7) A minimum of 30 percent of the area of commercial projects must be public open space. A minimum of 20 percent of the area of residential projects must be public open space. A minimum of 10 percent of the area of residential projects must be private open space. “Open space” as used in this provision means a plaza, terrace, or outdoor area located anywhere on the Property, including the roof of a structure.

(b) Landscape plan amendments. Any amendment, minor or major, to the landscape plan must be submitted to the Mayor’s Way Homeowner Association at the same time it is submitted to the city plan commission.

(c) Parking structure screening, lighting, and noise.

(1) An earthen berm planted with turf grass, ground cover, or other landscaping must be provided between the exterior wall of a parking structure and the sidewalk on North Pearl Street.

(2) Louvers must be provided in the openings on the facade of a parking structure adjacent to Pearl Street.

(3) Interior lighting in a parking structure may not have a visible source of illumination that produces glare or illumination across a property line of an intensity that creates a nuisance or detracts from the use or enjoyment of adjacent property.

(4) Interior lighting at the perimeter of each level of a parking structure must be designed to provide no more than 1.5 footcandles of illumination.

(5) Mechanical sweepers may not be operated in a parking structure between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

(d) Private license granted.

(1) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners and tenants (“owners”) of property in this subdistrict for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with this section. An owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by ordinance passed by the city council, at any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city of the necessity for such termination shall be final and binding, and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right- of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by city council, each owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public right-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(2) An owner is not required to comply with any landscaping or lighting requirement if compliance is made impossible due to revocation of a landscape permit or revocation of the license granted under this section.

(3) Upon the installation of landscaping or lighting in the public rights-of-way, the owner shall procure, pay for, and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the private license granted under this section, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence and $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an “occurrence” basis and the city shall be named as an additional insured. Proof of such insurance must be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla 1/C/N, Dallas, Texas, 75201, and the policy must provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent the same are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(4) Each owner shall be responsible for maintaining the landscaping in a healthy, growing condition, maintaining the lighting in good condition, and keeping the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from

any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping or lighting. The granting of a license for landscaping and lighting under this section does not release the owner or tenant from liability in the installation or maintenance of landscaping or lighting in the public rights-of-way.

(e) Maintenance. Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25591)

(3) To promote a pedestrian environment and provide public open space.

(4) To preserve landmark historic buildings and the city's cultural heritage.

(5) To encourage development that complements nearby properties.

(6) To achieve buildings efficient in design and utilization of space while providing adequate view corridors, light, and air to nearby properties.

(7) To achieve buildings that reduce natural resource consumption, enhance occupant comfort and health, lower utility consumption, minimize strain on local infrastructures, and improve quality of life. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Definitions And Interpretations
53.text:
SEC. S-53.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Conceptual Plan
53.text:
SEC. S-53.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-53A). In the event of a conflict between this division and the conceptual plan, this division controls. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Development Plan
53.text:
SEC. S-53.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit. Development and use of the Property must comply with the approved development plan. Each development plan and any amendments must comply with the conceptual plan and this division.

(b) The portion of Section 51-4.702(c) requiring submission of a development plan within six months of the city council's approval of this subdistrict does not apply in this subdistrict.

(c) The development plan must comply with the requirements of Section 51-4.702. Signs are not required to be shown on a development plan.

(d) In the event of a conflict between this division and the development plan, this division controls. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Main Uses Permitted
53.text:
SEC. S-53.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only uses permitted in this subdistrict are those uses permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted only by specific use permit (SUP) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is permitted only by SUP in this subdistrict; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict, etc. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Accessory Uses
53.text:
SEC. S-53.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult PD 193.

(b) A pedestrian skybridge is permitted as an accessory use if it meets all of the requirements of Subsection (12), “Pedestrian Skybridges,” of Section 51A-4.217, “Accessory Uses,” of Chapter 51A. A pedestrian skybridge may be located within 300 feet of an historic overlay district. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
53.text:
SEC. S-53.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) Front, side, and rear yard. No minimum front, side, or rear yard.

(b) Dwelling unit density. Maximum dwelling unit density is 250 units per acre.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) For residential uses, maximum floor area ratio is 5.5.

(2) For all other uses, maximum floor area ratio is 5.0.

(d) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this section, maximum structure height is 325 feet.

(2) Maximum structure height in Phase II is 50 feet.

(3) Structures located on a roof, such as chimneys, clerestories, communication towers, cooling towers, elevator penthouses or bulkheads, mechanical equipment rooms, plaza or terrace structures, pool structures, skylights, vent stacks, and visual screens that surround mechanical equipment are allowed to project up to 25 feet above the maximum structure height.

(4) Maximum structure height for that portion of any structure used primarily for parking is 145 feet, measured from the flow line of the curb on the west side of Harwood Street at the entrance to the parking structure.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) For residential structures in Phase I, maximum lot coverage is 80 percent.

(2) For nonresidential structures in Phase I, maximum lot coverage is 100 percent.

(3) In Phase II, maximum lot coverage is 30 percent.

(4) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
53.text:
SEC. S-53.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking/loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Environmental Performance Standards
53.text:
SEC. S-53.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI, “Environmental Performance Standards.”

(b) LEED certification.

(1) A United States Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) checklist, effective May 1, 2004, must be submitted with an application for a building permit for development on the Property, indicating how development of the Property will comply with a certified designation (26 to 32 project points). The development plans submitted for a building permit must be certified by a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, the building official shall determine that the project is consistent with the standards and criteria for a LEED certified designation.

(2) If during development of the Property, the developer is unable to achieve all of the green building rating system points identified on the checklist, the developer must replace any points not achieved with other green building rating system points acceptable under the United States Green Building Council’s LEED rating system.

(3) All supporting documentation and templates related to the points previously approved by the city for the LEED certified level designation must be submitted with an application for a certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy may not be issued until a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services certifies that the building complies with the LEED certified designation (26 to 32 project points). (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Landscaping
53.text:
SEC. S-53.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscape plan. A landscape plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of a building permit. The landscape plan must comply with the landscape requirements of Part I of this article, with the following exceptions:

(1) Required street trees may be located within the sidewalk area abutting the curb.

(2) Replacement trees may be planted anywhere on the Property and within the public right-of-way.

(3) Credit for trees planted in an open space shall serve as a credit to offset the tree replacement requirements on the Property. “Open space” as used in this provision means a plaza, terrace, or outdoor area, whether public or private, located anywhere on the Property, including the roof of a structure.

(4) A minimum of 30 percent of the exposed parking garage roof must be planted with plant materials approved for use under Article X, “Landscape and Tree Preservation Regulations.”

(5) A minimum of 30 percent of all impervious areas must be shaded. If trees are used, they must be capable of achieving compliance with this section within three years of planting.

(6) A minimum of 30 percent of the area of commercial projects must be public open space. A minimum of 20 percent of the area of residential projects must be public open space. A minimum of 10 percent of the area of residential projects must be private open space. “Open space” as used in this provision means a plaza, terrace, or outdoor area located anywhere on the Property, including the roof of a structure.

(7) Landscaping for the St. Ann’s School Historic Overlay District is controlled by the historic overlay district ordinance and Part I of this article, except that the area along Moody Street between Harwood Street and Harry Hines Boulevard is exempt from landscape requirements due to site constraints caused by the historic structure.

(b) Parking structure screening, lighting, and noise.

(1) Trees must be planted parallel to the exterior wall of the parking structure within the Wichita Street sidewalk. There must be one tree for every 25 feet of frontage. The trees must be either Live Oak or Magnolia with a minimum caliper of four inches.

(2) The Wichita Street facade of the parking structure must comply with the following requirements:

(A) A minimum of 20 percent of the facade must be materials similar to the façade of the main structure.

(B) A minimum of 1,500 square feet of the openings must be an open, recessed planting area, and the remainder of the openings must be louvers made of opaque materials. The open, recessed planting area must span seven floors. The open, recessed planting area must have a minimum of eight trees or have a living screen. Trees used must be evergreen trees permitted in PD 193 with a minimum caliper of three inches. Living screen used must be capable of achieving 12 feet in height and six feet in width within three years of planting. The open, recessed planting area may be placed within required parking spaces.

(C) Compliance with this subsection shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of Subsection (a), “Off-Street Parking Structures,” of Section 51P-193.127, “Structure Facade Standards.”

(3) Interior lighting in a parking structure may not have a visible source of illumination that produces glare or direct illumination across a property line of an intensity that creates a nuisance or detracts from the use or enjoyment of adjacent property.

(4) Interior lighting at the perimeter of each level of a parking structure must be designed to provide no more than 1.5 footcandles of illumination after 10 p.m.

(5) Mechanical sweepers may not be operated in a parking structure between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

(6) Exposed ductwork and mechanical equipment may not be located on the exterior garage wall parallel to Wichita Street.

(7) Subsection (8) of Section 30-2, “Loud and Disturbing Noises Presumed Offensive,” of the Dallas City Code, limiting the hours of construction adjacent to residential areas, applies.

(c) Private license granted.

(1) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners and tenants (“owners”) of property in this subdistrict for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with this section. An owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by ordinance passed by the city council, at any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city of the necessity for such termination shall be final and binding, and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right- of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by city council, each owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public right-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(2) An owner is not required to comply with any landscaping or lighting requirement if compliance is made impossible due to revocation of a landscape permit or revocation of the license granted under this section.

(3) Upon the installation of landscaping or lighting in the public rights-of-way, the owner shall procure, pay for, and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the private license granted under this section, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence and $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an “occurrence” basis and the city shall be named as an additional insured. Proof of such insurance must be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla 1/C/N, Dallas, Texas, 75201, and the policy must provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent the same are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(4) Each owner shall be responsible for maintaining the landscaping in a healthy, growing condition, maintaining the lighting in good condition, and keeping the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping or lighting. The granting of a license for landscaping and lighting under this section does not release the owner or tenant from liability in the installation or maintenance of landscaping or lighting in the public rights-of-way.

(d) Maintenance. Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Visibility Triangle Regulations
53.text:
SEC. S-53.113. VISIBILITY TRIANGLE REGULATIONS.

Those provisions of Subsection (d), “Visual Obstruction Regulations,” of Section 51-4.602 “Fence, Screening, and Visual Obstruction Regulations,” for central area districts apply in this subdistrict. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Signs
53.text:
SEC. S-53.114. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signs may contain the logo of a company that owns or controls a business entity that owns real property within this subdistrict. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Additional Provisions
53.text:
SEC. S-53.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Frontage on a street. A lot in this subdistrict is not required to front upon either a dedicated public street or a private street if adequate access is provided by an access easement. A lot is deemed to have adequate access if the access easement is a minimum of 15 feet wide for a one-way access easement and a minimum of 24 feet wide for a two-way access easement. The design and construction of the access easement must be approved by the director of public works and transportation in accordance with standard city rules and specifications.

(b) Trash compactors. Trash compactors must be used. Trash compactors must be located within a structure with access to Harwood Street. Trash dumpsters are not allowed.

(c) Location of HVAC units, loading docks, and garage access. HVAC units, loading docks, and entrances/exits to a parking structure may not be placed along Wichita Street or along Harwood Street within 25 feet of the Wichita Street and Harwood Street intersection.

(d) General maintenance. The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(e) Compliance with all other laws. Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(f) Compliance with Part I. Except as otherwise provided in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Paving
53.text:
SEC. S-53.116. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 25592)

53.title: Compliance With Conditions
53.text:
SEC. S-53.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 25592)

56.text:

PD Subdistrict 56 is established on property located southeast of Knight Street and southwest of Cedar Springs Road. The size of PD Subdistrict 56 is approximately 1.3 acres. (Ord. 25643)

56.text:

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Article 193 apply to this subdistrict.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Article 193. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Development Plan
56.text:
SEC. S-56.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(b) For all other uses, development and use of the Property must comply with a city plan commission-approved development plan that complies with the regulations governing Article 193 unless otherwise set forth herein. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Main Uses Permitted
56.text:
SEC. S-56.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Tract 1. Except as provided in Section S-56.105(c), the main uses permitted in Tract 1 (as shown in the development plan) are those uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict within Article 193, subject to the same conditions applicable in those subdistricts, as set out in Article 193, as amended. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit
(SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict.

(b) Tract 2. Except as provided in Section S-56.105(c), the main uses permitted in Tract 2 (as shown in the development plan) are those uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict within Article 193, subject to the same conditions applicable in those districts, as set out in Article 193, as amended. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict. A bank or savings and loan office use without drive-through window service is allowed by right in Tract 2.

(c) The following main uses are not permitted in this subdistrict:

(1) Residential uses.

-- Lodging or boarding house. -- Hotel and motel. -- Group residential facility. -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. -- Retirement housing. -- Overnight general purpose shelter.

(2) Utility and service uses.

-- Electrical substation. -- Radio, television, or microwave tower. -- Commercial radio or television transmitting station. -- Sewage pumping station. -- Sewage treatment plant. -- Telephone exchange, switching, and transmitting equipment. -- Water reservoir, well, or pumping station. -- Water treatment plant.

(3) Transportation uses.

-- Airport or landing field. -- Passenger bus station and terminal. -- Bus passenger shelter.

(4) Community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. -- Community service center. -- Foster home. -- Child-care facility. -- Halfway house.

(5) Medical uses.

-- Hospital. -- Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions. -- Ambulance service.

(6) Religious uses.

-- Convent or monastery. -- Cemetery or mausoleum.

(7) Educational uses.

-- Public or private school. -- College, university, or seminary. -- College fraternity or sorority house. -- College dormitory.

(8) Recreation and entertainment uses.

-- Game court center. -- Private recreation club or area. -- Public golf course. -- Country club with private membership. -- Inside commercial amusement. -- Outside commercial amusement. -- Theatre. -- Wax museum.

(9) Bar and restaurant uses.

-- Bar, lounge, or tavern. -- Private club. -- Dance hall.

(10) Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses.

-- Mortuary or funeral home. -- Custom cleaning shop. -- Self service laundry or dry cleaning. -- Commercial wedding chapel.

(11) Retail uses.

-- Liquor store. -- Feed store. -- Second hand store. -- Pawn shop. -- Home improvement center. -- Swimming pool sales and supply.

(12) Motor vehicle-related uses.

-- Auto glass, muffler, or seat cover shop. -- Auto parts sales (inside only). -- Auto repair garage (inside). -- Commercial parking lot or garage.

(13) Commercial uses.

-- Appliance fix-it shop. -- Building repair and maintenance shop. -- Plumbing, electrical, air conditioning, and heating shop. -- Tool and equipment rental (inside display only). -- Stone, sand, or gravel mining. -- Custom print shop. -- Garden shop, plant sales, or greenhouse. -- Diamond and precious stone sales (wholesale only).

(14) Storage and waste disposal.

-- Recycling buy-back center. -- Recycling collection center. -- Recycling drop-off container. -- Recycling drop-off for special occasion collection.

(15) Animal-related uses.

-- Farm or ranch. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Accessory Uses
56.text:
SEC. S-56.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Article 193.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this subdistrict:

56.text:

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Article 193. In the event of a conflict between this section and Article 193, this section controls.)

(B) For all other uses, consult the applicable zoning regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within Article 193.

(2) Tract 2.

(2) Tract 2.

(A) For a bank use, minimum side and rear yards are as shown on the development plan.

(B) For all other uses, consult the applicable zoning regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict within Article 193.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) Tract 1. Consult the applicable zoning regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within Article 193.

(2) Tract 2. Consult the applicable zoning regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict within Article 193.

(d) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Tract 1.

(A) For a bank use, maximum lot coverage is 25 percent.

(B) For all other uses, consult the applicable zoning regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within Article 193.

(2) Tract 2.

(B) For all other uses, consult the applicable zoning regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict within Article 193. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
56.text:
SEC. S-56.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(b) For all other uses, all landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with PD 193.
(c) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Signs
56.text:
SEC. S-56.110. SIGNS.

For all uses, signs must comply with the provisions for signs contained in Article VII of Chapter 51A. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Lighting
56.text:
SEC. S-56.111. LIGHTING.

Exterior lighting fixtures on the Property must comply with Section 51P-193.113(e)(2), “Lighting Provisions for Off-street Parking.” (Ord. 25643)

56.text:
SEC. S-56.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the City of Dallas. (Ord. 25643)

56.title: Zoning Map
56.text:

PD Subdistrit 56 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. 25643)

57.title: Legislative History

57.title: Property Location And Size
57.text:

57.title: Development Plan

57.title: Main Uses Permitted
57.text:
SEC. S-57.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

57.title: Accessory Uses

57.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
57.text:
SEC. S-57.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: the yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations of the TH-3 Townhouse Subdistrict apply in this subdistrict.

(b) Front yard. For a public school use, minimum front yard is as shown on the development plan.

(c) Side and rear yard. For a public school use, minimum side and rear yard is as shown on the development plan.

(d) Lot coverage. For a public school use, maximum lot coverage is 22 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(e) Height. For a pubic school use, maximum structure height is 33 feet. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Off Street Parking And Loading
57.text:
SEC. S-57.108. OFF STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For a public school use, off-street parking is allowed in the required yards.

(c) For a public school use with up to 45 classrooms, a minimum of 68 parking spaces must be provided. Additional parking in the amount required by Part I of this article must be provided for any classrooms beyond the initial 45 classrooms.

(d) For a pubic school use, a hedge of evergreen plant materials (e.g. holly) capable of reaching three feet in height within three years must be provided to screen parking areas adjacent to residential uses. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Landscaping
57.text:
SEC. S-57.109. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided as required in Part I of this article.

(b) For a public school use, landscaping must be provided as shown on the attached development plan.

(c) For a public school use, street trees must be planted along the portion of the street within a 300 foot radius of any structure within the expansion area shown on the development plan. These street trees must be planted within 30 months after October 13, 2004 for an existing structure and within six months after issuance of a building permit for any new structure. The trees listed in Subsection (2), “Species,” of Section 51A-10.134, “Replacement of Removed or Seriously Injured Trees,” must be used. These trees must be a minimum of three caliper inches. Any trees required this provision must be planted so that the spacing of trees along the street does not exceed 30 feet on center. Additional street trees do not need to be planted where street trees have already been provided pursuant to this provision.

(d) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Signs
57.text:
SEC. S-57.110. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non- business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For a public school use, signage must be provided as shown on the development plan. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Fences
57.text:
SEC. S-57.111. FENCES.

For a public school use, fences with a maximum height of six feet may be located in required yards. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Additional Provisions
57.text:
SEC. S-57.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the development plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Compliance With Conditions
57.text:
SEC. S-57.113. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 25771)

57.title: Zoning Map
57.text:
SEC. S-57.114. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict S-57 is located on Zoning Map No. H-6. (Ord. 25771)

58.title: Legislative History
58.text:
SEC. S-58.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 58 was established by Ordinance No. 25768, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 13, 2004. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Property Location And Size
58.text:
SEC. S-58.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 58 is established on property located west of Cedar Springs Road, southeast of Carlisle Street and northeast of Routh Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 58 is approximately 0.4397 acres. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Definitions And Interpretations
58.text:
SEC. S-58.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in PD 193 apply to this subdistrict.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this subdistrict are to articles, divisions, or sections in PD 193. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Development Plan
58.text:
SEC. S-58.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a financial institution with drive-in window, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-58A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this subdistrict and the development plan, the text of this subdistrict controls.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, development and use of the Property must comply with the GR General Retail Subdistrict regulations within PD 193 for all other uses. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Main Uses Permitted
58.text:
SEC. S-58.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) The following main uses are permitted in this subdistrict:

(1) Financial institution with drive-in window.

(2) Except as provided below, those uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193, subject to the same conditions applicable in that subdistrict, as set out in PD 193, as amended. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict.

(b) The following uses are not permitted in this district:

-- Airport or landing field. -- Amateur communications tower. -- Bar, lounge, or tavern. -- Car wash.

-- Commercial amusement (inside). -- Commercial parking lot or garage. -- Commercial radio or television transmitting station. -- Dance hall. -- Liquor store. -- Pawn shop. -- Passenger bus station and terminal. -- Private club. -- Service station. -- Sewage pumping station. -- Sewage treatment plant. -- Water reservoir, well, or pumping station. -- Water treatment plant. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Accessory Uses
58.text:
SEC. S-58.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained Section 51P-193.108, “Accessory Uses.” For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
58.text:
SEC. S-58.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot and space regulations in PD 193. In the event of a conflict between this section and PD 193, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard.

(1) For a financial institution with drive-in window, no minimum front yard is required.

(2) For all other uses, consult the use regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193.

(b) Side and rear yard.

(1) For a financial institution with drive-in window, no minimum side and rear yards are required.

(2) For all other uses, consult the use regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) For a financial institution with drive-in window, maximum floor area ratio is 0.25:1.

(2) For all other uses, consult the use regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193.

(d) Height. For all uses, consult the use regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193.

(e) Lot coverage. For all uses, consult the use regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict within PD 193. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
58.text:
SEC. S-58.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult the use regulations in PD 193 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Landscaping
58.text:
SEC. S-58.109. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For a financial institution with drive-in window, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-58B).

(b) For all other uses, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with the landscape requirements of PD 193.

(c) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Signs
58.text:
SEC. S-58.110. SIGNS.

For all uses, signs must comply with the provisions for signs contained in Article VII of Chapter 51A, as amended. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Lighting
58.text:
SEC. S-58.111. LIGHTING.

All exterior lighting fixtures on the property must comply with Section 51P-193-113(e)(2), “Lighting Provisions for Off-street Parking.” (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Additional Provisions
58.text:
SEC. S-58.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 25768)

58.title: Zoning Map
58.text:
SEC. S-58.113. ZONING MAP.

PD193 Subdistrict 58 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. 25768)

59.title: Legislative History
59.text:
SEC. S-59.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 59 was established by Ordinance No. 25824, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 8, 2004. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Property Location And Size
59.text:
SEC. S-59.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 59 is established on property located along Throckmorton Avenue, between Hawthorne Avenue and Avondale Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 59 is approximately 7.22 acres. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Definitions And Interpretations
59.text:
SEC. S-59.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) Except as provided in this section, this subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district.

(d) For the purpose of yard, lot, and space regulations in other zoning districts, all property in this subdistrict (save and except the western 65 feet of Lot 22 in City Block 8/2026) is considered to be a TH Townhouse Subdistrict.

(e) For the purpose of yard, lot, and space regulations in other zoning districts, the western 65 feet of Lot 22 in City Block 8/2026 in this subdistrict is considered to be an O-2 Office Subdistrict. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Development Plan
59.text:
SEC. S-59.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Development and use of the Property must comply with a city plan commission approved development plan that complies with this division. In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this division and a development plan, the provisions of this division control.

(b) All existing legal uses and legal structures on the Property as of December 8, 2004 shall remain legal nonconforming uses or structures and are not subject to the provisions of the Dallas City Code allowing for termination. Those uses or structures are not required to comply with this division, but they must comply with the development standards that existed on the Property immediately prior to December 8, 2004. Except as provided in Subsection (c), in the case of loss or destruction of any structure that existed on the Property as of December 8, 2004, that structure may be repaired or rebuilt.

(c) Notwithstanding Subsection (b), upon the filing of the first demolition permit for removal of any structure that existed on a lot or tract in this subdistrict as of December 8, 2004, all structures on that lot or tract must comply with this division. In addition, if a structure that existed on a lot or tract in this subdistrict as of December 8, 2004 is destroyed by the intentional act of the owner of the lot or tract or the owner’s agent, all development on that lot or tract must comply with this division.

(d) Development and use of Tract A must comply with the development plan for Tract A (Exhibit S-59B). In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. Nos. 25824; 26075)

59.title: Main Uses Permitted
59.text:
SEC. S-59.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those uses permitted in the TH-4 Townhouse Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-4 Townhouse Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the TH-4 Townhouse Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the TH-4 Townhouse Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Accessory Uses
59.text:
SEC. S-59.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult PD 193. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
59.text:
SEC. S-59.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as otherwise provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the TH-4 Townhouse Subdistrict apply in this subdistrict.

(b) Setback from streets.

(1) Except for garages and as provided in Paragraph (2) below, minimum setback from Throckmorton Avenue is 10 feet. Minimum setback from all other street frontages is 20 feet.

(2) For Tract A as shown on the map of Subdistrict 59 (Exhibit S-59A) and on the development plan for Tract A, the setback from all street frontages is 10 feet.

(c) Side yard. Except for garages or where a side yard fronts on a street, no minimum side yard setback.

(d) Rear yard. Minimum rear yard is five feet.

(e) Density. No more than 20 dwelling units per acre are allowed.

(f) Garages.

(1) Except as provided in Paragraph (2) below, garages must have a minimum setback of 20 feet.

(2) For Tract A, as shown on the map of Subdistrict 59 and on the development plan for Tract A, a garage may be set back five feet from the alley if:

(A) the garage door has a remote automatic control installed that is maintained in working condition; and

(B) no portion of the garage door encroaches into the public right-of-way when it opens or closes. (Ord. Nos. 25824; 26075)

59.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
59.text:
SEC. S-59.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking/loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Landscaping
59.text:
SEC. S-59.109. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For all uses, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Section 26 of Part I of this article.

(b) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Additional Provisions
59.text:
SEC. S-59.110. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise provided in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Paving
59.text:
SEC. S-59.111. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Compliance With Conditions
59.text:
SEC. S-59.112. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in

this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 25824)

59.title: Zoning Map
59.text:
SEC. S-59.113. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 59 is located on Zoning Map Nos. H-7 and I-7. (Ord. 25824)

60.title: Legislative History
60.text:
SEC. S-60.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 60 was established by Ordinance No. 25882, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 9, 2005. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Property Location And Size
60.text:
SEC. S-60.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 60 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Congress Avenue and Wycliff Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 60 is approximately 8,100 square feet. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Definitions And Interpretations
60.text:
SEC. S-60.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) This subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Development Plan
60.text:
SEC. S-60.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For the office use, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-60A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the development plan, the provisions of this article control.

(b) Unless otherwise provided, development and use of the Property for all other uses must comply with the MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict regulations within PD 193. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Main Uses Permiited
60.text:
SEC. S-60.105. MAIN USES PERMIITED.

The following main uses are permitted in this subdistrict:

(1) Office. Only the structure shown on the development plan that is in existence on February 9, 2005, may be utilized for this purpose.

(2) All other uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this PD subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this PD subdistrict. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Accessory Uses

SEC. S-60.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108, “Accessory Uses." For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Part I of this article. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
60.text:
SEC. S-60.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in PD 193. In the event of a conflict between this section and PD 193, this section controls.)

(a) Except as provided below, the yard, lot, and space regulations in Section 51P-193.125, “MF-2 Multiple Family Subdistrict,” apply to this subdistrict.

(b) Minimum setbacks for the office use are as shown on the development plan.

(c) Maximum floor area is 1,596 square feet.

(d) Maximum structure height is 24 feet.

(e) Maximum number of stories is one. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Off-Street Parking
60.text:
SEC. S-60.108. OFF-STREET PARKING.

(a) For the office use, parking must be provided in accordance with the requirements of PD 193.

(b) For all other uses, consult the use regulations in PD 193 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Environmental Performance Standards
60.text:
SEC. S-60.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Landscaping
60.text:
SEC. S-60.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For the office use, landscaping must be provided in accordance with the landscape plan (Exhibit S-60B).

(b) For all other uses, landscaping must be provided in accordance with the requirements of PD 193.

(c) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Signs
60.text:
SEC. S-60.111. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Additional Provisions
60.text:
SEC. S-60.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the development plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article.

60.title: Paving
60.text:
SEC. S-60.113. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Compliance With Conditions
60.text:
SEC. S-60.114. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 25882)

60.title: Zoning Map
60.text:
SEC. S-60.115. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 60 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. 25882)

61.title: Legislative History
61.text:
SEC. S-61.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 61 was established by Ordinance No. 25954, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 27, 2005. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Property Location And Size
61.text:
SEC. S-61.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 61 is established on property bounded by Bowen Street, Katy Trail, Turtle Creek Trail, and Cedar Springs Road. The size of PD 193 Subdistrict 61 is approximately 5.85 acres. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Definitions And Interpretations
61.text:
SEC. S-61.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) RETIREMENT HOUSING COMMUNITY means one lot, constituting the entire subdistrict, with any combination of a retirement housing use and a convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions use along with any limited and accessory uses.

(2) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(3) SUBDIVISION SIGN means a sign that identifies a single family, duplex, or townhouse residential neighborhood, a retirement housing community, or a business park.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) For a retirement housing community use, this subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning subdistrict. For all other uses, this subdistrict is considered to be a non-residential zoning subdistrict.

(e) The provisions of the Turtle Creek Environmental Corridor Ordinance (Ordinance No. 14874) apply to the Property. In the event of a conflict between the terms of the Turtle Creek Environmental Corridor Ordinance and this article, the terms of the Turtle Creek Environmental Corridor Ordinance control. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Development Plan
61.text:
SEC. S-61.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a retirement housing community, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-61A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For a retirement housing community, an amendment to the development plan to provide access from the Property to Katy Trail shall be considered to be a minor amendment to the development plan.

(c) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51- 4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Main Uses Permitted
61.text:
SEC. S-61.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are:

(1) a retirement housing community (permitted by right). For a retirement housing community, all patients in the convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions use must reside in dwelling units or suites.

(2) if the property is not used as a retirement housing community, those uses permitted in the O-2 Office Subdistrict in Part I of this article, subject to the same conditions applicable in the O-2 Office Subdistrict as set out in Part I of this article, except that a combination of a retirement housing use and a convalescent nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions use on one lot is prohibited. For example, a use permitted only by specific use permit (SUP) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is permitted only by SUP in this subdistrict, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Accessory Uses
61.text:
SEC. S-61.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Part I of this article. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(b) For a retirement housing community, the following accessory uses are limited to use by residents, guests, and employees of the retirement housing community:

-- Game court (private). -- Private recreation, club, or area. -- Swimming pool (private). (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Limited Uses
61.text:
SEC. S-61.107. LIMITED USES.

In conjunction with a retirement housing community, the following uses are permitted by right as limited uses only, and are subject to all of the regulations set forth in Section 51P-193.109 except as provided in this section:

-- Bank or savings and loan office (without drive-in window service). -- Bar, lounge, or tavern. -- Barber and beauty shop. -- Car wash.

-- Community center (private). [This use must comply with Section 51P- 193.108(b)(6)(E).] -- Common dining facility. [This use and any related kitchen must enhance its exterior venting filtration system with charcoal or equivalent filters to mitigate the amount of odor vented to the exterior of the building.] -- Drug store. -- Florist store. -- Health studio. -- Handcrafted art work studio. -- Hotel and motel. -- Instructional arts studio. -- Laundry or cleaning pickup and receiving station. -- Medical clinic. -- Office. -- Private club. -- Retail food store. -- Retail store other than listed. -- Theatre. -- Warehouse. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
61.text:
SEC. S-61.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the O-2 Office Subdistrict apply in this subdistrict.

(b) Retirement housing community. For a retirement housing community, the following regulations apply:

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(2) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yards are 20 feet.

(3) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units and suites together is 350.

(4) Height and stories. Maximum structure height is 240 feet in the tower area as shown on the development plan, not to exceed 23 stories. Maximum structure height is 50 feet in the four- story area as shown on the development plan, not to exceed four stories. Any proposed changes to the maximum structure heights, number of stories, or location of the building envelopes for the tower area or the four-story area as shown on the development plan shall be considered a request for a change in zoning and shall not be considered as a minor amendment to the development plan.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 75 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 25954)

61.title: Off Street Parking And Loading
61.text:
SEC. S-61.109. OFF STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) For a retirement housing community, the minimum required parking is 1.2 spaces per dwelling unit or suite. Additional parking spaces are not required for accessory uses or limited uses.

(b) For a retirement housing community, two loading spaces are required, and they must be located in the parking garage, or within the residential structure.
