61.title: Signs
61.text:
SEC. S-61.112. SIGNS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Retirement housing community signs. For a retirement housing community, the following regulations modify the sign regulations for business zoning districts.

(1) Premise signs. A single detached premise sign is permitted along Bowen Street in the location shown on the development plan. No attached premise signs are permitted.

(2) Subdivision signs.

(A) In general. Except as provided in this section, all regulations in Section 51A-7.402(d) for subdivision signs apply to subdivision signs as defined in this division.

(B) Subdivision signs. Two subdivision signs with related landscaping and other related amenities, such as an irrigation system, are permitted, one in each of the two areas located within the city's right-of-way along Turtle Creek Boulevard as identified on the development plan and Exhibit S-61C. Neither of the two subdivision signs may exceed 10 feet in height, nor may they exceed

180 square feet in effective area, with a maximum effective message area of 40 square feet (for a subdivision sign, effective message area is the area within a minimum imaginary rectangle of vertical and horizontal lines that fully contains all characters, symbols or logos on the sign) per sign. Each of these two subdivision signs may be located on top of, within, or made part of a garden wall/guard-rail wall. Both subdivision signs may only contain the name of the retirement housing community.

(C) Private license granted.

(i) The city council hereby grants a 40-year revocable, non- exclusive license to the owner(s) of the property ("property owner") and/or a duly formed and existing homeowner’s association ("homeowner’s association") for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the subdivision sign requirements contained herein. The property owner and/or homeowner’s association are required to pay an annual fee of $1,000.00 per sign in accordance with Sec. 43-115 of the Dallas City Code as well as a one-time fee of $1,000.00 fee per sign in accordance with Sec. 43-115.1 of the Dallas City Code. A maximum of two subdivision signs are permitted on city property and in the city's right-of-way along Turtle Creek Boulevard as identified on the development plan with related landscaping and other related amenities. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. Except as provided in Subparagraph (D)(iv), the property owner and/or homeowner’s association is entitled to 30 days notice of any determination by the city of the necessity for such termination. Following the 30 days notice given to the property owner and/or homeowner’s association by the city, the city's determination shall be final and binding and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any further notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by the director, the property owner and/or homeowner’s association shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(ii) The property owner and/or homeowner’s association is not required to comply with any subdivision sign requirement contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a subdivision sign permit or the revocation of the license granted herein affecting signage.

(iii) Upon the installation of the subdivision signs, related landscaping and other related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the property owner and/or homeowner’s association shall procure, pay for and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the license granted herein, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence, $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an "occurrence" basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance shall be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, 1/C/North, Dallas, Texas 75201 and the policy shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the office of risk management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent same are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(iv) The property owner and/or homeowner’s association shall be responsible for maintaining the subdivision signs, related landscaping and other related amenities in good repair and condition and to keep the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to

maintain the subdivision signs, related landscaping and other related amenities. The granting of a license for subdivision signs, related landscaping and other related amenities under this section does not release the property owner and/or homeowner’s association from liability in the installation or maintenance of subdivision signs, related landscaping, and other related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(D) Subdivision sign permit.

(i) It is the responsibility of the property owner and/or homeowner’s association to apply for and obtain a subdivision sign permit before locating subdivision signs, related landscaping, or other related amenities in the parkway. An application for a subdivision sign permit must be made to the director of public works and transportation before an application for a building permit is made for work concerning the subdivision sign. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the subdivision signs, related planting or other related amenities proposed.

(ii) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction and planting or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a subdivision sign permit to the property owner; otherwise the director shall deny the permit.

(iii) The property owner and/or homeowner’s association is not required to comply with any subdivision sign requirements contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's denial of a subdivision sign permit.

(iv) A subdivision sign permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if, at any time, the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right- of-way. The property owner and/or homeowner’s association are not required to comply with any subdivision sign requirements contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a subdivision sign permit.

(v) The issuance of a subdivision sign permit under this section does not excuse the property owner and/or homeowner’s association, their agents, or employees from liability in the installation or maintenance of the subdivision signs, related landscaping or other related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(3) Temporary marketing signs. Two temporary marketing signs (in conjunction with the construction or sales office) are permitted in accordance with the following provisions:

(A) The temporary marketing sign located along Bowen Street must be removed prior to or simultaneously with the installation and final approval of the detached premise sign along Bowen Street. The temporary marketing sign located in the right-of-way along Turtle Creek Boulevard must be removed prior to or simultaneously with the installation and final approval of the subdivision signs in the right-of-way along Turtle Creek Boulevard.

(B) One temporary marketing monument sign is permitted along Bowen Street with no minimum setback required. For the purpose of this section, monument sign means a detached sign applied directly onto a ground level support structure instead of a pole support, with no separation between the sign and the ground, This temporary marketing monument sign may not exceed 10 feet in height, nor may it exceed 180 square feet in effective area.

(C) One temporary marketing sign (non-monument sign) is permitted on the Property or on city property and in the city's right-of-way immediately adjacent to the Property along Turtle Creek Boulevard, with a minimum setback of four feet from the front of the existing curb. The support structure for the non-monument sign may be affixed to the backside (creekside) of the retaining wall that is immediately adjacent to and along Turtle Creek Boulevard. In addition, this temporary marketing sign may not exceed 10 feet in height (as measured from the grade of the existing sidewalk located adjacent to and along Turtle Creek Boulevard), nor may it exceed 180 square feet in effective area.

(D) Private license granted.

(i) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owner(s) of the property ("property owner") for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the temporary marketing sign requirements contained herein. No annual fee is required for the temporary marketing sign. Only one temporary marketing sign is permitted on city property and in the city's right-of-way along Turtle Creek Boulevard. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. Except as provided in Subparagraph (E)(iv), the property owner is entitled to 30 days notice of any determination by the city of the necessity for such termination. Following the 30 days notice given to the property owner by the city, the city's determination shall be final and binding and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any further notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by the director, the property owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(ii) The property owner is not required to comply with any temporary marketing sign requirement contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a temporary marketing sign permit or the revocation of the license granted herein affecting signage.

(iii) Upon the installation of the temporary marketing sign, related landscaping and other related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the property owner shall procure, pay for and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the license granted herein, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $1,000,000 for each occurrence, $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an "occurrence" basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance shall be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, 1/C/North, Dallas, Texas 75201 and the policy shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the office of risk management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent same are covered by this liability insurance policy.

(iv) The property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the temporary marketing sign, related landscaping and other related amenities in good repair and condition and to keep the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the temporary sign, related landscaping and other related amenities. The granting of a license for a temporary marketing sign, related landscaping, and other related amenities under this section does not release the property

owner from liability in the installation or maintenance of the temporary marketing sign, related landscaping, and other related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(E) Temporary marketing sign permit.

(i) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a sign permit before locating the temporary marketing sign, related landscaping, or other related amenities in the parkway. An application for the temporary marketing sign permit must be made to the director of public works and transportation before an application for a building permit is made for work concerning the temporary marketing sign. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the temporary marketing sign, related planting or other related amenities proposed.

(ii) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction and planting or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue the temporary marketing sign permit to the property owner; otherwise the director shall deny the permit.

(iii) The property owner is not required to comply with any temporary marketing sign requirement contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's denial of a temporary marketing sign permit.

(iv) A temporary marketing sign permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if, at any time, the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any temporary marketing sign requirement contained herein if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a temporary marketing sign permit.

(v) The issuance of a temporary marketing sign permit under this section does not excuse the property owner, its agents, or employees from liability in the installation or maintenance of the temporary marketing signs, related landscaping, or other related amenities in the public right-of-way. (Ord. 25954)

SEC. S-61.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

which may be revoked if the builder does not make reasonable and continuous progress toward completion of construction following the initial four-year period. The temporary construction or sales office must be removed when a certificate of occupancy is issued for a residential use on the Property.

(3) For a retirement housing community, a minimum of one trash compactor is required. All trash compactors and dumpsters must be located in the parking garage, or within the residential structure.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

66.title: Definitions And Interpretations
66.text:
SEC. S-66.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193; and

(2) SUBAREA A and SUBAREA B mean the subareas shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-66A).

In the event of a conflict between the description of Subareas A and B in the Exhibit A of the ordinance establishing this subdistrict and the conceptual plan, the description in Exhibit A controls.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) Subarea A is considered to be a residential zoning district. Subarea B is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

SEC. S-66.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-66A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit S-66B: Subarea A development plan. (Ord. 29243)

66.title: Conceptual Plan
66.text:
SEC. S-66.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-66A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

66.title: Development Plan
66.text:
SEC. S-66.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Development and use of Subarea A must comply with the development plan for Subarea A (Exhibit S-66B).

(b) For Subarea B, a development plan in compliance with the conceptual plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in Subarea B.

(c) In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and a development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 26205)

66.title: Main Uses Permitted
66.text:
SEC. S-66.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this subsection, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted only by specific use permit (SUP) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is permitted in this subarea only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subarea; etc.

(B) The following main uses are prohibited:

(1) Utility and service uses.

-- Radio, television, or microwave tower. -- Telephone exchange, switching, and transmitting equipment.

(2) Transportation uses.

-- Airport or landing field. -- STOL (short takeoff or landing) port. -- Passenger bus station and terminal. -- Helicopter base. -- Heliport. -- Helistop. -- Railroad passenger station. -- Railroad team track.

(3) Community service uses.

-- Adult day care facility. -- Halfway house.

(4) Medical uses.

-- Hospital. -- Convalescent and nursing homes, hospice care, and related institutions. -- Ambulance service.

(5) Educational uses.

-- Business school. -- Technical school. -- College, university, or seminary. -- College fraternity or sorority house. -- College dormitory.

(6) Recreation and entertainment uses.

-- Carnival or circus (temporary). -- Wax museum.

(7) Bar and restaurant uses.

-- Dance hall.

(8) Professional, personal service, and custom crafts uses.

-- Trade center. -- Mortuary or funeral home. -- Commercial laundry or dry cleaning. -- Taxidermist. -- Broadcasting or recording studio. -- Commercial wedding chapel.

(9) Retail uses.

-- Liquor store. -- Feed store. -- Pawn shop.

(10) Motor vehicle related uses.

-- Automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (inside display). -- Automobile or motorcycle display, sales, and service (outside display). -- Auto auction. -- Auto glass, muffler, or seat cover shop. -- Auto parts sales (inside only). -- Auto parts sales (outside display). -- Auto repair garage (inside). -- Auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside). -- Car wash. -- Engine or motor repair shop.

(11) Commercial uses.

-- Plumbing, electrical, air conditioning, and heating shops. -- Lumber, brick, or building materials sales yard. -- Tool and equipment rental (inside display only). -- Stone, sand, or gravel mining. -- Sand, gravel, or earth sales and storage.

(12) Storage and waste disposal uses.

-- Warehouse. -- Inside salvage and reclamation.

(13) Animal related uses.

-- Farm or ranch. -- Veterinarian's office. -- Animal pound.

(14) Industrial and manufacturing uses.

-- U-cart concrete system. -- Light fabrication and assembly. -- Clothing manufacturing. -- Bedspread, drapes, and headboard manufacturing. -- Manufacturing laboratory. -- Corrugated cardboard box fabrication.

(Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

66.title: Accessory Uses
66.text:
SEC. S-66.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(b) In this subdistrict, the following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Amateur communication tower. -- Open storage. -- Private stable.

(c) In this subdistrict, the following accessory uses are permitted accessory to a multifamily use, provided that these accessory uses are primarily for the use of the occupants of the building, are contained entirely within the main building housing the multifamily use and connected parking garage, and have no exterior advertising or signs.

-- Community centers (private), specifically including, but not limited to such amenities as health studio areas, wine storage areas, hot tubs, pools, steamrooms, poolside refreshment areas, offices (e.g. business centers, internet cafés, etc.) theatres, pool tables, meeting rooms, and demonstration/party kitchens. (Ord. 26205)

66.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
66.text:
SEC. S-66.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict apply in this subdistrict.

(b) Setbacks from street frontages. Minimum setback from McKinney Avenue is 15 feet as shown on the development plan. Minimum setback from Harwood Street is 11 feet. No minimum setback from St. Paul Street.

(c) Side and rear setbacks. Minimum side and rear setback in Subarea A is 10 feet as shown on the development plan. No side or rear yard setback in Subarea B.

(d) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units in Subarea A is 230.

(e) Height.

(1) For multiple-family uses, maximum structure height in Subarea A is 285 feet.

(2) In Subarea A, structures located on a roof, such as chimneys, clerestories, communication towers, cooling towers, elevator penthouses or bulkheads, mechanical equipment rooms, plaza or terrace structures, pool structures, skylights, vent stacks, and visual screens that surround mechanical equipment are allowed to project up to 25 feet above the maximum structure height.

(3) No maximum structure height in Subarea B.

(f) Maximum floor area.

(1) Maximum floor area for all uses combined in Subarea A is 415,000 square feet.

(2) Maximum floor area for all non-residential uses combined in Subarea A is 5,000 square feet.

(3) No maximum floor area in Subarea B.

(g) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

66.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
66.text:
SEC. S-66.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) Parking structures with facades facing St. Paul Street, McKinney Avenue, and Harwood Street, must be either underground or have a façade consisting of any combination of pre-cast concrete (with or without stucco finish), stone, or metal finish provided that the metal finish matches design elements on the main structure for which parking is provided, and glass or louvers. Except for the garage entrances and exits, openings in these parking structure facades may not exceed 40 percent of the total parking structure facade area and must be concealed with louvers or enclosed with glass.

(c) Subarea B. All permanent parking structures must be either underground or concealed in a building with a facade that is similar in appearance to the facade of the main non-parking building for which the parking is accessory. At least 12 percent of the parking structure facade area (including openings, if any) must be covered with the same material used predominantly on the first 24 feet of height of the main non-parking building. Openings in the parking structure facade may not exceed 52 percent of the total facade area. (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

SEC S-66.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI.

(b) LEED certification in Subarea A.

(1) A United States Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) checklist, effective May 1, 2004, must be submitted with an application for a building permit for development on the Property, indicating how development of the Property will comply with a certified designation (26 to 32 project points). The development plans submitted for a building permit must be certified by a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, the building official shall determine that the project is consistent with the standards and criteria for a LEED certified designation.

(2) If during development of the Property, the developer is unable to achieve all of the green building rating system points identified on the checklist, the developer must replace any points not achieved with other green building rating system points acceptable under the United States Green Building Council’s LEED rating system.

(3) All supporting documentation and templates related to the points previously approved by the city for the LEED certified level designation must be submitted with an application for a certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy may not be issued until a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services certifies that the building complies with the LEED certified designation (26 to 32 project points). (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

66.title: Landscaping And Sidewalks
66.text:
SEC. S-66.111. LANDSCAPING AND SIDEWALKS.

(a) Landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with the landscape and screening requirements of PD 193.

(b) Sidewalks must be provided on the Property fronting on McKinney Avenue, Harwood Street, and St. Paul Street, with a minimum of five feet of parkway provided between the sidewalk and the curb. The McKinney Avenue and the Harwood Street sidewalk must be at least 10 feet wide, and the St. Paul Street sidewalk must be at least seven feet wide. The St. Paul Street sidewalk must be located at least two feet away from any building on the Property.

(c) A minimum of two pedestrian scale lighting fixtures must be provided along the sidewalk adjacent to Harwood Street in Subarea B. (Ord. Nos. 26205; 29243)

66.title: Signs
66.text:
SEC. S-66.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 26205)

66.title: Additional Provisions
66.text:
SEC. S-66.113. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise provided in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 26205)

66.title: Paving
66.text:
SEC. S-66.114. PAVING.

All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 26205)

66.title: Compliance With Conditions
66.text:
SEC. S-66.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26205)

67.title: Legislative History
67.text:
SEC. S-67.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 67 was established by Ordinance No. 26226, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 25, 2006. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Property Location And Size
67.text:
SEC. S-67.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 67 is established on property generally bounded by Dorothy Avenue, Bowser Avenue, Wheeler Street, Lemmon Avenue, Mahanna Street, Gilbert Avenue, the city limit line, Miles Street, and Holland Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 67 is approximately 25.0253 acres. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Definitions And Interpretations
67.text:
SEC. S-67.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions in Chapter 51 and in Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division:

(1) INTERMEDIATE LEVEL means any habitable floor area between the floor and ceiling of any story.

(2) RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT TRACT means a development of three or more individually platted lots in which the dwelling units, whether attached or detached, are accessed from a shared driveway, and the dwelling units do not have any other dwelling units above or below them.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) Tract H is considered to be a nonresidential subdistrict. All tracts except for Tract H are considered to be residential zoning districts.

(d) Tracts A through H are shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-67A). (Ord. 26226)

SEC. 51P-S-67.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-67A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit S-67B: Tract E development plan.

(3) Exhibit S-67C: Tract E landscape plan. (Ord. 29837)

67.title: Conceptual Plan
67.text:
SEC. S-67.104. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan except as provided in Section S-67.112. In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Development Plan
67.text:
SEC. S-67.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a development plan and landscape plan must be approved by the city plan commission before issuance of a building permit to authorize work in this subdistrict other than repair of existing structures, demolition and grading, the installation of fencing or other structures for security purposes, work associated with permitted temporary uses, or work intended to provide for the irrigation or maintenance of landscaping.

(b) For Tract E, development and use of the Property must comply with the Tract E development plan (Exhibit S-67B).

(c) In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and a development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. Nos. 26226; 29837)

67.title: Main Uses Permitted
67.text:
SEC. S-67.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Tracts A through G. The only main uses permitted in Tracts A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are those main uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in these tracts only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in these tracts, etc.

(b) Tract H.

(1) The only main uses permitted on Tract H are those main uses permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in Tract H only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in Tract H, etc.

(2) The following additional limitations apply to nonresidential main uses in Tract H:

(A) Nonresidential main uses are limited to the ground floor only.

(B) No exterior customer entrances or exits other than emergency exits may be located within 116 feet of Bowser Avenue. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Accessory Uses
67.text:
SEC. S-67.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted.

(b) In Tracts D, E, G, and H, an accessory use for a multiple-family main use on one of those tracts may also serve multiple-family main uses on other of those tracts.

(c) Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
67.text:
SEC. S-67.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) Front, side and rear yard.

(1) Tracts A, D, E, and F. Minimum front, side, and rear yard is as shown on the conceptual plan.

(2) Tracts B, C, G, and H. Minimum front, side, and rear yard is 15 feet.

(3) Steps and stoops. Stoops and stairs not exceeding eight feet in width, four feet in height from grade to the top of the stairs, and two-and-one-half feet in height from grade to the top landing of the stoop may extend up to five feet into a required front yard.

(4) Tract E. Planter boxes, retaining walls, stairs, and entry stoops/decks are permitted in required front yards as shown on the development plan and landscape plan. Listed improvements other than railing elements may not extend more than eight inches above the finished ground level of the building to which they are attached.

(b) Dwelling unit density.

(1) Total. Maximum number of dwelling units on the Property is 905.

(2) Tract A. Maximum number of dwelling units is 35.

(3) Tract B. Maximum number of dwelling units is 30.

(4) Tract C. Maximum number of dwelling units is 46.

(5) Tract F. Maximum number of dwelling units is 70.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) Tracts A, B, C, D, and F. Maximum floor area ratio is 1.5.

(2) Tract E and G. Maximum floor area ratio is 2.25.

(3) Tract H. Maximum floor area ratio is 2.0.

(4) Intermediate levels. The aggregate floor area of all intermediate levels may not exceed more than 50 percent of the floor area of the story in which the intermediate level is contained.

(5) Residential development tract. A residential development tract shall be treated as one lot for purposes of calculating floor area ratio.

(d) Height. Maximum structure height is as shown on the conceptual plan.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Tracts A, B, C, D, and F. Maximum lot coverage is 50 percent.

(2) Tract G. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent.

(3) Tracts E and H. Maximum lot coverage is 75 percent.

(4) Residential development tract. A residential development tract shall be treated as one lot for purposes of calculating lot coverage.

(5) Parking. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(6) Pools. Pools are not included in lot coverage calculations unless they are covered by a structure.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(g) Stories.

(1) Tracts A, B, C, E, and F. Maximum number of stories is three.

(2) Tract D. Maximum number of stories is four, with a maximum of three stories of habitable space and a maximum of one story of parking structure fully or partially above grade.

(3) Tract G. Maximum number of stories is four.

(4) Tract H. Maximum number of stories on the northern portion is four, and maximum number of stories on the southern portion is five, as shown on the conceptual plan.

(5) Intermediate levels. Intermediate levels are not counted as a story.

(h) Courts. One outer court may be provided on Tract H that is exempt from the minimum width and depth requirements of Section 51P-193.107(a)(3)(E)(iii). (Ord. Nos. 26226; 29837)

67.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
67.text:
SEC. S-67.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Except as provided in this section, consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information about off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) Required parking for multiple-family or single family uses on Tracts A, B, C, and F.

(1) Two garage parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit.

(2) In addition to the parking required in Paragraph (1), .25 unassigned guest parking spaces available for use by visitors and residents are required for each dwelling unit. The parking surface for guest parking spaces within the lot (not on-street) may be permeable pavement for motor vehicles. Spaces adjacent to the lot and on a public street may be counted toward this guest parking requirement if one additional two-inch caliper tree is planted on the lot for each on-street guest parking space. No more than two on-street parking spaces per tract may be used to meet the guest parking requirements. These on- street guest parking spaces remain subject to the city's authority to regulate public streets.

(c) Required parking for multiple-family uses on Tracts D, E, G, and H.

(1) Subject to the limitation in Paragraph (5), for each dwelling unit of less than 900 square feet with one or no separate bedroom, 1.12 parking spaces are required.

(2) Subject to the limitation in Paragraph (5), for each dwelling unit of 900 square feet or greater with one or no separate bedroom, one-and-one-half parking spaces are required.

(3) Subject to the limitation in Paragraph (5), for each dwelling unit with two or more bedrooms, 1.12 parking spaces per bedroom are required.

(4) For each dwelling unit, .25 unassigned guest parking spaces available for use by visitors and residents are required. The parking surface for guest parking spaces within the lot (not on- street) may be permeable pavement for motor vehicles. Spaces adjacent to the lot and on a public street may be counted toward this guest parking requirement if one additional two-inch caliper tree is planted on the lot for each on-street guest parking space. These on-street guest parking spaces remain subject to the city's authority to regulate public streets.

(5) Notwithstanding the number of parking spaces required pursuant to Paragraphs
(1) through (3), the minimum number of parking spaces provided for each phase for each of these tracts may not be less than 90 percent of the number of parking spaces that would be required for a multiple- family use pursuant to Part I of this article.

(d) Residential development tracts. A residential development tract shall be treated as one lot for purposes of guest parking requirements.

(e) Surface parking on Tract H. Surface parking on Tract H is not permitted in the area between an adjacent street frontage and a building façade facing that street frontage except for surface parking that is located within 132 feet of Lemmon Avenue.

(f) Structured parking. Structured parking decks located wholly above ground shall be concealed from the street by the façade or roof structure of a main building except that a break in the façade shall be permitted at the location of driveway and entryway areas not to exceed 40 feet in width.

On Tract H, structured parking decks adjacent to the out parcel on the same block may be concealed pursuant to Section 51P-193.127(a). (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Residential Development Tracts
67.text:
SEC. S-67.110. RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT TRACTS.

(a) The provisions of Part I of this article concerning residential development tracts apply to residential development tracts in this subdistrict. In the event of a conflict between a provision of this division and a provision of Part I of this article concerning residential development tracts, the provision of this division controls.

(b) In a residential development tract platted as a shared access development, more than 18 lots may be served by a shared access point, and more than two shared access points are permitted. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Environmental Performance Standards
67.text:
SEC. S-67.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Landscaping
67.text:
SEC. S-67.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) Landscaped open spaces adjacent to the public right-of-way must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan. In addition to the open space areas shown on the conceptual plan, the location of a landscaped open space a minimum 3,000 square feet in area adjacent to the public right-of-way must be identified on Tract F at the time of development plan approval. The following provisions apply to these landscaped open spaces:

(1) Except for the open space on Tract D, the location of a landscaped open space may be modified by the city plan commission at the time of development plan approval provided that the relocated open space is the same overall size as shown on the conceptual plan and has street frontage.

(2) Impervious surface for internal sidewalks, fountains, benches, and related uses must not exceed 35 percent. Required sidewalks adjacent to the street are not included in the calculation of impervious surface.

(3) The minimum planting requirements for a special planting area, as defined in Section 51P-193.126(b)(1)(D)(iii), apply.

(c) Front yard privacy fencing not exceeding eight feet in height is permitted in Tract A adjacent to Dorothy Avenue provided that the height of the main buildings adjacent to the fence on the same lot do not exceed 39 feet. The front yard privacy fencing must meet the following requirements:

(1) A minimum setback of 10 feet and a minimum average setback of 11 feet from the property line must be provided.

(2) An offset of at least 18 inches must be provided no less than every 55 feet.

(3) The total length may not exceed 150 feet without an intervening landscape area at least 15 feet in length.

(4) The fence must be constructed of masonry, except that decorative metal may be used to span landscape areas.

(5) One tree must be provided between the sidewalk and the fence for every 25 feet of fence length.

(d) When a phasing plan is approved as part of a development plan for a tract, landscaping may be installed by phase. Individual units, including individual buildings in a residential development tract, may qualify for a final inspection prior to the completion of the landscaping installation for the remainder of the development plan.

(e) At the time of landscape plan approval, the city plan commission may approve alternative locations for required trees provided that it finds the alternative placement meets the spirit and intent of Section 51P-193.126.

(f) At the time of landscape plan approval, the city plan commission may approve sidewalk locations, widths, and designs that vary from the requirements of this subsection and Section 51P- 193.126(b)(4) when necessary to preserve existing trees.

(g) In Tracts A and B, a minimum 10-foot-wide landscape buffer must be provided adjacent to properties not included in this subdistrict as shown on the conceptual plan. Fences are permitted to cross the landscape buffer.

(h) For Tract E, landscaping must be provided in accordance with the Tract E landscape plan (Exhibit S-67C).

(i) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 26226; 29837)

67.title: Signs
67.text:
SEC. S-67.113. SIGNS.

(a) Signs in Tracts A through G must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signs in Tract H must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. On Tract H, the following additional limitations apply:

(1) Detached pole-mounted signs containing a commercial message are limited to a maximum height of four feet.

(2) No sign for a nonresidential main use may be located within 116 feet of Bowser Avenue. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Additional Provisions
67.text:
SEC. S-67.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division or shown on the conceptual plan, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 26226)

67.title: Compliance With Conditions
67.text:
SEC. S-67.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) Except as otherwise provided in this division, or in Part I of this article, all paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, on any building site in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city with respect to that building site. (Ord. 26226)

70.title: Legislative History
70.text:
SEC. S-70.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 70 was established by Ordinance No. 26315, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 26, 2006. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Property Location And Size
70.text:
SEC. S-70.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 70 is established on property generally bounded by Cedar Springs Road, Hawthorne Avenue, Hartford Street, and the northern half of Raleigh Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 70 is 3.32 acres. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Definitions And Interpretations
70.text:
SEC. S-70.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Development Plan
70.text:
SEC. S-70.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For multiple-family uses, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-70A). In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51A- 4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. Nos. 26315; 26964)

70.title: Main Uses
70.text:
SEC. S-70.105. MAIN USES.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Accessory Uses
70.text:
SEC. S-70.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
70.text:
SEC. S-70.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict apply in this subdistrict.

(b) Multiple-family uses. The following restrictions apply for multiple-family uses.

(1) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 125.

(2) Height. The following height restrictions apply if any part of a building is used for multiple-family uses.

(A) Buildings A, B, C, D, E, and F.

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, maximum structure height is 38 feet.

(ii) Maximum height of parapets is two feet above the roof line.

(iii) Maximum height for elevator penthouses and stairwells is 44 feet.

(B) Building G.

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, maximum structure height is 58 feet.

(ii) Maximum height of parapets is three feet above the roof line.

(iii) Maximum height for elevator penthouses and stairwells is 66 feet.

(3) Location. Buildings A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and the entrance to the property must be located as shown on the development plan. All elevator penthouses and stairwells must also be located as shown on the development plan.

(4) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Stories.

(A) Maximum number of stories above grade for Buildings A, B, C, D, E, and F is three.

(B) Maximum number of stories above grade for Building G is four. (Ord. Nos. 26315; 26964)

70.title: Off Street Parking And Loading
70.text:
SEC. S-70.108. OFF STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations of PD 193 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Environmental Performance Standards
70.text:
SEC. S-70.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Landscaping
70.text:
SEC. S-70.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article and the perimeter planting plan (Exhibit S-70B). In case of conflict, the perimeter planting plan controls.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 26315; 26964)

70.title: Signs
70.text:
SEC. S-70.111. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Additional Provisions
70.text:
SEC. S-70.112. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except as otherwise specified in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Compliance With Conditions
70.text:
SEC. S-70.113. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 26315)

70.title: Zoning Map
70.text:
SEC. S-70.114. ZONING MAP.

PD Subdistrict 70 is located on Zoning Map No. I-7. (Ord. 26315)

The size of PD Subdistrict 72 is approximately 2.5576 acres. (Ord. 26393)

72.title: Development Plan

74.title: Legislative History
74.text:
SEC. S-74.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 74 was established by Ordinance No. 26412, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 9, 2006. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Property Location And Size
74.text:
SEC. S-74.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 74 is established on property located at the west corner of Cedar Springs Road and McKinnon Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 74 is approximately 5.203 acres. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Definitions And Interpretations
74.text:
SEC. S-74.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.
(b) In this division:

(1) PARKWAY means the portion of a street right-of-way between the projected street curb and a lot line.

(2) RECIPIENT OF NOTICE means the property owner of record of Lot 1A in City Block 1/929, commonly known as 2828 N. Harwood.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Subareas And Subtracts
74.text:
SEC. S-74.104. SUBAREAS AND SUBTRACTS.

This subdistrict has two subareas, A and B, as shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-74A). Subareas A and B are further divided into Subtracts A1, A2, A3, B1, and B2 as shown on the conceptual plan. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Conceptual Plan
74.text:
SEC. S-74.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

(a) Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan.

(b) Any requested change to the conceptual plan must be provided to the Recipient of Notice by the applicant when an application is submitted to the city. Notice is only required until July 1, 2016. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Development Plan
74.text:
SEC. S-74.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Development and use of Subarea A must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S- 74B).

(b) A development plan for Subarea B that complies with the conceptual plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in Subarea B. Development plans may be submitted in phases.

(c) Any requested development plan, or requested amendment to a development plan, must be provided to the Recipient of Notice by the applicant when an application is submitted to the city. Notice is only required until July 1, 2016.

(d) In the event of a conflict between the text of this division and a development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Main Uses Permitted
74.text:
SEC. S-74.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in Subsections (b) and (c), the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) The following uses are prohibited in this subdistrict:

-- Airport or landing field. -- Auto glass, muffler, or seat cover shop. -- Auto repair garage (inside or outside). -- Building repair and maintenance shop. -- Car wash. -- Lodging or boarding house. -- Outside commercial amusement. -- Overnight general purpose shelter. -- Passenger bus station and terminal. -- Plumbing, electrical, air conditioning, and heating shop. -- Service station. -- Water treatment plant.

(c) Residential uses are prohibited in Subarea A. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Accessory Uses
74.text:
SEC. S-74.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P- 193.108.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this subdistrict:

-- Amateur communication tower.

-- Open storage (except during construction). -- Private stable.

(c) A community center (private) is permitted if it is accessory to a multifamily use, is primarily for the occupants of the multifamily use, is contained entirely within the main structure or connected parking garage, and has no exterior signage or advertising. An accessory community center (private) may include amenities such as health studios, wine storage areas, hot tubs, pools, steamrooms, poolside refreshment areas, offices, theaters, pool tables, meeting rooms, and demonstration/party kitchens. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
74.text:
SEC. S-74.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. In the event of a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) Front, side, and rear yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no minimum front, side, and rear yard.

(2) Minimum setback from Cedar Springs Road is 35 feet.

(3) In Subarea A, minimum setback from McKinnon Street is as shown on the conceptual plan. In Subarea B, minimum setback from McKinnon Street is 10 feet.

(4) Minimum setback from the private drive along the northern boundary of the Property is 20 feet.

(5) Minimum setback from the private drive along the western boundary of the Property is 10 feet.

(6) Pedestrian amenities set forth in Section S-74.110(b) are permitted in the setback areas.

(b) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 375.

(c) Floor area.

(1) Total floor areas.

(A) Maximum floor area for all uses combined on the Property is 885,000 square feet.

(B) Maximum floor area for all uses combined in Subarea A is 435,000 square feet.

(C) Maximum floor area for all uses combined in Subarea B is 450,000 square feet.

(2) Retail floor area.

(A) Maximum floor area for all retail uses combined on the Property is 55,000 square feet.

(B) Maximum floor area for all retail uses combined in Subarea B is 25,000 square feet.

(3) Office floor area.

(A) Maximum floor area for all office uses combined on the Property is 450,000 square feet.

(B) Maximum floor area for all office uses combined in Subarea B is 25,000 square feet.

(d) Height.

(1) Absolute height limits.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height, including mechanical equipment, is the lower of 276 feet or 740 feet above mean sea level (AMSL).

(B) Maximum structure height in Subtract A1 is the lower of 276 feet or 740 feet AMSL.

(C) Maximum structure height for Subtract A2 is the lower of 256 feet or 720 feet AMSL.

(D) Maximum structure height for Subtract A3 is the lower of 105 feet or 569 feet AMSL.

(E) Maximum structure height for Subtract B1 is the lower of 276 feet or 736 feet AMSL.

(F) Maximum structure height for Subtract B2 is the lower of 185 feet or 645 feet AMSL.

(2) Allocation of structure heights.

(A) Structures with a height equal to or lower than the lower of 105 feet or 569 feet AMSL may cover no more than 70 percent of the Property.

(B) Structures with a height higher than the lower of 105 feet or 569 feet AMSL may cover no more than 35 percent of the Property.

(e) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground structures are not. For the purposes of calculating lot coverage, the Property is considered to be one lot.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(g) Stories. No maximum number of stories above grade. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
74.text:
SEC. S-74.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Parking reduction for nonresidential uses for pedestrian amenities.

(1) For each of the following pedestrian amenities provided in excess of three, the required parking for nonresidential uses may be reduced by four percent, up to a maximum 20 percent reduction:

(A) Bicycle parking at one five-bicycle unit per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two units per lot.

(B) Awning/canopies with a minimum overhang of four feet and a minimum length of 25 feet per 100 feet of building facade.

(C) A combination of street trees and evergreen shrubs with a minimum of one small tree per 25 feet of frontage and a minimum of one shrub per five feet of frontage.

(D) Benches at one per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two units per lot.

(E) Trash receptacles at one per 100 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two receptacles per lot.

(F) Pedestrian street lamps (free-standing or wall-mounted) at one lamp per 50 feet of frontage.

(G) Enhanced sidewalk with stamped concrete or brick pavers for the full width of the sidewalk along the entire frontage.

(H) Public art or water features costing no less than $2,500, at one per lot.

(I) Drinking fountains at one per lot.

(2) Bicycle parking must be one of the amenities.

(3) The pedestrian amenities must be provided within the curb-to-building area, in a pedestrian plaza, or within private streets or driveways and their pedestrian ways.

(4) Pedestrian amenities must serve to enhance pedestrian pathways from building entrances to trolley or transit stops.

(5) Amenities must be placed far enough apart from the street curb so as not to create a physical barrier to buses.

(6) Canopies, awnings, and pedestrian street lamps must have a minimum of nine- foot clearance.

(7) Light fixtures may not exceed 14 feet in height and may not emit light upward into the windows of dwelling units.

(8) All pedestrian amenities must be maintained by the owner of the lot; if there is more than one owner, all owners are severally liable for maintenance.

(c) Shared parking adjustments.

(1) Total required parking may be adjusted pursuant to the mixed use development option provided in Section 51P-193.113(g)(4).

(2) Up to 20 percent of the parking for residential uses may be used as nonresidential parking between 7:30 a.m. and 6:30 p.m.

(d) Limits on parking reductions.

(1) All reductions to parking requirements must be indicated on an approved development plan.

(2) In no event may the total parking requirement for each subarea be reduced by more than 30 percent.

(e) Residential uses.

(1) One parking space is required for each dwelling unit with one or fewer bedrooms, and one parking space is required per bedroom for dwelling units with more than one bedroom.

(2) One visitor parking space is required for each eight dwelling units.

(f) Aboveground parking structures.

(1) Aboveground parking structures with facades facing Cedar Springs Road, Pearl Street, or McKinnon Street must have a facade consisting of any combination of pre-cast concrete (with or without stucco finish), stone, metal (the metal finish must match design elements on the main structure), glass, or louvers.

(2) Except for the garage entrances and exits, openings in aboveground parking structure facades may not exceed 80 percent of the total parking structure facade area and must be concealed with louvers or enclosed with glass.

(3) Interior lighting in an aboveground parking structure may not have a visible source of illumination and must be installed to reduce glare and the consequent interference with boundary streets or adjacent property.

(4) Interior lighting at the perimeter of each level of a parking structure must provide no more than 1.5 footcandles of illumination from 10 p.m. until 6 a.m.

(5) Exposed ductwork or mechanical equipment other than for ventilation may not be located on an aboveground parking structure facade facing McKinnon Street; the ductwork or mechanical equipment on this facade that is necessary for ventilation must be screened.

(6) Climbing vegetation must be provided on the parking structure facade facing McKinnon Street.

(g) Loading. Loading doors must remain closed except when in use. (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Environmental Performance Standards
74.text:
SEC. S-74.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, see Article VI.

(b) LEED compliance. For all uses, the following LEED compliance provisions must be met.

(1) A United States Green Building Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) checklist, effective May 1, 2004 (or more current), must be submitted with an application for a building permit for development on the Property, indicating how development of the Property will comply with a LEED compliance designation (26 to 32 project points). A LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services must affirm that development plans submitted for a building permit are LEED compliant. Prior to the issuance of a building permit, the building official shall determine that the project is consistent with the standards and criteria for a LEED compliance designation.

(2) If during development of the Property, the developer is unable to achieve all of the green building rating system points identified on the checklist, the developer must replace any points not achieved with other green building rating system points acceptable under the United States Green Building Council’s LEED rating system.

(3) All supporting documentation and templates related to the points previously approved by the city for the LEED level designation must be submitted with an application for a certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy may not be issued until a LEED accredited professional designated by the department of development services affirms that the building complies with the LEED compliance designation (26 to 32 project points). (Ord. 26412)

74.title: Landscaping
74.text:
SEC. S-74.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscape plans.

(1) Trees and sidewalks must be provided as shown on the tree and sidewalk plan (Exhibit S-74C).

(2) Landscaping for Subarea A must be provided as shown on the Subarea A landscape plan (Exhibit S-74D).

(3) Landscaping for Subarea B must be provided as shown on the Subarea B landscape plan (Exhibit S-74E).

(4) Any requested change to landscape plans must be provided to the Recipient of Notice by the applicant when an application is submitted to the city. Notice is only required until July 1, 2016.

(b) Pedestrian amenity and parking garage rooftop plan. For each subarea, a pedestrian amenity and parking garage rooftop plan that complies with the conceptual plan, development plan, and landscape plans must be approved by the city plan commission prior to issuance of a building permit in that subarea. The pedestrian amenity and parking garage rooftop plan must show all pedestrian amenities to be used for parking reduction purposes, and all landscaping in outdoor amenity areas on top of parking structures. The pedestrian amenity plan and parking garage rooftop plan must be provided to Recipient of Notice by the applicant when it is submitted to the city. Notice is only required until July 1, 2016.

(c) Parking garage rooftop enhancements and planting materials.

(1) A minimum of 20 percent of exposed parking garage rooftops must be landscaped area, with low maintenance plant materials, such as mosses, vines, grasses, herbs, or water features. The remaining 80 percent must be visually enhanced with geometric patterns of colored roof ballast or pavers, patios, or roof architectural features such as skylights, trellises with plant materials, canopies, or awnings.

(2) Planting materials in outdoor amenity areas on parking garage rooftops count toward the landscaping requirements.

(d) Permeable area. A minimum of 4.5 percent of the Property must be permeable area.

(e) Timing of landscape installation. All required landscaping must be installed prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for a use in that subarea.

(f) Sidewalks. Sidewalks along Cedar Springs Road, Pearl Street, and McKinnon Street must have a minimum width of eight feet, with a minimum unobstructed width of five feet. Information and advertising kiosks are prohibited in the sidewalk area.

(g) Street trees. Trees along McKinnon Street must have a minimum caliper of four inches. Street trees must be planted at a maximum of 25 feet on center as shown on the tree and sidewalk plan.

(h) Planter walls. Planter walls in Subarea A as shown on the tree and sidewalk plan must be provided on McKinnon Street and must be covered with vines and other vegetative materials.

(i) Private license granted.

(1) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners, or with the written consent of the owner, to the tenants (“property owner”) of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the parkway landscaping requirements and pedestrian amenity options of this division. A property owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a parkway landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code, or Subsection (j) of this section. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city of the necessity for such termination shall be final and binding and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by the director, each property owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(2) A property owner is not required to comply with any landscaping requirement if compliance is made impossible due to the director’s revocation of a landscape permit or the revocation of the license granted herein affecting landscaping.

(3) Upon the installation of landscaping, pedestrian amenities, and related amenities, such as irrigation systems, in the public rights-of-way, the property owner shall procure, pay for and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the license granted herein, with combined single limits of liability

for bodily injury and property damage of not less that $1,000,000 for each occurrence, $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an occurrence basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance shall be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, 1/C/North, Dallas, Texas 75201 and the policy shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the Office of Risk Management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal, or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent it is covered by this liability insurance policy.

(4) Each property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the landscaping, pedestrian amenities, and related amenities in good repair and condition and to keep the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city, and the City shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the landscaping, pedestrian amenities, and related amenities. The granting of a license for landscaping, pedestrian amenities, and related amenities under this section does not release the property owner from liability in the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, pedestrian amenities, and related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(j) Parkway landscape permit.

(1) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain a parkway landscape permit before locating trees, landscaping, pedestrian amenities, or related amenities in the parkway. An application for a parkway landscape permit must be made to the director of public works and transportation before an application for a building permit is made for work on the lot. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the parkway affected and the planting or other amenities proposed.

(2) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction and planting or other amenities proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a parkway landscape permit to the property owner; otherwise, the director shall deny the permit.

(3) A property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this division if compliance is made impossible due to the director's denial of a parkway landscape permit.

(4) A parkway landscape permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the director determines that the use of the parkway authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any parkway landscaping requirement of this division if compliance is made impossible due to the director's revocation of a parkway landscape permit.

(k) For the purpose of all landscaping calculations required by this section, the Property is considered to be one lot.

(l) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 26412)

PD Subdistrict 75 was established by Ordinance No. 26593, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 14, 2007. (Ord. Nos. 26953; 28979)

75.title: Property Location And Size
75.text:
SEC. S-75.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 75 is established on property bounded by Lucas Drive, Cotton Belt Avenue, and Arroyo Drive. The size of PD Subdistrict 75 is 6.09 acres. (Ord. Nos. 26953; 28979)

75.title: Definitions And Interpretations
75.text:
SEC. S-75.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. In the event of a conflict, this division controls. In the event of a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

SEC. S-75.103.1. EXHIBIT.

SEC. S-75.103.2. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-75A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 28979)
