145.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
145.text:
SEC. S-145.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(b) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet on Maple Avenue and five feet on Amelia Street. Stoops, steps, handrails, guardrails, planters, patios, shade structures, transformers and other utility equipment, benches and other pedestrian seating, pots, raised planters, sculptures, and other decorative landscape features may project a maximum of five feet into the required front yard.

(c) Floor area.

(1) Maximum floor area for a retail use is 8,000 square feet.

(2) Maximum floor area for a restaurant without drive-through service use is 4,000 square feet.

(3) Maximum floor area for a bar, lounge, or tavern use is 1,800 square feet.

(d) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 0.8.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet. (Ord. 31095)

145.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
145.text:
SEC. S-145.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off- street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service requires a minimum of one parking space per 110 square feet of floor area.

(c) Maximum height of light fixtures is eight feet. (Ord. Nos. 31095; 32980)

145.title: Environmental Performance Standards
145.text:
SEC. S-145.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

(a) See Article VI.

(b) All light fixtures must be designed to direct the light source downward and away from adjoining properties. (Ord. 31095)

145.title: Landscaping
145.text:
SEC. S-145.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-145B).

(b) For a bank or savings and loan office with a drive in window, landscaping must be provided as required by SUP.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 31095; 32980)

145.title: Screening
145.text:
SEC. S-145.112. SCREENING.

(a) A minimum eight-foot solid screening fence is required to screen surface parking along a portion of the northeast boundary of this subdistrict.

(b) A minimum six-foot solid screening fence is required to screen surface parking along a portion of the northwest boundary of this subdistrict. (Ord. Nos. 31095; 32980)

SEC. S-145.112.1. DESIGN STANDARDS

(a) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum six-foot wide unobstructed sidewalk with a minimum five-foot wide buffer is required along all street frontages. If the building official determines there is a conflict with existing utilities, the required landscape buffer width may be reduced entirely.

(2) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and must be designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk.

(b) Ground level transparency. A minimum transparency of 20 percent is required on the ground-level street-facing facades of buildings. Screening materials that are more than 40 percent open are permitted between the transparent surface and the street if a street-facing facade has over 50 percent transparency.

(c) Ground floor entries. All street-facing facades must have an entrance that accesses the street with an improved path connecting to the sidewalk. A single building entry served by a common exterior covered entry may be provided in lieu of separate facade entries.

(d) Driveways.

(1) Maple Avenue. A driveway may not exceed 16 feet in width where it crosses a

sidewalk. A driveway on Maple Avenue may only be used for vehicle egress.

(2) Amelia Street. Only one driveway is permitted. This driveway many not exceed 26 feet in width where it crosses a sidewalk.

(e) Buffers. Except within a visibility triangle, where public sidewalks abut any driving surface, off-street or on-street loading area, or parking surface, the following buffering must be used:

(1) Landscaping plantings with a minimum height of 36 inches; or

(2) Bollards with a minimum height of 36 inches, spaced no more than six feet in distance from each other. (Ord. 32980)

145.title: Signs
145.text:
SEC. S-145.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31095)

145.title: Additional Provisions
145.text:
SEC. S-145.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Except for a drive-through loudspeaker for a bank or savings and loan office that complies with Section 51P-193.129, outdoor loudspeakers are prohibited.

(d) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. Nos. 31095; 32980)

145.title: Compliance With Conditions
145.text:
SEC. S-145.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31095)

146.title: Legislative History
146.text:
SEC. S-146.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 146 was established by Ordinance No. 31087, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 9, 2019. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Property Location And Size
146.text:
SEC. S-146.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 146 is established on property located at the west corner of Cedar Springs Road and Maple Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 146 is 2.56 acres. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Definitions And Interpretations
146.text:
SEC. S-146.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division,

(1) BLANK WALL AREA means any portion of the exterior of a building that does not include a material change, windows or doors, or columns, pilasters, or other articulation greater than 12 inches in depth. Blank wall area is measured horizontally on each story of a building.

(2) GROUND STORY means the story closest to and above grade along the street.

(3) ON-SITE OPEN SPACE means the portion of a building site that is accessible to the general public. On-site open space is principally open to the sky but allows for architectural elements such as colonnades, pergolas, and gazebos. The on-site open space must be a contiguous open area of not less than 10 feet in width or length.

(4) STOOP means a small porch that may include stairs leading to the entrance of a residence.

(5) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(6) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window and door openings filled with glass, expressed as a percentage of the total facade area by story. Transparency is measured from floor to floor of each story of a building.

(7) UPPER STORY means any story above the ground story.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31087)

SEC. S146.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-146A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-146B: landscape plan. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Development Plan
146.text:
SEC. S-146.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S- 146A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Main Uses Permitted
146.text:
SEC. S-146.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict:

(1) Residential uses.

None permitted.

(2) Utility and service uses.

-- Utility or governmental installation other than listed. -- Local utilities. -- Tower/antenna for cellular communication. [Limited to a mounted cellular antenna.]

(3) Transportation uses.

None permitted.

(4) Community services uses.

None permitted.

(5) Medical uses.

-- Medical clinic. -- Optical shop.

(6) Religious uses.

-- Church.

(7) Educational uses.

-- Library, art gallery or museum.

(8) Recreation and entertainment uses.

-- Public park or playground.

(9) Bar and restaurant uses.

-- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. -- Private club. -- Catering service.

(10) Professional, personal service, and custom crafts uses.

-- Office. -- Temporary construction or sales office. -- Bank or savings and loan office. [Drive-in window service prohibited.] -- Barber and beauty shop. -- Health studio. -- Laundry or cleaning pick-up and receiving station. -- Travel bureau. -- Broadcasting or recording studio. -- Handcrafted art work studio. -- Photography studio. -- Safe deposit boxes.

(11) Retail uses.

-- Retail food store. -- Bakery or confectionery shop. -- Book and stationery store. -- Camera shop. -- Cigar, tobacco, and candy store. -- Clothing store. -- Drug store.

-- Florist store.

(12) Motor vehicle related uses.

None permitted.

(13) Commercial uses.

None permitted.

(14) Storage and waste disposal uses.

None permitted.

(15) Animal related uses.

None permitted.

(16) Industrial and manufacturing uses.

None permitted. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Accessory Uses
146.text:
SEC. S-146.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
146.text:
SEC. S-146.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for LC Light Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Increased development standards. When the provisions of S-146.113 are met, the following modifications to LC Light Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet for the first 36 feet in height and 25 feet for any portion of a building above 36 feet in height. Encroachments of retaining walls, uncovered patios, public access points, garage access stairs, and related canopies, and up to 48

inches in height for stairs, steps, stoops, railings, bicycle racks, and freestanding walls are allowed in the required front yard without limitation. Canopies, awnings, and roof eaves may project up to five feet into the required front yard.

(2) Side and rear yard. No minimum side or rear yard.

(3) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 6.0:1. For purposes of this paragraph, covered outdoor patios and building terraces are excluded from the calculation of floor area.

(4) Height. Maximum structure height is 399 feet.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 50 percent. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations.

(6) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is 27. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
146.text:
SEC. S-146.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Alternative parking standards. When the provisions of Section S-146.113 are met, the following modifications to the specific off-street parking and loading requirements in Part I of this article apply.

(1) Office uses. For office uses, a minimum of one space per 430 square feet of floor area is required. Covered and uncovered patios and terraces are excluded from the calculation of floor area for purposes of calculating minimum parking requirements.

(2) Service area screening. All delivery, trash collection, storage, and removal facilities must be screened from the public right-of-way. The screening materials must be a minimum of six feet tall and constructed with masonry, steel, aluminium, or composite metal panels. Wood gates are prohibited.

(3) Loading. Three off-street loading spaces are required on the Property. A minimum of one loading space must be a large loading space, and two loading spaces may be small loading spaces.

(4) Mechanized parking. Except as provided in this paragraph, mechanized parking in accordance with Division 51A-4.340 may be used to satisfy off-street parking requirements.

(A) Mechanized parking licenses issued for the Property do not expire.

(B) If the building official determines that substantive changes to the original application apply, a new application for mechanized parking must be submitted under Section 51A-4.343. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Environmental Performance Standards
146.text:
SEC. S-146.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Landscaping
146.text:
SEC. S-146.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with LC Light Commercial Subdistrict of Part I of this article.

(b) When a building exceeds 240 feet in height or 4.0:1 floor area ratio, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-146B).

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Signs
146.text:
SEC. S-146.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Urban Design Provisions
146.text:
SEC. S-146.113. URBAN DESIGN PROVISIONS.

(a) Applicability. For a project to qualify for the increased development standards in Section S-146.108(b) and the alternative parking standards in Section S-146.109(b), it must comply with all requirements in this section. If the increased development standards and the alternative parking standards are not applied, the provisions of this section do not apply.

(b) Blank wall. Maximum blank wall area for street-facing facades is 20 linear feet.

(c) Off-street parking setback. Off-street parking is prohibited between the street and street-facing building facade.

(d) On-site open space.

(1) In general.

(A) A minimum 17,000 cumulative square feet must be provided at grade as on-site open space.

(B) Each on-site open space must be a minimum of 2,000 contiguous square feet and contain a minimum 30 percent general planting areas as defined in Part I.

(C) On-site open space may contain paths, benches, water features, public art, open shelters, stairs, and elevators.

(D) Except for emergency vehicles, on-site open space may not be parked or driven upon.

(2) Public access pathways. Public access pathways must be provided to connect the sidewalk and the on-site open space. Each pathway must provide a line of sight connection and a pervious or impervious walkway between the sidewalk and open space and must be a minimum of 10 feet wide.

(A) Along Bookhout Street, a minimum of two public access pathways are required.

(B) Along Cedar Springs Road, a minimum of three public access pathways are required.

(C) Along Maple Avenue, a minimum of one public access pathway is required.

(e) Sidewalks. A minimum 10-foot wide unobstructed sidewalk is required on Maple Avenue. A minimum eight-foot wide unobstructed sidewalk is required on Bookhout Street and Cedar Springs Road.

(f) Pedestrian lighting. Public access pathways and sidewalks required in Subsections
(d) and (e) must provide free-standing or wall-mounted pedestrian lighting at a minimum ratio of one per 75 linear feet.

(g) Sidewalk crossings. Where a sidewalk crosses a driveway, the sidewalk must be constructed of a material, texture, or color that contrasts to the material, texture, or color of the driveway.

(h) Structured parking. Above-ground structured parking is prohibited.

(i) Transparency.

(1) Except on Bookhout Street, minimum ground story transparency for all street-facing and open space-facing facades is 50 percent. On Bookhout Street, minimum ground story transparency is 40 percent.

(2) Minimum upper story transparency for street-facing facades is 20 percent.

(j) Vehicular maneuvering setback. Except for required fire lanes, entry court, service and loading areas shown on the development plan, and garage access drives, areas used for vehicular maneuvering is prohibited within 50 feet of the right-of-way. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Additional Provisions
146.text:
SEC. S-146.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31087)

146.title: Compliance With Conditions
146.text:
SEC. S-146.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31087)

147.title: Legislative History
147.text:
SEC. S-147.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 147 was established by Ordinance No. 31169, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 10, 2019. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Property Location And Size
147.text:
SEC. S-147.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 147 is established on property located at the west corner of Turtle Creek Boulevard and Dickason Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 147 is 2.473 acres. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Definitions And Interpretations
147.text:
SEC. S-147.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division,

(1) BLANK WALL AREA means any portion of the exterior of a building that does not include a material change, windows, doors, columns, pilasters, or other articulation greater than 12 inches in depth. Blank wall area is measured horizontally on each story.

(2) GREEN ROOF means a roof assembly which consists of a waterproofing membrane, growing medium, and vegetation.

(3) OPEN SPACE means the portion of a building site that is principally open to the sky but allows for architectural elements. Open space must be a contiguous open area of not less than 10 feet in width or length and reserved for active or passive recreation, green roofs, or landscaping.

(4) SPECIAL HOTEL PROJECT means a development having:

(i) a hotel and motel use occupying a minimum of 40 percent of the total floor area;

(ii) a residential use occupying a minimum of 15 percent of the total floor area; and

(iii) any combination of recreation and entertainment uses; bar and restaurant uses; professional, personal service, and custom craft uses; and retail uses occupying a minimum of five percent of the total floor area.

(5) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(6) TANDEM PARKING means one parking space in front of another parking space, making it necessary to pass through one parking space to gain vehicular access to the other parking space.

(7) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window and door openings filled with glass, or openings in a parking garage facade, expressed as a percentage of the total facade area by story.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Exhibits
147.text:
SEC. S-147.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-147A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-147B: landscape plan. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Development Plan
147.text:
SEC. S-147.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a special hotel project, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-147A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Main Uses Permitted
147.text:
SEC. S-147.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the O-2 Office Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the O-2 Office Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the O-2 Office Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the O-2 Office Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) When located within a special hotel project, the following main uses are also permitted:

-- Health studio. -- Restaurant without drive-in or drive-through service. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Accessory Uses
147.text:
SEC. S-147.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
147.text:
SEC. S-147.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the O-2 Office Subdistrict apply.

(b) Increased development standards. For a special hotel project that complies with the provisions of S-147.113, the following modifications to the O-2 Office Subdistrict apply.

(1) Side and rear yard.

(A) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum side and rear yard is 10 feet.

(B) For portions of a nonresidential structure that exceed 36 feet in height and do not contain residential uses or a hotel or motel use for a minimum 40 feet of depth from the side or rear property line, minimum side and rear yard is one-half the overall height of that portion of the building, up to a maximum total setback of 50 feet. The additional setback is only required for that portion of a building that exceeds 36 feet in height.

(2) Density.

(A) For a multiple family use, maximum number of dwelling units is 85.

(B) For a hotel and motel use, maximum number of guest rooms is 180.

(3) Floor area ratio.

(A) Maximum floor area ratio is 4.75:1.

(B) When the total floor area of residential uses on a lot is equal to or greater than the lot area, maximum floor area ratio may be increased by 0.5.

(4) Height.

(A) Except as provided in this section, maximum structure height is 150 feet.

(B) Maximum structure height is 325 feet for portions of a building with a maximum floor plate of 28,386 square feet.

(C) Mechanical equipment and penthouses and visual screens that surround roof-mounted mechanical equipment may project up to eight feet above the maximum structure height.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 60 percent. Surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
147.text:
SEC. S-147.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Special hotel project.

(1) Parking spaces are not required to be shown on the development plan.

(2) Tandem parking is permitted for up to 100 percent of the required parking for a hotel or motel and multiple-family uses provided a valet license is obtained from the City of Dallas.

(3) All required loading spaces must be located within a structure.

(c) Service drives. Service drives are prohibited along Gillespie Street. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Environmental Performance Standards
147.text:
SEC. S-147.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Landscaping
147.text:
SEC. S-147.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) Special hotel project.

(1) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S- 147B).

(2) Street trees must be spaced a minimum of 20 feet and maximum of 30 feet on center. Spacing may be adjusted to accommodate visibility triangles, fire safety requirements, or existing trees to be preserved.

(3) Tree species may be singular or varied.

(4) Trees may not be located within a utility easement.

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Signs
147.text:
SEC. S-147.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31169)

147.title: Urban Design Standards For A Special
147.text:
SEC. S-147.113. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS FOR A SPECIAL HOTEL PROJECT.

(a) Public realm design.

(1) Sidewalks.

(A) Sidewalks must be a minimum width of six feet.

(B) Sidewalk materials must be constructed of enhanced concrete, concrete pavers, or stone materials, as approved by the director.

(C) The sidewalk edge must be located a minimum of three feet and a maximum of five feet from the back of the projected street curb.

(D) Sidewalks must be constructed at a continuous level across all driveways.

(2) Lighting.

(A) Pedestrian lighting must be provided at regular intervals consistent

with street tree locations along Dickason Avenue to enhance pedestrian safety on sidewalks, streets, walkways, and plazas to enhance pedestrian safety. Pedestrian light fixtures must be spaced no more than 100 feet apart. Spacing may be adjusted to achieve optimal photometric performance with a minimum of 0.5-foot candles between fixtures.

(B) Lighting must have illumination cut-offs.

(b) Architectural elements.

(1) Ground-level, street-facing facades must provide a minimum of 60 percent transparency.

(2) Maximum blank wall area for street-facing, ground-story building facades within 100 feet of a street is 20 feet.

(c) Bicycle parking. The provisions of Division 51A-4.330 regarding bicycle parking apply.

(d) Mechanical equipment. All utility boxes, generators, and other mechanical equipment must be located out of view from the street. When conditions do not permit compliance with this provision, equipment must be screened from view by a minimum six-foot-tall solid screening structure, building element, or landscaping elements such as shrubs, bushes, and trees.

(e) Open space.

(1) A minimum of 30 percent of the building site must be reserved as open space.

(2) A minimum of 20 percent of building roofs must be green roofs.

(3) The following structures are the only structures permitted within the open space: architectural elements, playground equipment, fountains, outdoor decks and terraces, roof terraces including pool amenities, publicly accessible outdoor balconies or terraces, temporary tents within the function lawn area shown on the development plan, trellises, pergolas, bridges, and signs.

(4) Open space may contain landscaping, water, natural elements, benches, walks, and green roofs.

(5) Private balconies, sidewalks, parking spaces, parking lots, drive aisles, and areas primarily intended for vehicular use are not considered open space and do not count towards the open space requirement.

(f) Structured parking. Above-ground structured parking is prohibited. (Ord. 31169)

SEC. S-147.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31169)

SEC. S-147.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31169)

148.title: Legislative History
148.text:
SEC. S-148.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 148 was established by Ordinance No. 31202, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 8, 2019. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Property Location And Size
148.text:
SEC. S-148.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 148 is established on property located north of Fitzhugh Avenue, west of Buena Vista Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 148 is 0.677 acres. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Definitions And Interpretations
148.text:
SEC. S-148.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) BREEZEWAY means an unenclosed passage connecting two buildings or portions of a building, or an open-air passageway through a building that is unenclosed on two sides.

(2) OPEN SPACE means a contiguous open area of not less than 10 feet in width or length that is principally open to the sky but allows for architectural elements such as trellises, colonnades, pergolas, building overhangs above 30 feet, and gazebos.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Exhibits
148.text:
SEC. S-148.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-148A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-148B: landscape plan. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Development Plan
148.text:
SEC. S-148.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S- 148A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, text of this division controls. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Main Uses Permitted
148.text:
SEC. S-148.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Residential uses.

-- Multiple family.

(2) Utility and service uses.

-- Local utilities.

(3) Transportation uses.

None permitted.

(4) Community service uses.

-- Post office.

(5) Medical uses.

-- Medical or scientific laboratory. -- Optical shop. -- Medical appliance fitting and sales.

(6) Religious uses.

None permitted.

(7) Educational uses.

-- Library, art gallery, or museum.

(8) Recreation and entertainment uses.

-- Public park or playground.

-- Game court center. -- Private recreation club or area.

(9) Bar and restaurant uses.

-- Bar, lounge, or tavern. [May only operate between 6:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Monday through Sunday] -- Restaurant without drive-in service. -- Private-club. -- Catering service.

(10) Professional, personal service, and custom crafts uses.

-- Office. -- Temporary construction or sales office. -- Bank or savings and loan office. [RAR] -- Barber and beauty shop. -- Health studio. -- Laundry or cleaning pickup and receiving station. -- Key shop. -- Shoe repair. -- Tailor, custom sewing, and millinery. -- Travel bureau. -- Broadcasting or recording studio. -- Instructional arts studio. -- Handcrafted art work studio. -- Handcrafted bookbinding. -- Photography studio. -- Safe deposit boxes.

(11) Retail uses.

-- Retail stores other than listed. -- Antique shop. -- Retail food store. -- Bakery or confectionery shop. -- Book and stationery store. -- Camera shop. -- Clothing store. -- Florist store. -- Feed store. -- Pet shop. -- Furniture store. -- Hardware or sporting goods store.

(12) Motor vehicle related uses.

-- Commercial parking lot or garage

(13) Commercial uses.

-- Garden shop, plant sales, or greenhouse. -- Diamond and precious stone sales.

(14) Storage and waste disposal uses.

-- Recycling drop-off container.

(15) Animal related uses.

-- Veterinarian’s office. -- Animal clinic without outside runs.

(b) Nonresidential uses are not permitted above the second story. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Accessory Uses
148.text:
SEC. S-148.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(b) The following additional accessory uses are permitted:

-- Swimming pool (private). -- Home occupation. -- Occasional sales (garage sales). -- Community center (private). (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
148.text:
SEC. S-148.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(2) For purposes of yard, lot, and space regulations, the subdistrict is considered one lot.

(b) Front yard.

(1) Fitzhugh Avenue.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(B) For a maximum of 15 percent of the total facade area above 36 feet in height, minimum front yard is five feet.

(C) For a maximum of five percent of the total facade area, no minimum front yard.

(2) Buena Vista Street.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, for portions of a building 36 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet. No minimum front yard is required within 50 feet of Fitzhugh Avenue.

(B) For portions of the building above 36 feet in height:

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(ii) For a maximum of 60 percent of the total facade area above 36 feet in height, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(iii) For a maximum of 20 percent of the total facade area above 36 feet in height, no minimum front yard.

(3) Corner clip. No setback is required from the corner clip at the intersection of Fitzhugh Avenue and Buena Vista Street.

(4) Encroachments.

(A) When less than 12 feet in height above average grade, bollards, stairs, hand rails, ramps, utility equipment, retaining/landscape walls, bicycle racks, guardrails, fountains, raised patio/seating areas, raised patio areas, fixed raised planters, and seat walls are permitted in a front yard.

(B) Benches, tables, chairs, and patio furniture are permitted in a front yard.

(c) Side and rear yard.

(1) Katy Trail.

(A) For portions of a building 36 feet in height or less, minimum side yard is 15 feet.

(B) Except as provided in this paragraph, for portions of a building above 36 feet height, minimum side yard is 35 feet.

(i) For a maximum of 10 percent of the total facade area above 36 feet in height, minimum side yard is 15 feet.

(ii) For a maximum of 60 percent of the total facade area above 36 feet in height, minimum side yard is 25 feet.

(2) Northeast boundary.

(A) Minimum side yard for portions of a building 36 feet or less in height is 45 feet.

(B) For portions of a building that exceed 36 feet in height, minimum side yard is 35 feet.

(3) Encroachments.

(A) When less than 12 feet in height above average grade, fixed raised planters, seat walls, stairs, ramps, bicycle racks, retaining walls, steps, handrails, safety railings, utility equipment, landscape planters, tree planters, sculptures, guardrails, fountains, raised patio/seating areas, raised patio areas, and other decorative landscape features are permitted in a required side yard.

(B) Benches, tables, chairs, and patio furniture are permitted in a required side yard.

(C) When less than 22 feet in height above grade, landscape trellises that are 50 percent or more open are permitted in a required side or rear yard.

(d) Floor area ratio.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum floor area ratio is 2.0:1.

(2) An additional 1.1:1 floor area ratio bonus applies when a minimum of 6,200 square feet is reserved for open space as shown on the development plan and the provisions of Section S-148.113 are met.

(3) An additional 0.5:1 floor area ratio bonus applies when the total floor area of residential uses exceeds the lot area.

(4) Private residential balconies and breezeways are excluded as floor area for the purpose of calculating floor area ratio.

(e) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 120 feet.

(2) Elevator penthouse, roof-mounted mechanical equipment, and screening may exceed the maximum structure height by 12 feet. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
148.text:
SEC. S-148.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off- street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Off-street loading spaces within this subdistrict may be shared by uses located anywhere within the subdistrict.

(c) All required off-street loading spaces must be enclosed within a building.

(d) Bicycle parking spaces must be provided in accordance with Division 51A-4.330.

(e) Off-street parking reductions are available for providing bicycle parking. See Section 51A-4.314. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Environmental Performance Standards
148.text:
SEC. S-148.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Landscaping
148.text:
SEC. S-148.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-148B).

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Signs
148.text:
SEC. S-148.112. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Urban Design Standards
148.text:
SEC. S-148.113. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS.

The following conditions must be met in order to qualify for the floor area ratio bonus in Section S-148.108(d)(2).

(1) Pedestrian amenities. Frontages on Buena Vista Street and Fitzhugh Avenue must provide the following pedestrian amenities:

(A) A minimum of one bench, bicycle rack, and trash receptacle per 300 feet of frontage.

(B) Sidewalks that cross vehicular driveways must be constructed with a material, pattern, or color that contrasts with the driveway.

(C) Except for visibility triangles, vehicular drives, and restrictions due to existing utilities, a minimum of one freestanding pedestrian street lamp, bollard, or sidewalk light must be provided for every 60 feet of street frontage.

(2) Building entrances. A minimum of one of the following must be provided on building facades at all pedestrian street entry points:

(A) Architecturally prominent public entrance.

(B) Architecturally prominent open staircase with five-foot minimum clearance.

(C) Enhanced landscape feature, such as a raised planter.

(D) Landscape trellis or overhang.

(3) Building facades. At least one of the following elements must be provided on each facade of the building:

(A) Architecturally prominent features, such as arches, on the ground floor.

(B) A minimum of 40 percent of the building cladding materials must be natural materials, such as masonry, brick, stone, or wood.

(C) Deep set windows of a minimum four-inch depth.

(4) Open space.

(A) Americans with Disabilities Act-compliant and bike-friendly public access to the Katy Trail from Buena Vista Street must be provided and maintained through the open space area with a minimum width of 10 feet, as shown on the development plan.

(B) A minimum of 6,200 square feet of open space must be provided.

(C) A minimum of two of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided

within the open space area:

(i) Benches.

(ii) Bicycle racks.

(iii) Water fountains.

(iv) Trash receptacles.

(5) Breezeway. A breezeway must be provided as shown on the development plan to connect Buena Vista Street to the Katy Trail for pedestrian access. A minimum of one of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided within the breezeway area:

(i) Benches.

(ii) Enhanced paving material, such as brick/masonry, stone, decorative concrete, or tile.

(iii) Architecturally prominent public entrances.

(6) Structured parking. Above-ground structured parking is prohibited. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Additional Provisions
148.text:
SEC. S-148.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31202)

148.title: Compliance With Conditions
148.text:
SEC. S-148.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31202)

149.text:

PD Subdistrict 149 was established by Ordinance No. 31199, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 8, 2019. (Ord. 31199)

PD Subdistrict 149 is established on property located at the north corner of Cedar Springs Road and Maple Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 149 is 1.0 acres. (Ord. 31199)

150.title: Legislative History
150.text:
SEC. S-150.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 150 was established by Ordinance No. 31297, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 28, 2019. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Property Location And Size
150.text:
SEC. S-150.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 150 is established on property generally located at the south corner of Olive Street and Cedar Springs Road. The size of PD Subdistrict 150 is approximately 0.525 acres. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Definitions And Interpretations
150.text:
SEC. S-150.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division,

(1) BLANK WALL AREA means any portion of the exterior of a building that does not include a material change; windows or doors; or columns, pilasters, or other articulations greater than 12 inches in depth. Blank wall area is measured horizontally on each story.

(2) FACADE means any separate face of a building, including parapet walls and omitted wall lines, or any part of a building which encloses or covers usable space. Where separate facades are oriented in one direction, or in directions within 45 degrees of one another, they are to be considered as part of a single facade.

(3) GROUND-LEVEL means the level of a building closest to, adjacent to, and above the street.

(4) PEDESTRIAN OPEN SPACE means a pedestrian area, facility, or feature that is located on the Property, outside of the public right-of-way, and that is publicly accessible and privately maintained. Examples include but are not limited to green space, public art, hardscape, and seating areas. Pedestrian open space may be located beneath a cantilevered portion of a building.

(5) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(6) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window and door openings filled with glass, expressed as a percentage of facade area.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Exhibits
150.text:
SEC. S-150.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-150A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-150B: landscape plan. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Development Plan
150.text:
SEC. S-150.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a hotel and motel use, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-150A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Main Uses Permitted
150.text:
SEC. S-150.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Accessory Uses
150.text:
SEC. S-150.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(b) For a hotel and motel use, a minimum of 800 square feet of accessory restaurant or retail uses must be located in the ground-level of the building.

(c) For a hotel and motel use, the following accessory uses may not have exterior advertising or signs:

(1) Restaurant.

(2) Meeting rooms.

(d) Ground-level accessory uses must have direct access to the sidewalk along a pedestrian path and may include areas for outdoor dining and gathering. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
150.text:
SEC. S-150.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Hotel and motel use.

(1) Front yard.

(A) Olive Street.

(i) Except as provided in this subparagraph, for any portion of a building 20 feet above grade and below, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) A portion of an underground parking structure may be located in the front yard and above grade and must be concealed by a combination of landscaping or screening wall with planting materials. Ground-level transparency is not required for the portion of the underground parking structure that is located above the street.

(iii) Retaining walls, planters, railings, access ramps, outdoor dining areas, enhanced paving, canopies, balconies, and architectural elements may be located within the required front yard.

(B) Cedar Springs Road.

(i) Minimum front yard is 17.5 feet.

(ii) Retaining walls, planters, railings, access ramps, outdoor dining areas, enhanced paving, canopies, balconies, and architectural elements may be located within the required front yard.

(2) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent. Surface parking lots, underground parking, and portions of predominantly underground parking structures are not included in lot coverage calculations.

(3) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 7.1:1. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
150.text:
SEC. S-150.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Hotel and motel use.

(1) Required parking for a hotel and motel use is 0.5 space per guest room. No additional parking is required for accessory uses such as restaurants, retail, and meeting rooms.

(2) Except for a portion of an underground parking structure projecting above grade, above-ground parking structures are prohibited. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Environmental Performance Standards
150.text:
SEC. S-150.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Landscaping
150.text:
SEC. S-150.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Hotel and motel use.

(1) Landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S- 150B).

(2) Minimum landscape site area is 25 percent of the lot area.

(3) Minimum general planting area is 35 percent of the minimum landscape site area.

(4) Minimum special planting area is 50 percent of the minimum general planting area.

(5) The building official may approve minor deviations in tree planting locations at time of building permit due to utility or driveway conflicts.

(6) A 1.5-foot vertical landscape buffer is required between the sidewalk and the vehicular drop-off area along Cedar Springs Road as shown on the landscape plan.

(7) Required trees must have a minimum trunk caliper at planting of five inches measured at a point 12 inches above the root ball.

(8) A landscape buffer is not required between a predominantly underground parking structure and adjacent uses or streets. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Urban Design Standards For Hotel And Motel
150.text:
SEC. S-150.112. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS FOR HOTEL AND MOTEL USE.

(a) Transparency.

(1) Ground-level.

(A) Street-facing facades, other than a portion of an underground parking structure that is partially located above the street, must have a minimum transparency of 70 percent for that portion of the building on the ground-level between grade and 12 feet in height.

(B) A minimum of 60 percent of the required minimum transparency must allow views into the ground-level use to a minimum depth of four feet. Windows must be clear or unpainted, or, if treated, must be transparent or translucent. Spandrel glass and backpainted glass are not considered transparent for purposes of this requirement.

(2) Above ground-level.

All street-facing facades above ground-level must have a minimum combined transparency of 50 percent.

(b) Glass. For the areas of the facade utilizing glass, only spandrel, non-vision glass is allowed where indicated on the development plan.

(c) Blank wall area.

(1) Blank wall areas located on street-facing facades may not exceed 30 feet in length.

(2) A minimum of two different facade materials must be provided on each street-facing facade.

(d) Architectural elements. A minimum of one of the following architectural elements must be provided at each public entry point:

(1) Canopies.

(2) Awnings.

(3) Attached towers.

(4) Turrets.

(5) Porte cocheres.

(6) Similar architectural features intended to accentuate the building entrance.

(e) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical and related equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as not to be visible from any public right-of-way.

(f) Utility boxes. All electrical and utility boxes at the ground-level must be screened and located away from public view.

(g) Outdoor seating. Outdoor seating is required along Olive Street in the area designated on the development plan.

(h) Pedestrian open space. A minimum of 3,800 square feet of contiguous pedestrian open space is required.

(i) Screening of off-street loading and garbage areas. Screening of off-street loading and garbage areas is required and must consist of masonry, evergreen plantings, extended building walls, or a combination of those materials. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Sidewalks And Pedestrian Amenities For Hotel
150.text:
SEC. S-150.113. SIDEWALKS AND PEDESTRIAN AMENITIES FOR HOTEL AND MOTEL USE.

(a) Sidewalks.

(1) Sidewalks must be provided at a minimum width of six feet and must be located outside a five-foot-wide landscape buffer measured from the back of the street curb.

(2) Tree wells may be located along the street frontages of the Property but may not be located in visibility triangles.

(3) Sidewalk materials must change and be distinguished by color or texture from intersecting driveways.

(4) Sidewalks must remain level across all driveways.

(b) Pedestrian amenities.

(1) A minimum of one of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along the Cedar Springs Road and Olive Street frontages:

(A) Bench.

(B) Trash and recycling receptacle.

(C) Bicycle rack.

(2) One pedestrian street lamp is required for every 50 feet along sidewalks. The building official may approve minor deviations in street lamp locations at time of building permit due to utility, tree, planting, or driveway conflicts. Pedestrian street lamps may not be located in visibility triangles. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Signs
150.text:
SEC. S-150.114. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Additional Provisions
150.text:
SEC. S-150.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31297)

150.title: Compliance With Conditions
150.text:
SEC. S-150.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.
(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31297)

151.title: Legislative History
151.text:
SEC. S-151.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 151 was established by Ordinance No. 31438, passed by the Dallas City Council on January 22, 2020. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Property Location And Size
151.text:
SEC. S-151.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 151 is established on property located at the west corner of Lemmon Avenue and Oak Lawn Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 151 is approximately 2.2 acres. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Definitions And Interpretations
151.text:
SEC. S-151.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Exhibits
151.text:
SEC. S-151.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-151A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-151B: landscape plan. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Development Plan
151.text:
SEC. S-151.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply.

(b) For a project to qualify for the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d)(2) and height in Section S-151.108(e)(2), development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-151A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Main Uses Permitted
151.text:
SEC. S-151.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Accessory Uses
151.text:
SEC. S-151.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
151.text:
SEC. S-151.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(2) For purposes of yard, lot, and space regulations, the subdistrict is considered one lot. No additional setbacks applicable to the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(b) Front yard. For a structure to qualify for the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d) and height in Section S-151.108(e), the following setbacks apply:

(1) Oak Lawn Avenue.

(A) For the first 30 feet of structure height, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(B) For any portion of a structure above 30 feet in height, minimum front yard is 50 feet.

(2) Lemmon Avenue.

(A) For the first 58 feet of structure height, minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(B) For any portion of the structure above 58 feet in height, minimum front yard is shown on the development plan.

(c) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is 10 feet.

(d) Floor area ratio.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum floor area ratio is 2.5:1.

(2) When the provisions of Sections S-151.105(b), S-151.108(b), S-151.111(a), S-151.113, and S-151.114 are met, maximum floor area ratio is 3.9:1, and the Property is considered one lot for purposes of floor area ratio.

(e) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 120 feet.

(2) When the provisions of Sections S-151.105(b), S-151.108(b), S-151.111(a), S-151.113, and S-151.114 are met, maximum structure height is 175 feet.

(3) The following structures may project a maximum of 10 feet above the maximum structure height:

(A) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(B) Mechanical equipment room.

(C) Visual screens which surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(D) Parapet wall, limited to a height of four feet. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
151.text:
SEC. S-151.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off- street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) This district is considered one lot for purposes of required off-street parking and loading. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Environmental Performance Standards
151.text:
SEC. S-151.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Landscaping
151.text:
SEC. S-151.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) For a project to qualify for the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d)(2) and height in Section S-151.108(e)(2), landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-151B). Otherwise, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Signs
151.text:
SEC. S-151.112. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) One additional attached premise sign is permitted along the facade facing Oak Lawn Avenue subject to the following restrictions:

(1) The sign must be two-sided and display a message on both sides of the sign.

(2) The maximum effective area is 120 square feet per side.

(3) The sign may project up to five feet from the building facade at an angle other than parallel from the vertical plane.

(4) Letters must exceed four inches in height.

(5) No portion of the sign may be located more than 65 feet above grade or project above any roof. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Urban Design Standards
151.text:
SEC. S-151.113. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Applicability. For a project to qualify for the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d)(2) and height in Section S-151.108(e)(2), it must comply with all requirements in this section. If the increased development standards are not applied, the provisions of this section do not apply.

(b) Public realm design.

(1) Sidewalks.

(A) On Oak Lawn Avenue, a sidewalk with a minimum unobstructed clear zone width of eight feet must be provided. An additional minimum landscape buffer of five feet must be provided between the back of curb and the sidewalk.

(B) On Lemmon Avenue, a sidewalk with a minimum unobstructed clear zone of six feet must be provided. An additional minimum landscape buffer of three feet must be provided between the back of curb and sidewalk.

(C) Sidewalks must be constructed of concrete pavers or finished concrete surfaces.

(D) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and be designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk.

(E) If a portion of a sidewalk is located on private property, the property owner must dedicate a sidewalk easement to the city to assure its availability to the public as a permanent pedestrian way.

(2) Pedestrian amenities.

(A) A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along street-facing facades, with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives, in order to promote pedestrian activity and safety:

(i) Benches.

(ii) Bicycle racks.

(iii) Trash receptacles.

(B) Pedestrian amenities may be located within the landscape buffer zone but must not obstruct the required sidewalk clear zone.

(3) Street trees. Street trees must be provided within the landscape buffer zone and must be spaced 30 feet on center, unless the director determines an interference with overhead or underground utilities or other subsurface conditions exists.

(4) Mechanical equipment. Aboveground utility boxes, generators, and other large mechanical equipment must be located out of view from the public right-of-way. When conditions do not permit mechanical equipment to be located so as not to be seen from public right-

of-way, equipment must be screened from view by a building element or solid wood or masonry fence or wall at least six feet in height and screened with landscaping such as shrubs, bushes, and trees.

(5) Lighting.

(A) Except as provided in this subparagraph, lighting must be spaced 75 to 100 feet apart, with the center of the foundation two to three feet from the back of curb, with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives, in order to provide lighting on sidewalks, streets, walkways, and plazas to enhance pedestrian safety. Spacing may be adjusted to achieve optimal photometric performance of a minimum of 0.5 footcandles between fixtures.

(B) Lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent properties.

(C) The property owner is responsible for the cost of installation, operation, and maintenance of the lighting.

(c) Architectural elements.

(1) Enhanced architectural elements, such as the following, must be provided at all building corners and at public entry points: architecturally prominent public entrances, canopies, awnings, variations in building massing, increased transparency, and variations in fenestration.

(2) The ground-level of a building must provide a minimum of 40 percent transparency for all street-facing facades located within the first 20 feet of the building.

(3) Variations in facade plane must be provided. Variations may include wall recesses and projections, bays, offsets, reveals. Facade articulation of one foot in depth must be provided for every 100 feet of facade length on all street-facing facades.

(d) Service and loading.

(1) Service entries and back-of-house functions must be located away from primary facades and must be visually screened with landscaping such as shrubs, bushes, and trees.

(2) Loading areas and loading docks must:

(A) be located away from primary street facades and pedestrian routes; and

(B) provide a closable gate or door that can block the loading area from the sidewalk during times when it is not in use.

(e) Parking.

(1) Surface parking. Except where shown on the development plan, surface parking is prohibited between the street-facing facade and the Property line. For buildings with more than two street frontages, only two street frontages are subject to this requirement.

(2) Parking structures.

(A) The portion of the ground-level floor facing the street of any multi- floor aboveground parking structure must have an active use other than parking to a minimum depth of 25 feet, or must have an exterior facade that is compatible to the facade of the main structure.

(B) Exterior parking structure facade non-entry openings must provide solid screening for a minimum of 42 inches above the floor level within the parking structure to screen vehicles and vehicle headlights. Screening may include architectural grill work or other materials that provide ventilation. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Mixed Income Housing
151.text:
SEC. S-151.114. MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A-4.1100 is required to obtain the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d) and increased height in Section S-151.108(e).

(b) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required.

(c) Compliance with Section 20A-27(g) is not required.

(d) During the rental affordability period, for any multifamily use that depends on the increased floor area ratio in Section S-151.108(d) and increased height in Section S-151.108(e), five percent of the total residential rental units must be made available for lease at an affordable rent (as defined in Section 20A-24) with an income band of 61 percent to 80 percent of adjusted median family income and three percent of the total residential rental units must be made available for lease at an affordable rent (as defined in Section 20A-24) with an income band of 101 percent to 120 percent of adjusted median family income. The mixed-income restrictive covenant in Section 20A-26 and the rental affordability period are for a term of 15 years. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Additional Provisions
151.text:
SEC. S-151.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31438)

151.title: Compliance With Conditions
151.text:
SEC. S-151.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31438)

152.title: Legislative History
152.text:

152.title: Creation Of Tracts
152.text:
SEC. S-152.105. CREATION OF TRACTS.

(a) This district is divided into two tracts: Tract I and II.

(b) The tracts may, but are not required to, correspond to platted lot lines. (Ord. 31421)

152.title: Conceptual Plan

SEC. S-152.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S- 152A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 31421)

152.title: Development Plan

SEC. S-152.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Tract I. Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-152B). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, text of this division controls.

(b) Tract II. A development plan, for all or a portion of Tract II, must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in Tract II that increases the existing building height, floor area ratio, or nonpermeable coverage of Tract II, unless the work is to restore a building that has been damaged or destroyed by fire, explosion, flood, tornado, riot, act of public enemy, or accident of any kind. If there is conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 31421)

152.title: Main Uses Permitted
152.text:
SEC. S-152.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 31421)

152.title: Accessory Uses
