163.title: Legislative History
163.text:
SEC. S-163.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

Planned Development Subdistrict 163 for LC Subdistrict uses within Planned Development District No. 193 (‘PD Subdistrict 163”) was established by Ordinance No. 31863, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 14, 2021. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Property Location And Size
163.text:
SEC. S-163.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 193 Subdistrict 163 is established on property bounded by McKinney Avenue and Boll Street. The size of PD 193 Subdistrict 163 is approximately 1.1197 acres. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Definitions And Interpretations
163.text:
SEC. S-163.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division,

(1) PRIVATE OPEN SPACE means an area that is unobstructed to the sky, except structures supporting outdoor activities, such as colonnades, pergolas, gazebos, shade structures, planters, a swimming pool, water features, seating areas, an outdoor kitchen, or similar improvements or fixtures.

(2) SPECIAL PROJECT means a development containing a combination of (i) multiple-family; and (ii) office, retail, professional, personal service, custom craft, and/or restaurant uses that satisfies the urban design requirements of this article in order to allow total floor area ratio greater than 4.5:1.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(4) TRANSPARENCY means that total area of window opening, door opening, or other opening, express as a percentage of the total facade area by story.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Exhibits
163.text:
SEC. S-163.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit 163A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit 163B: landscape plan.

(3) Exhibit 163C: height plan. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Development Plan
163.text:
SEC. S-163.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a special project, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-163A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Main Uses Permitted
163.text:
SEC. S-163.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit
(SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict, etc.

(b) For a special project, the following use is prohibited:

-- Bar, lounge, or tavern. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Accessory Uses
163.text:
SEC. S-163.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
163.text:
SEC. S-163.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Special project.

(1) Front yard.

(A) McKinney Avenue.

(i) For portions of a building 36 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of a building greater than 36 feet in height, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(iii) A maximum of 60 percent of the required front yard may be outside seating area.

(B) Boll Street.

(i) Minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) A maximum of 25 percent of the required front yard may be outside seating area.

(2) Side and rear yard.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, for portions of a building 36 feet in height or less, no minimum side or rear yard.

(B) Except as provided in this paragraph, for portions of a building greater than 36 feet in height, minimum side and rear yard is 10 feet.

(D) Along the alley perpendicular to Boll Street,

(i) for portions of a building 36 feet in height or less, minimum side yard is 10 feet.

(ii) for portions of a building over 36 feet in height and up to 47 feet in height, minimum side yard is 50 feet.

(iii) for portions of a building over 47 feet in height and up to 190 feet in height, minimum side yard is 75 feet.

(iv) for portions of a building greater than 190 feet in height, minimum side yard is 85 feet.

(3) Encroachments.

(A) Windowsills, belt courses, cornices, trellises, screens, awnings, balconies, roof eaves, canopies, and other architectural features may project up to five feet into the required minimum front, side, or rear yards. Any awnings, balconies, roof eaves or canopies must have a minimum clearance of eight feet above the sidewalk or finished grade (in the event a sidewalk is not required).

(B) Along McKinney Avenue and Boll Street, outside seating areas, retaining walls, signs, benches, landscaping, fences, planters, and related improvements are permitted within the required front yard.

(C) Any improvements allowed to encroach into the required front yard shall not obstruct the minimum sidewalk dimensions required in Section S-163.109(a).

(4) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 290.

(5) Floor area ratio.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum floor area ratio for all uses combined is 6.0:1.

(B) If the Property complies with Section S-163-114, maximum floor area ratio for all uses combined is 7.99:1.

(C) Land area that is located outside this subdistrict but is located within the same platted lot as land within this subdistrict is included for floor area ratio calculations.

(D) Maximum floor area for office uses above the ground story is 60,000 square feet.

(E) Maximum floor area for nonresidential uses within the ground story is 16,500 square feet.

(6) Height.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 240 feet.

(B) Maximum structure height in height zone A-2 shown on the height plan (Exhibit S-163C) is 190 feet.

(C) Maximum structure height in height zone B shown on the height plan is 47 feet.

(D) Maximum structure height in height zone C shown on the height plan is 36 feet.

(E) Maximum structure height in height zone D shown on the height plan is 36 feet.

(7) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(8) Lot size. No minimum lot size per dwelling unit.

(9) Floor plate. Maximum floor plate for the portion of a building greater than 47 feet in height is 26,000 square feet. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Urban Design Requirements For A Special
163.text:
SEC. S-163.109. URBAN DESIGN REQUIREMENTS FOR A SPECIAL PROJCT.

(a) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum eight-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required to be provided along Boll Street.

(2) A minimum 10-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk along is required to be provided along McKinney Avenue.

(3) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the rest of the sidewalk.

(b) Pedestrian lighting. Pedestrian street lamps are require along street frontages spaced between 45 feet and 60 feet with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives.

(c) Pedestrian amenities.

(1) A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along the McKinney Avenue frontage:

(A) Benches.

(B) Trash receptacles.

(C) Bicycle racks.

(2) One of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along the Boll Street frontage:

(A) Bench.

(B) Trash receptacle.

(C) Bicycle rack.

(D) Pet waste station.

(d) Architectural Elements. A minimum of one architectural element, such as but not limited to the following, must be provided at all public entry points:

(1) Architecturally prominent public entrances.

(2) Canopies.

(3) Awnings.

(4) Attached towers.

(5) Turrets.

(e) Ground level transparency.

(1) Facades facing McKinney Avenue. Ground level facades between grade and 13 feet above grade must have a minimum transparency of 50 percent.

(2) Facades facing Boll Street. Ground level facades between grade and 13 feet above grade must have a minimum transparency of 40 percent.

(3) Exception. This subsection does not apply to parking structures.

(f) Building articulation. Street-facing facades must provide articulation at a minimum depth of three feet at least once every 75 feet of facade length.

(g) Street level activating uses.

(1) A minimum of 10,000 square feet of floor area on the ground story of any building must contain one or a combination of the following uses:

(A) Restaurant.

(B) Retail.

(C) Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses.

(h) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical and related equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as to not be visible from adjacent public rights-of- way.

(i) Street lights along Boll Street. Street lights along Boll Street must be of a historical character and appearance that is compatible with the State Thomas Historic District and be approved by the historic preservation officer.

(j) Private open space. For a special project containing 100 or more dwelling units, a minimum of 2,500 square feet of private open space must be provided that is accessible to all residents of the building. Private open space may be located on top of a roof, on any floor of a building, or in the areas internal to the site at grade.

(k) Special provisions for residential uses.

(1) Amplified sound is prohibited.

(2) Outdoor lighting must be hooded or shielded to prevent the casting of light onto adjacent properties.

(3) Private outdoor amenity space for accessory office use may only be used for programmed events between 9:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
163.text:
SEC. S-163.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Special project.

(1) Except for surface parking spaces shown on the development plan, all required off-street parking must be located below grade.

(2) For retail, restaurant, professional, personal service, and custom craft uses, packed parking may count toward the off-street parking requirements.

(3) Valet parking drop-off and pick-up:

(A) must be located within the same building site as the special project; and

(B) may not occur within the surface parking area adjacent to Boll Street shown on the development plan.

(4) Two medium size off-street loading spaces are required and two small size off-street loading spaces are required. Loading spaces must be located within the building site of the special project and may not be located in the surface parking area adjacent to Boll Street shown on the development plan. The dimensions of the off-street loading spaces must comply with the requirements of Section 51P-193.115(b)(5) and (6). Loading may only occur between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Environmental Performance Standards
163.text:
SEC. S-163.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Landscaping
163.text:
SEC. S-163.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) For a special project, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S- 163B). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the landscape plan, the text of this division controls.

(c) Tree wells within the planting area must have a maximum spacing of 30 feet on center with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives.

(d) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Signs
163.text:
SEC. S-163.113. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signage attached to a facade facing Boll Street must be compatible with the State Thomas Historic District. Signage design, but not content, must be approved by the historic preservation officer. This signage does not need to be shown on a development plan or landscape plan. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Mixed Income Housing
163.text:
SEC. S-163.114. MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, as amended, is required to obtain the increased floor area ratio in Section S-163.108(b)(5)(B).

(b) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required.

(c) Compliance with Section 20A-27(g) is not required.

(d) During the rental affordability period, for any multifamily use that depends on the increased floor area ratio in Section S-163.108(b)(5)(B), three and five tenths percent of the total residential rental units must be made available for lease at an affordable rent, as defined in Section 20A-24 of the Dallas City Code, with an income band of 81 percent to 100 percent of adjusted median family income. The mixed-income restrictive covenant in Section 20A-26 and the rental affordability period are for a term of 20 years. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Driveway
163.text:
SEC. S-163.115. DRIVEWAY.

Prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy, the owner or developer shall design and install a driveway along the McKinney Avenue frontage aligned with the existing eastbound approach of Boll Street in the approximate location shown on the development plan. At the time of building permit, deviations in the location of the driveway may be approved by the building official as necessary such that a traffic signal pole and mast arm may be designed and installed to align with the proposed site driveway for the westbound approach of Boll Street. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Additional Provisions
163.text:
SEC. S-163.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31863)

163.title: Compliance With Conditions
163.text:
SEC. S-163.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been

full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of thy city. (Ord. 31863)

164.title: Legislative History
164.text:
SEC. S-164.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 164 was established by Ordinance No. 31954 passed by the Dallas City Council on August 11, 2021. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Property Location And Size
164.text:
SEC. S-164.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 164 is established on property located on the southwest line of Nowitzki Way between Houston Street and Field Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 164 is 10.8481 acres. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Definitions And Interpretations
164.text:
SEC. S-164.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division,

(1) GROUND LEVEL means the story of a building closest to and above grade along a public street or an internal street.

(2) INTERNAL STREET means a public or private street or a private drive that is designated as Street Type A or B on the conceptual plan.

(3) LARGE TREE means a tree species that typically attains a canopy height and canopy width of at least 50 feet at maturity or as classified by the director.

(4) LOW-IMPACT DEVELOPMENT means a development consisting of one or more uses permitted pursuant to Section S-164.107(e), each of which does not exceed 20,000 square feet in floor area or a structure height of 45 feet.

(5) MEDIUM TREE means a tree that typically attains a canopy height of at least 30 feet and a canopy width between 15 feet and 50 feet at maturity or as otherwise classified by the director.

(6) SUBAREA means a subarea designated as Subarea A, B, C, or D on the conceptual plan.

(7) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(8) TOWER means the portion of a building greater than 110 feet in height.

(9) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window opening, door opening, or other opening, expressed as a percentage of the total facade area by story.

(10) TREE CANOPY COVER means the amount of ground area directly beneath a tree’s crown to the drip line or the combined crowns of a stand of trees, measured in square feet.

(11) VITRINE means a minimum five-foot-deep cavity or display case with a transparent surface used for the display of art, merchandise, or other objects, and which is:

(i) embedded in the front facade of a building or structure; and

(ii) similar to or complimentary in appearance to the front facades of commercial spaces such as a retail storefront, office, or hotel lobby.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a non-residential zoning district. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Exhibits
164.text:
SEC. S-164.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-164A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit S-164B: height map – perpendicular to Houston Street.

(3) Exhibit S-164C: height map – non-perpendicular to Houston Street.

(4) Exhibit S-164D: streetscape standards. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Conceptual Plan
164.text:
SEC. S-164.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-164A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Changes to the location of the open space shown on the conceptual plan and the alignment, network, and types of streets and drives shown on the conceptual plan to accommodate open space (including but not limited to reconfiguration or relocation of open space) may be

approved by the city plan commission through the procedure for minor amendments in Section 51A-4.702(h); provided that the following requirements are met:

(1) the amount of open space provided does not decrease below one-and-a-half acres;

(2) the minimum one-and-a-half acres of open space is concentrated in one contiguous area in either Subarea A or Subarea C;

(3) internal street Type A – Segment 1 as shown on the conceptual plan does not change alignment; and

(4) the minimum one-and-a-half acres of open space must remain generally centralized. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Development Plan
Main Uses Permitted
164.text:
SEC. S-164.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the CA-1 Central Area Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the CA-1 Central Area Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the CA-1 Central Area Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the CA-1 Central Area Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) The following uses are prohibited within this subdistrict:

-- Airport or landing field. -- Auto auction. -- Auto painting or body rebuilding shop (inside). -- Auto painting or body rebuilding shop (outside). -- Auto repair garage (inside). -- Auto repair garage (outside). -- Automobile or motorcycle display, sales and service (inside display). -- Automobile or motorcycle display, sales and service (outside display). -- Building repair and maintenance shop. -- Bus or truck repair/parking garage. -- Car wash. -- Clothing manufacturing. -- Commercial cleaning shop. -- Commercial laundry or dry cleaning. -- Custom print shop. -- Drag strip, go-cart tract, or commercial racing. -- Engine or motor repair shop. -- Fairgrounds. -- Gummed label printing. -- Job printing, lithographer, printing or blueprinting plant. -- Labor hall.

-- Light fabrication and assembly. -- Lumber, brick or building materials sales yard. -- Machine or welding shop. -- Machinery sales and services. -- Manufacturing laboratory. -- Motor freight hauling and storage. -- Outside commercial amusement. -- Passenger bus station and terminal. -- Pawn shop. -- Plumbing, electrical, air conditioning, and heating shops. -- Railroad freight terminal. -- Railroad team track. -- Rodeo. -- Sewage pumping station. -- Sewage treatment plant. -- Steam cleaning of vehicles and machinery. -- STOL (short takeoff or landing) port. -- Taxidermist. -- Tool and equipment rental (with outside display). -- Venetian blind or window shade repair, assembly and sales. -- Warehouse. -- Water reservoir, well, or pumping station. -- Water treatment plant.

(c) A bar, lounge, or tavern use is only allowed if located within the same building as an office, hotel and motel, or multiple-family use.

(d) The following uses are only allowed by specific use permit:

-- Drive-in restaurant. -- Drive-through restaurant. -- Service station.

(e) The following are the only uses permitted as part of a low-impact development:

Educational uses.

-- Library, art gallery, or museum.

Bar and restaurant uses.

-- Drive-in restaurant. -- Restaurant without drive-through service.

Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses.

-- Office. -- Temporary construction or sales office. -- Bank or saving and loan office. -- Barber and beauty shop. -- Health studio. -- Laundry or cleaning pickup and receiving station. -- Tailor, custom sewing, and millinery. -- Instructional arts studio. -- Handcrafted artwork studio. -- Photography studio.

Retail uses.

-- Retail stores other than listed. -- Antique shop. -- Retail food store. -- Bakery or confectionary shop. -- Book and stationary store. -- Camera shop. -- Cigar, tobacco, and candy store. -- Clothing store. -- Drug store. -- Liquor store. -- Florist store. -- Pet shop. -- Furniture store. -- Hobby and art supplies store.

Motor vehicle related uses.

-- Surface parking. [Maximum coverage of 25 percent per subarea.] -- Commercial parking lot or garage. [Maximum coverage of 25 percent per subarea.] (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Accessory Uses
164.text:
SEC. S-164.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
164.text:
SEC. S-164.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the CA-1 Central Area Subdistrict apply.

(b) Front yard. For the Houston Street frontage in Subareas B and C:

(1) For portions of a building 30 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(2) For portions of a building between 30 feet and 110 feet in height, minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(3) If a tower is oriented perpendicular to Houston Street, for portions of a building above 110 feet in height, minimum front yard is 50 feet.

(4) If a tower is not oriented perpendicular to Houston Street, for portions of a building above 110 feet in height, minimum front yard is 60 feet in subarea B and 70 feet in subarea
C.

(c) Building proximity.

(1) Ground level separation for buildings fronting Houston Street. For any building with frontage on Houston Street, any portion of the building between grade and 110 feet in height must be at least 50 feet away from the ground-level of any other building with frontage on Houston Street.

(2) Building spacing.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, any portion of a building greater than 180 feet in height must be at least 75 feet away from any other portion of a building greater than 180 feet in height located within this subdistrict.

(B) For any building in Subareas B or C with frontage on Houston Street, any portion of a building greater than 110 feet in height must be at least 90 feet away from any other portion of a building greater than 110 feet in height with frontage on Houston Street within Subarea B or C.

(C) The average spacing between portions of buildings greater than 180 feet in height with frontage on Houston Street in Subareas B, C, and D must be a minimum of 100 feet.

(d) Floor area ratio.

(1) Maximum floor area ratio for all uses combined is 8.0:1.

(2) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum floor area ratio for any multiple-family use in a subarea is 7.0:1.

(A) The floor area ratio of any multiple-family use in a subarea may be increased to 8.0:1 if, after reaching the maximum floor area ratio of 7.0:1, any future development in any subarea within the district that includes a multiple-family use that complies with Section S- 164.114 and provides percentages of reserved units in accordance with the table below.

(B) The mixed-income housing requirements do not apply to any buildings constructed prior to the date that the floor area ratio on any subarea exceeds 7.0:1.

Type of building Percentage of units Buildings seven stories* or less Five percent of multifamily dwelling units in buildings seven stories* or less must be available to households earning 51 to 60 percent of the area median family income
(AMFI) for the Dallas TX HUD Metro FMR Area Buildings eight stories* or more Five percent of multifamily dwelling units in buildings eight stories* or more must be available to households earning 81 to 100 percent of the area median family income
(AMFI) for the Dallas TX HUD Metro FMR Area

*Levels of a parking structure are not included in the calculation of the number of stories.

(3) Maximum floor area ratio for uses approved as low-impact developments is 0.75:1 per subarea. The floor area ratio for low-impact developments is calculated on a subarea- by-subarea basis for purposes of determining compliance with this requirement.

(4) This subdistrict is considered one lot for purposes of total floor area ratio calculations.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, for any portion of a building 180 feet in height or greater, maximum lot coverage is 40 percent per subarea. Lot coverage is calculated on a subarea-by-subarea basis for purposes of determining compliance with this requirement.

(2) In Subarea C along Houston Street:

(A) except as provided in this paragraph, for any portion of a building 400 feet in height or greater, maximum lot coverage is 35 percent of Subarea C.

(B) for any portion of a building 630 feet in height or greater, maximum lot coverage is 30 percent of Subarea C.

(3) Maximum lot coverage for a surface parking lot and commercial parking lot or garage approved as low-impact development is 25 percent per subarea. Lot coverage is calculated on a subarea-by-subarea basis for purposes of determining compliance with this requirement. This lot coverage limitation only applies to low-impact developments and does not apply to parking areas shown on an approved development plan.

(4) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(f) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is any legal height.

(2) For buildings with frontage on Houston Street with towers that are oriented perpendicular to Houston Street:

(A) maximum structure height for height zone B as shown on the height map – perpendicular to Houston Street (Exhibit S-164B) is 110 feet.

(B) maximum structure height for height zone C as shown on the height map – perpendicular to Houston Street is 30 feet.

(3) For buildings with frontage on Houston Street with towers that are not perpendicular to Houston Street:

(A) maximum structure height for height zone B as shown on the height map – non-perpendicular to Houston Street (Exhibit S-164C) is 110 feet.

(B) maximum structure height for height zone C as shown on the height map – non-perpendicular to Houston Street is 30 feet.

(4) The maximum structure height of any parking structure within Subarea C fronting Houston Street is 110 feet. A building may be connected to and located above the parking structure without a height limitation. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Urban Design Requirements
164.text:
SEC. S-164.110. URBAN DESIGN REQUIREMENTS.

(a) Streets and sidewalks.

(1) Houston Street, Field Street, and Nowitzki Way.

(A) Houston Street, Field Street, and Nowitzki Way must comply with the streetscape standards (Exhibit S-164D). On Field Street there are two separate sections: one section (with a bike lane shown) applies north of internal street Type A – Segment 1, and the second section (without a bike lane shown) applies south of internal street Type A – Segment 1.

(B) Except as provided in this subsection, minimum unobstructed sidewalk width along Houston Street, Field Street, and Nowitzki Way is 10 feet.

(C) Minimum unobstructed sidewalk width along the portion of Houston Street north of internal street Type A – Segment 2 as shown on the conceptual plan is 12 feet.

(2) Internal streets.

(A) Except as provided in this subsection, internal streets must comply with the streetscape standards.

(B) Minimum unobstructed sidewalk width on internal streets is eight feet. Sidewalks located within the pedestrian zone shown on the streetscape standards.

(C) The vehicular zone shown on the streetscape standards may be widened to accommodate parallel parking. Head-in or perpendicular parking is not allowed on internal streets.

(D) The vehicular zone and one of the two pedestrian zones shown on the streetscape standards may be eliminated for internal street Type B – Segment 2, so long as a minimum eight feet unobstructed sidewalk is provided for internal street Type B – Segment 2.

(3) Former River Street (private street). The southern boundary of the subdistrict labeled as Former River Street (Private) on the conceptual plan must comply with the streetscape standards. Minimum unobstructed sidewalk width along former River Street is eight feet.

(4) Conflicts. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the streetscape standards, the text of this article controls.

(5) Sidewalks. Sidewalks must be level across all driveways, curb cuts, and entrances or exits to loading areas.

(6) Private streets. Private internal streets must be publicly accessible; however, private internal streets may be closed temporarily for special events up to a maximum of 48 hours for each special event. During special events, at least one ingress and egress point along Houston Street and at least one ingress and egress point along Field Street must remain open at all times.

(b) Pedestrian amenities.

(1) Public streets. The following pedestrian amenities must be provided at a quantity of at least one per every 100 feet of public street frontage, excluding frontage with visibility triangles or driveways:

(A) bench (minimum of 10 linear feet), and

(B) trash receptable.

(2) Internal streets. The following pedestrian amenities must be provided at a quantity of at least one per every 100 feet of internal street frontage, excluding frontage with visibility triangles or driveways:

(A) bench (minimum of 10 linear feet),

(B) trash receptacle, and

(C) bicycle rack.

(3) Benches. Benches may be concentrated or grouped at one or more central locations or focal points of a development, provided there must be at least one bench per each 250 feet of public and internal street frontage.

(4) Bicycle racks. Bicycle racks may be concentrated or grouped at one or more central locations or focal points of a development, provided there must be at least one bicycle rack per each 250 feet of internal street frontage.

(c) Architectural elements. At least one architectural element, such as the following, must be provided at all public entry points to a main building:

(1) Architecturally prominent public entrance;

(2) Canopy;

(3) Awning;

(4) Turret;

(5) Arcade;

(6) Portal;

(7) Cantilevered building above the entry point; or

(8) Similar architectural feature.

(d) Ground level transparency.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, any building facade fronting on a public street, internal street, or publicly accessible open space must have a minimum transparency of 40 percent for the portion of the building on the ground level between grade and 13 feet in height.

(2) This subsection does not apply to parking structures or loading areas.

(e) Building articulation. Street-facing facades must provide articulation with a minimum depth of two feet of variation within the vertical plane at least once every 100 feet of facade length.

(f) Minimum open space.

(1) No certificate of occupancy may be issued that would authorize the use of floor area that would cause the total floor area within this subdistrict to exceed 300,000 square feet until a minimum of one-and-a-half acres of contiguous open space has been provided within this subdistrict.

(2) Except as provided in this paragraph, a minimum of 70 percent of the one- and-a-half acres of contiguous open space area must be unobstructed to the sky. Area covered by trees or tree canopies are considered unobstructed to the sky. Open space may not have permanent structures except structures supporting pedestrian or outdoor recreational uses, including but not limited to shade structures, pavilions, seating, play equipment, gazebos, kiosks that provide information related to the open space, or security, audio-visual, or maintenance equipment.

(3) Paved areas (excluding traffic lanes or drive aisles), plazas, and planting areas within the one-and-a-half acres of contiguous open space may be counted as part of the open space area. A maximum of 50 percent of the one-and-a-half acres of contiguous open space may be paved areas or plazas.

(4) At a minimum, the open space must contain the following design elements. Bicycle racks and trash receptacles provided pursuant to subsection (b)(2) may be counted towards the minimum requirements below:

(A) Benches or an exterior seating area.

(B) A minimum of 25 percent of the one-and-a-half acres of open space must be improved to provide shade, using tree canopy cover (which may include trees provided pursuant subsection S-164.113(d), awnings, shade structures, building overhangs, or other means to provide users refuge from the elements).

(C) A minimum of five trash receptacles dispersed throughout the open space.

(D) A minimum of five bicycle racks dispersed throughout the open space.

(g) Corner of Nowitzki Way and Houston Street.

(1) The area of street frontage cross-hatched on the conceptual plan at the corner of Nowitzki Way and Houston Street must:

(A) Provide a pedestrian connection from the public right-of-way at the corner of Nowitzki Way and Houston Street to the one-and-a-half acres of open space required pursuant to subsection (f).

(B) The pedestrian connection may be provided via connecting sidewalks.

(C) The pedestrian connection must include one or a combination of the following:

(i) ground-level activating uses including retail, bar and restaurant, residential, or professional, office, personal service, and custom craft uses; or

(ii) an open space or plaza to encourage pedestrian activity.

(2) The area of frontage along Houston Street between the area cross-hatched on the conceptual plan and internal street Type A – Segment 2, if any, must include one or a combination of the following:

(A) ground-level activating uses including retail, bar and restaurant, residential, or professional, personal service, and custom craft uses; or

(B) an open space or plaza to encourage pedestrian activity.

(h) Pedestrian plaza. A pedestrian plaza must be provided connecting to the area of street frontage cross-hatched on the conceptual plan at the corner of Nowitzki Way and Houston Street. The area may include the sidewalk and landscape buffer shown on the streetscape standards. The minimum depth of the pedestrian plaza is 25 feet. At a minimum, the pedestrian plaza must be constructed with one or more types of enhanced pavement such as, natural stone, concrete, brick or stone pavers, or a specialty concrete material (e.g., stamped, patterned, tinted, stained, scored, or textured concrete). Landscape amenities (e.g., planters or trees) may be incorporated into the design of the plaza to create a welcoming and comfortable space for pedestrians

(i) Houston Street frontage.

(1) A minimum of 50 percent of the Houston Street frontage of the subdistrict (approximately 320 linear feet) must include one or a combination of the following:

(A) ground level activating uses including retail, bar and restaurant, residential, or professional, personal service, and custom craft uses;

(B) vitrines;

(C) no building or structure within the first 100 feet of depth, measured from the front lot line of Houston Street;

(D) an open space or plaza to encourage pedestrian activity; or

(E) internal streets.

(2) The minimum 50 percent of frontage is determined by measuring the Houston Street frontage of the subdistrict in linear feet. A maximum of 30 feet of frontage containing vitrines may be used to satisfy the minimum 50 percent requirement.

(j) Parking structures.

(1) Except as provided in this paragraph, exterior parking structure facade openings on aboveground parking structures must provide solid screening with a painted, stained, or masonry-like finish, similar in appearance or complimentary to the facade of the main non- parking building, a minimum of 42 inches from the floor level within the parking structure to screen vehicles and vehicle headlights. Glass is not a required screening material, regardless of whether glass is the primary building material for the main building.

(2) Sloping ramps located at the perimeter of aboveground parking structures must be screened through use of vegetation, panels, solid walls, or other architectural elements to obscure at least half of the sloping ramps’ length from view. Screening may include architectural grill work or other materials that provide ventilation. The garage is not required to be fully enclosed to satisfy this condition.

(3) Parking structure facades facing public streets or internal streets must contain retail, bar and restaurant, residential, or professional, personal service, and custom craft uses at the ground level.

(k) Ground floor entries for multiple-family uses. A minimum of 60 percent of the public street-facing, ground level dwelling units in a multiple-family building must have:

(1) individual entries directly from the outside;

(2) street access; and

(3) an improved path connecting the dwelling unit to the sidewalk.

(l) Fencing for multiple-family uses. Any fencing of private front yards may not exceed 48 inches in height.

(m) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as not to be visible from any adjacent public right-of-way.

(n) Lighting. Pedestrian lighting must be provided at regular intervals along all building facades facing a public street, an internal street, and the southern boundary of the subdistrict labeled as Former River Street (Private) on the conceptual plan in order to provide suitable lighting on sidewalks, streets, walkways, or plazas, as applicable, to enhance pedestrian safety. Lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent residential properties. Lighting must be spaced a maximum of 100 feet apart.

(o) Service and loading zones along Nowitzki Way. Service and loading zones are prohibited along Nowitzki Way and must either be concealed by a building or internal to a building so as not visible from Nowitzki Way.

(p) Service and loading zones north of internal street Type A – Segment 2 along Houston Street. Service and loading zones are prohibited on the portion of Houston Street north of internal street Type A – Segment 2. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
164.text:
SEC. S-164.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this subsection, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) On-street loading spaces may not be used to satisfy the off-street loading requirements.

(c) This subdistrict is considered one lot for purposes of required parking calculations.

(d) When a development includes a multiple-family use that complies with Section S- 164.114, required parking may be reduced in accordance with the following:

(1) Multiple-family use. A minimum of 0.95 space per dwelling unit is required.

(2) Hotel and motel use. A minimum of 0.5 space per unit is required, plus a minimum of one space per 300 square feet of floor area of event, meeting, conference, restaurant, and bar space.

(3) Bar and restaurant uses. A minimum of the lesser of one space per 300 square feet of floor area or compliance with Part I of this article is required.

(4) Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses. Except for office uses, a minimum of the lesser of one space per 300 square feet of floor area or compliance with Part I of this article is required. For office uses a minimum of one space per 440 square feet of floor area is required.

(5) Retail uses. A minimum of the lesser of one space per 300 square feet of floor area or compliance with Part I of this article is required. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Environmental Performance Standards
164.text:
SEC. S-164.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Landscaping
164.text:
SEC. S-164.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) Plant materials. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(c) Landscape phase area. An applicant for a building permit may request that the building official create a landscape phase area to satisfy the landscaping requirements of Part I of this article. Any landscape phase area created by the building official must:

(1) wholly include the area on which the construction work is to be done; and

(2) include the tree planting zone and sidewalk for new construction that is located within 60 feet of the nearest public street frontage. A landscape phase area need not be platted; however, it must be delineated on plans approved by the building official prior to the issuance of a building permit.

(d) Street trees.

(1) Along all public streets, internal streets, and the southern boundary of the subdistrict labeled as Former River Street (Private) on the conceptual plan trees must be provided within the tree planting zone shown on the streetscape standards.

(2) One large canopy tree must be provided for every 25 feet of frontage, with a minimum of two trees required, excluding frontage with visibility triangles or driveways.

(3) One large tree or medium tree must be provided for each 1,100 square feet of the one-and-a-half acres of contiguous open space provided in accordance with Section S- 164.110. Street trees and site trees may count toward the requirements. No more than 25 percent of the required street trees may be medium. Open space trees may count toward the site tree requirements.

(4) Along internal streets, the tree spacing requirements in Part I of this article do not apply. Trees along internal streets required pursuant to paragraph (1) may be concentrated or grouped at one or more central locations or focal points of a development.

(5) If the property owner is unable to locate a required tree within the tree planting zone shown on the streetscape standards due to overhead or underground utility conflicts or proximity to structures, the building official may approve a reduction in the size of the required trees, or a different location for the required trees outside of the tree planting zone or landscape buffer, elsewhere within the subdistrict or adjacent public right-of-way.

(e) Garbage storage areas. Where off-street loading or garbage storage areas are concealed by a building or internal to a building, the screening required by Part I of this article is not required.

(f) Parking structures. Where parking structures contain retail, bar and restaurant, residential, or professional, personal service, and custom craft uses at ground level, compliance with the landscape buffer for aboveground parking structures required by Part I of this article is not required. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Mixed Income Housing
164.text:
SEC. S-164.114. MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, as amended, is required to obtain the development bonuses in Sections S-164.109 and S-164.111. Compliance with Division 51A-4.1100 is not required for any buildings constructed prior to the date that the floor area ratio on any subarea exceeds 7.0:1.

(b) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Signs
164.text:
SEC. S-164.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Additional Provisions
164.text:
SEC. S-164.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) A maximum of two separate low-impact developments are allowed per subarea by right. More than two separate low-impact developments per subarea may be approved by specific use permit.

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(d) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 31954)

164.title: Compliance With Conditions
164.text:
SEC. S-164.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31954)

165.title: Legislative History
165.text:
SEC. S-165.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 165 was established by Ordinance No. 31958, passed by the Dallas City Council on August 11, 2021. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Property Location And Size
165.text:
SEC. S-165.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 165 is established on property bounded by Vine Street, Cole Avenue, and Laclede Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 165 is 1.13 acres. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Definitions And Interpretations
165.text:
SEC. S-165.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division, SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a non-residential zoning district. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Exhibits
165.text:
SEC. S-165.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division: Exhibit S-165A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Conceptual Plan
165.text:
SEC. S-165.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit S- 165A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Main Uses Permitted
165.text:
SEC. S-165.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the GR General Retail

Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the GR General Retail Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the GR General Retail Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 31958)

165.title: Accessory Uses

167.text:

PD Subdistrict 167 is established on property located along the northeast line of Fairmount Street southeast of Carlisle Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 167 is 0.83 acres. (Ord. 32190)

167.title: Definitions And Interpretations
167.text:
SEC. S-167.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) ELECTRIC VEHICLE SUPPLY EQUIPMENT (EVSE) means the conductors, including the ungrounded, grounded, and equipment grounding conductors, and the electric vehicle connectors, attachment plugs, and all other fittings, devices, power outlets, or apparatus installed specifically for the purpose of transferring energy between the premises wiring and the electric vehicle.

(2) EV CAPABLE means electric capacity, conduit, and space to support a circuit for each EV parking space, and the installation of raceways, both underground and surface mounted, as required, to support the EVSE.

(3) EV INSTALLED means a designated parking space with a branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles and an electric vehicle charging station installed.

(4) EV READY means a designated parking space which is provided with one dedicated branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles. The circuit shall terminate in a suitable termination point such as a receptacle or junction box and be located in close proximity to the proposed location of the EV parking spaces.

(5) LAST-MILE DELIVERY VEHICLES means vehicles for short term deliveries including, but not limited to, restaurant and food delivery and last-mile retail contract deliveries that are typically made in non-commercial vehicles that can safely park and maneuver within a standard parking space.

(6) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging micro-mobility vehicles such as e-scooters and e-bikes.

(7) MICRO-UNIT means an efficiency, studio, or one-bedroom unit less than 450 square feet in size.

(8) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 32190)

167.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
167.text:
SEC. S-167.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(b) Multiple-family or mixed-use development.

(1) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet for the first 36 feet in height and 25 feet for all portions of the building over 36 feet in height.

(2) Side and rear yard. No minimum side or rear yard.

(3) Yard encroachments.

(A) The following may encroach up to the Carlisle Street and Fairmount Street property line having a maximum height of four feet: stoops, steps, handrails, guardrails, retaining walls, seating walls, patios, benches, stone blocks, pots, raised planters, decks, and sculptures.

(B) The following may encroach up to the Carlisle Street and Fairmount Street property line having a maximum height of six feet: balcony privacy screens perpendicular to the building facade and above the first story.

(C) Awnings, arcades, balconies, cantilevered roofs, parapets and canopies with a minimum 10-foot clearance above grade may project up to six feet into the required yards.

(4) Floor area ratio and height.

(A) Floor area ratio. Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum floor area ratio is 2.5:1.

(B) Height. Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 120 feet.

(C) Development bonuses. Maximum floor area ratio may be increased to 9.4:1 and maximum height may be increased to 320 feet if the following conditions are met:

(i) a minimum of two and one-half percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 61 and 80 percent of the area median family income (AMFI) and a minimum of two and one-half percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 81 and 100 percent of the AMFI;

(ii) compliance with Section S-167.113; and

(iii) five percent of the multiple-family rental units are micro- units. Micro-units may not be used to fulfill the requirements of Section S-167.108(b)(4)(C)(i).

(5) Minimum lot area. Minimum lot area per unit must comply with the MF-4 subdistrict standards as described in Section 51P-193.125. (Ord. 32190)

167.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
167.text:
SEC. S-167.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off- street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Multiple-family.

(1) One off-street parking spaces per unit is required.

(2) Two small and one medium off-street loading spaces are required.

(3) A total of eight guest parking spaces must be available outside of any secured area, and such guest parking may be included in the other parking spaces required in this section.

(c) Bar and restaurant. For bar and restaurant uses, covered outdoor dining areas are excluded for the purposes of calculating off-street parking requirements.

(d) Electric vehicle charging.

(1) A minimum of one percent of parking spaces must be EV installed parking spaces.

(2) A minimum of two percent of parking spaces must be EV ready.

(3) A minimum of 10 percent of all parking spaces must be EV capable.

(4) The EV ready and EV installed spaces may be included in required EV capable required spaces.

(e) Last-mile delivery parking. One parking space must be available outside of any secured area for use by last-mile delivery vehicles. (Ord. 32190)

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32190)

167.text:

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 32190)

167.title: Urban Design Standards
167.text:
SEC. S-167.113. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Applicability. For a project to qualify for the increased development standards in Section S-167.108(b)(4), it must comply with all requirements in this section. If the increased development standards in Section S-167.108(b)(4) are not applied, the provisions of this section do not apply.

(b) Structured parking screening. Above ground parking levels must be concealed by the main building along Fairmont Street and Carlisle Street and fully enclose any street-facing garage with garage openings not to exceed the average of the windows on that facade and to be clad in like materials, excluding at grade vehicle entrances. Other elevations of above ground structured parking must contain solid headlight screening a minimum of 44 inches from the floor level within the parking structure. A minimum of one level of parking must be provided below- grade.

(c) Sidewalks. A minimum eight-foot-wide sidewalk is required along Fairmount Street and Carlisle Street. A minimum of 50 percent of the landscape buffer between the curb and sidewalk must be pervious.

(d) Pedestrian safety. Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk wherever possible, subject to approval of the director.

(e) Pedestrian scale lighting. Pedestrian scale lighting that provides a minimum maintained average illumination level of 1.5-foot candles must be provided along public sidewalks

and adjacent to public streets. Exterior lighting sources must be oriented down and onto the property they light and generally away from adjacent residential properties. Unless otherwise provided, the property owner is responsible for the cost of installation, operation, and maintenance of the lighting.

(f) Micro-mobility charging and parking. Micro-mobility charging and parking for six vehicles must be provided along Fairmount Street or Carlisle Street.

(g) Open space. Landscaped areas between the sidewalk and the primary structure adjacent to Carlisle Street and within 60 feet of the intersection of Fairmont Street must be a minimum of 90 percent pervious materials. A minimum of 1,500 square feet of total open space must be provided at the intersection of Carlisle Street and Fairmount Street.

(h) Ground level uses. A minimum of 4,000 square feet of non-residential uses must be provided at ground level.

(i) Building configuration and articulation.

(1) For building elevations parallel to Fairmount Street, a minimum of 50 percent of the building over 36 feet in height must be setback at least 10 feet from the base facade.

(2) For building elevations parallel to Carlisle Street, a minimum of 40 percent of the building over 36 feet in height must be setback at least six feet from the base facade.

(3) Balconies located at the corner of the building at Fairmount Street and Carlisle Street must be a minimum of five feet in depth and 60 square feet in area.

(4) A minimum 5,000 square foot outdoor amenity deck and an additional 1,000 square foot upper tower outdoor amenity deck are required.

(5) The southwest building corner must have a minimum setback of 40 feet from the intersection of Carlisle Street and Fairmount Street. Canopies, arcades, overhangs, and other permitted setback encroachments may project into this setback. (Ord. 32190)

(a) Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A-4.1100 is required to obtain development bonuses in Section S-167.108(b)(4).

(b) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required.

(c) A maximum 15 percent of the total units may be specialty units and are not required to be part of the dispersal of reserved dwelling units by type; however, the overall five percent mixed-income housing requirement is calculated based on the total number of all units. (Ord. 32190)

(iv) do not apply. (Ord. 32190)

168.text:
SEC. S-168.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the GR General Retail Subdistrict apply.

(b) Front yard.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, minimum front yard is 10 feet. Encroachments such as awnings, balconies, bay windows, generators and equipment less than eight feet in height, ramps, retaining walls, stairs, stoops, and unenclosed porches may encroach into the required front yard and need not to be shown on the development plan.

(2) Urban form.

(A) Additional setbacks for portions of buildings along Fairmount Street are required to provide for light and air circulation. Front yards are measured in accordance with

Section 51P-193.118(a)(2). Calculation of the percentage of the facade that requires an additional setback is a percentage of the building facade length of the street level of the building along Fairmount Street.

(B) For portions of a building above 36 feet in height, a minimum setback of 20 feet is required for at least 75 percent of the length of the front building facade. The remaining percentage is not required to provide additional setback.

(c) Side and rear yard. No minimum side or rear yard is required.

(d) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 3:1.

(e) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 162 feet.

(2) Ornamental cupolas, spires, tempiettos, or domes on top of a building may project up to a maximum height of 240 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 65 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(g) Tower coverage. Maximum tower coverage for portions of a structure above 150 feet is four percent and limited to the location shown on the development plan.

(h) Building separation. At least one 35-foot minimum facade separation is required between building facades above the third floor on the Fairmount Street and Throckmorton Street facades, as shown on the development plan. The facade separations must be for the full depth of the building. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
168.text:
SEC. S-168.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Office. One space per 400 square feet of floor area is required.

(c) Location. A minimum of 90 percent of the required parking must be located underground.

(d) Loading. For an office use, a minimum of one medium loading space is required. Ingress to and egress from Throckmorton Street as shown on the development may be used to access off-street loading spaces. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Environmental Performance Standards
168.text:
SEC. S-168.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Landscaping
168.text:
SEC. S-168.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) Street trees. In addition to trees required in the tree planting zone, the general planting zone must contain one tree for each 25 feet of lot frontage, excluding driveways and visibility triangles.

(c) Foundation planting. Shrubs located between fencing and the building face must be planted along the building face to maintain an open yard. Shrubs must be planted and maintained to not obscure windows.

(d) Sidewalks. In accordance with the Street Design Manual, sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk whenever possible. A waiver of this requirement is available subject to approval of the director.

(e) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Design Standards
168.text:
SEC. S-168.112. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Applicability. The following design standards apply to any structures built after April 27, 2022.

(b) Recommend architecture. To be compatible with development on the southwest side of Maple Avenue and north of Oak Lawn Avenue, exterior building materials are recommended to be masonry, cast stone, or similar materials; classical architectural style; and similar in the detailing of architectural features of those properties.

(c) Entrances.

(1) All street-facing entrances must be architecturally prominent and clearly visible from the street.

(2) Primary entrances for retail uses and professional, personal service, and custom crafts uses must face the street or a courtyard, door yard, or plaza with direct access to the

street. Primary entrances must be clearly visible through the use of two or more of the following architectural details.

(A) Arcade.

(B) Arch.

(C) Awning.

(D) Canopy.

(E) Decorative elements such as tile work, molding, raised banding, or projected banding.

(F) Enhanced cornice details.

(G) Recess.

(c) Surface parking location. Surface parking must comply with special retail street parking setback requirements. For purposes of this paragraph, surface parking means at grade parking not within or under a structure.

(d) Street facing facades.

(1) Entrances. A minimum of one entrance is required for each street frontage. Each entrance must face the street and access the street with an improved path connection to the sidewalk.

(2) Transparency.

(A) The following minimum transparency is required for street-facing facades.

(i) Ground story. 25 percent.

(ii) Upper story transparency. 20 percent.

(B) All street facing facades must have no more than 30 continuous linear feet without a transparent area (e.g., a window or a transparent door or opening).

(3) Visual division. The street facing facades of all buildings other than accessory buildings must be visually divided into a base, a middle, and a top.

(A) The base must span at least 24 feet above the ground-level finish floor and be distinguished from the middle by a change of materials, horizontal banding, change of color, or change of plane.

(B) The top must be distinguished from the middle by cornice treatments, roof overhangs with brackets, stepped parapets, corbeling, textured materials, change in window patterning, change in balcony expression, or differently colored materials. Color bands are not acceptable as the only treatment for the top.

(4) Four-sided architecture. A building’s architectural features and treatment must be applied to all sides of buildings. Building details, including roof forms, windows, doors, and trim, must reflect the architectural style of the building. All sides of a commercial building must display a similar level of quality and architectural detailing.

(e) Pedestrian driveway crossings. At each driveway and sidewalk intersection, driveways must be continuous and level and clearly marked by colored concrete, patterned or stamped concrete, or brick pavers for pedestrian crossing.

(f) Non-required fences. Non-required fences are limited to the fencing shown on the development plan.

(1) Fence panels. Except for required screening, all fence panels along a street must have a surface area that is a minimum of 50 percent open.

(2) Height. Maximum fence height for non-required fences is six feet.

(3) Fairmount Street. Fencing along Fairmount Street is prohibited within a required Fairmount Street front yard.

(g) Screening of loading spaces. Off-street loading spaces abutting a street must be screened with a minimum five-foot-wide planting area with large evergreen shrubs installed in accordance with Part I of this article. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Signs
168.text:
SEC. S-168.113. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Attached signs may not be internally illuminated or installed with back lighting. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Additional Provisions
168.text:
SEC. S-168.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 32187)

168.title: Compliance With Conditions
168.text:
SEC. S-168.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32187)

169.title: Legislative History
169.text:
SEC. S-169.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 169 was established by Ordinance No. 32217, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 25, 2022. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Property Location And Size
169.text:
SEC. S-169.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 169 is established on property located at the intersection of Travis Street and Knox Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 169 is 3.876 acres. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Definitions And Interpretations
169.text:
SEC. S-169.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls. In this division:

(1) BLANK BUILDING WALL means exterior ground floor walls of buildings fronting a public street that do not include a window, door, building modulation, or other architectural fenestrations.

(2) ELECTRIC VEHICLE SUPPLY EQUIPMENT (EVSE) means the conductors, including the ungrounded, grounded, and equipment grounding conductors, and the electric vehicle connectors, attachment plugs, and all other fittings, devices, power outlets, or apparatus installed specifically for the purpose of transferring energy between the premises wiring and the electric vehicle.

(3) EV CAPABLE means electric capacity, conduit, and space to support a circuit for each EV parking space, and the installation of raceways, both underground and surface mounted, as required, to support the EVSE.

(4) EV INSTALLED means a designated parking space with a branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles and an electric vehicle charging station installed.

(5) EV READY means a designated parking space which is provided with one dedicated branch circuit for EVSE servicing electric vehicles.

(6) GROUND LEVEL means the story of a building closest to and above grade along the street.

(7) INTERNAL WAY means a private street or drive that is labeled as the internal way on the development plan (Exhibit S-169A).

(8) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging micro-mobility vehicles such as e-scooters and e-bikes.

(9) OPEN SPACE means an area not less than 10 feet in width or length that is unobstructed to the sky and containing no structures except for ordinary projections of cornices and eaves or an area that is otherwise open air and has a building clearance of at least 30 feet in height and is not less than 25 feet in width.

(10) SPECIAL PROJECT means a development with a height greater than 240 feet or floor-to-area ratio greater than 4.5 to 1 that qualifies for a bonus in accordance with Section S-169.110.

(11) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(12) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window opening, door openings, or other opening, expressed as a percentage of total facade area by story.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this ordinance are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Exhibits
169.text:
SEC. S-169.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-169A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-169B: height plan. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Development Plan
169.text:
SEC. S-169.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a special project, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-169A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Main Uses Permitted
169.text:
SEC. S-169.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Accessory Uses
169.text:
SEC. S-169.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
169.text:
SEC. S-169.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Special project.

(1) Minimum front yard.

(A) Existing building walls on Knox Street. No minimum front yard is required for the portion of the Knox Street frontage noted on the development plan as the area where the existing building walls will remain.

(B) Remaining Knox Street frontage. Except for the portion of the Knox Street frontage noted on the development plan as the area where the existing building walls will remain, the following minimum front yard must be provided for all buildings and structures fronting on Knox Street:

(i) For portions of a building 40 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of a building greater than 40 feet in height, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(C) Armstrong Avenue and Travis Street frontages. Front yards are measured from the property line rather than any street easements, and the following minimum

front yards must be provided for all buildings and structures fronting on Armstrong Avenue and Travis Street:

(i) For portions of a building 40 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of a building greater than 40 feet in height, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(D) Encroachments. Canopies may project up to five feet into the required front yard on Knox Street. Otherwise, ordinary projections of windowsills, belt courses, cornices, or other architectural features may not project more than 12 inches into the required front yard. Cantilevered roof eaves and balconies may not project more than five feet into the required front yard.

(2) Height.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 240 feet.

(B) Maximum structure height in height zone A1 shown on the height plan (Exhibit S-169B) is 170 feet.

(C) Maximum structure height in height zone A2 shown on the height plan is 165 feet.

(D) Maximum structure height in height zone A3 shown on the height plan is 55 feet.

(E) Maximum structure height in height zone A4 shown on the height plan is 40 feet.

(F) Maximum structure height in height zones A5 and A6 shown on the height plan is 22 feet.

(G) Maximum structure height in height zone B1 shown on the height plan is 399 feet.

(H) Maximum structure height in height zone B2 shown on the height plan is 383 feet.

(I) Maximum structure height in height zone B3 shown on the height plan is 330 feet.

(J) Maximum structure height in height zone B4 shown on the height plan is 270 feet.

(K) Maximum structure height in height zone B5 shown on the height plan is 200 feet.

(L) Maximum structure height in height zone B6 shown on the height plan is 135 feet.

(M) Maximum structure height in height zone B7 shown on the height plan is 65 feet.

(N) Maximum structure height in height zone B8 shown on the height plan is 50 feet.

(O) Maximum structure height in height zone C1 shown on the height plan is 345 feet.

(P) Maximum structure height in height zone C2 shown on the height plan is 145 feet.

(Q) Maximum structure height in height zone C3 shown on the height plan is 40 feet.

(R) The following may project a maximum of 10 feet above the maximum structure heights:

(i) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead;

(ii) Mechanical equipment;

(iii) Cooling tower;

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids;

(v) Skylights;
