(vi) Visual screens which surround roof mounted mechanical equipment;

(vii) Chimney and vent stacks;

(viii) Lightning protection equipment;

(ix) Cell towers or other communication equipment;

(x) Parapet wall.

(3) Floor area ratio.

(A) If compliant with Section S-169.110, maximum floor area ratio is 5 to 1.

(B) Land area that is located outside of this subdistrict but is located within the same platted lot as land within this subdistrict is included for floor area ratio calculations.

(4) Lot coverage.

(A) For any portion of buildings or structures 40 feet or less in height, maximum lot coverage is 70 percent.

(B) For any portion of buildings or structures above 40 feet in height and up to 155 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 56 percent.

(C) For any portions of buildings or structures above 155 feet in height and up to 260 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 35 percent.

(D) For any portions of buildings or structures above 260 feet in height and up to 330 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 19 percent.

(E) For any portions of buildings or structures above 330 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 16 percent.

(F) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; but surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(5) Below grade parking structures. Below grade parking structures may extend to the lot line and across lot lines within this subdistrict. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Urban Design Requirements For A Special Project
169.text:
SEC. S-169.109. URBAN DESIGN REQUIREMENTS FOR A SPECIAL PROJECT.

(a) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum six-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required along Armstrong Avenue.

(2) A minimum 10-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required along Travis Street from Knox Street to Armstrong Avenue.

(3) Except as provided in this subsection, a minimum 10-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required along Knox Street. A minimum five-foot-wide unobstructed

sidewalk is required along the portion of the Knox Street frontage noted on the development plan as the area where the existing building walls will remain.

(4) A minimum seven-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required along the internal way noted on the development plan.

(5) Pedestrian streetlamps are allowed within the sidewalk spaced at 45 feet to 60 feet on center with the exception of visibility triangles and vehicular drives.

(6) Sidewalks must be level across all driveways and curb cuts.

(b) Pedestrian amenities. The following minimum pedestrian amenities are required along the Travis Street and Knox Street frontages:

(1) benches (occupying at least 10 linear feet per street frontage),

(2) trash receptacles (one per street frontage), and

(3) bicycle racks (two per street frontage and one in the location marked open space on the development plan along the Katy Trail)

(c) Restrooms. Restrooms must be provided at ground level along the Katy Trail-facing facade of a building.

(d) Ground level transparency and maximum blank wall.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, any facade facing Knox Street must have a minimum transparency of 65 percent for the portion of the building at ground level between grade and 15 feet in height.

(2) Except as provided in this subsection, any facade facing Travis Street must have a minimum transparency of 70 percent for the portion of the building at ground level between grade and 15 feet in height.

(3) Except as provided in this subsection, the length of a blank building wall at ground level between grade and 15 feet in height fronting a public street may not exceed 30 feet.

(4) This subsection does not apply to parking structures or loading areas.

(e) Street level activating uses.

(1) A minimum of 9,000 square feet of floor area on the ground level of any building that has frontage along Knox Street or Travis Street must contain one or a combination of the following uses:

(A) Bar and restaurant uses.

(B) Retail uses.

(C) Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses.

(2) For any building that has frontage along Knox Street or Travis Street, the minimum 9,000 square feet of floor area required under this subsection must be located along building facades facing a public street.

(3) A minimum of 2,000 square feet of floor area on the ground level of any building that has frontage along Armstrong Avenue must contain one or a combination of the following uses:

(A) Bar and restaurant uses.

(B) Retail uses.

(C) Professional, personal service, and custom craft uses.

(f) Minimum open space. A minimum of 18,000 square feet of open space must be provided in the locations shown on the development plan. Paved areas such as sidewalks, walkways, and plazas may be counted as part of the open space area. A maximum of 50 percent of the 18,000 square foot open space area may be impervious. Parking structures may be located below grade underneath pervious or impervious open space area. At a minimum the open space must contain the following design elements:

(1) Decorative pavement, which may include colored concrete pavers; brick; stone; stamped, textured, or colored concrete; or exterior grade tile.

(2) Benches or exterior seating area.

(g) Shade. A minimum of 25 percent of the 18,000 square feet of open space area must be improved to provide shade, using trees, awnings, shade structures, building overhangs, or other means to provide users refuge from the elements.

(h) Parking structures. Except for surface parking spaces shown on the development plan, all required off-street parking must be located below grade.

(i) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical and related equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as not to be visible from any adjacent public right- of-way.

(j) Pedestrian lighting. Pedestrian lighting must be provided at regular intervals along all building facades facing a public street or the internal way in order to provide suitable lighting on sidewalks, streets or walkways, as applicable, to enhance pedestrian safety. Lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent residential properties.

(k) Outdoor amplified sound. Retail and bar and restaurant uses may not utilize outdoor amplified sound systems after 10:00 p.m. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Development              Bonus         For        Mixed-Income
169.text:
SEC. S-169.110 DEVELOPMENT BONUS FOR MIXED-INCOME HOUSING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a special project qualifies for the development bonus in Section S-169.108(b) if a minimum of six percent of the total dwelling units within the building containing residential uses in the southwest portion of the Property as shown on the development plan are available to households earning between 61 percent and 80 percent of the area median family income in compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, as amended.

(b) A maximum of 50 percent of the total units may be specialty units including club suites and penthouse suites and are not required to be part of the dispersal of reserved dwelling units by type; however, the overall six percent requirement of this subsection is calculated based on the total number of units in the building containing residential units in the southwest portion of the Property as shown on the development plan.

(c) A minimum of 25 percent of the reserved units must contain two or more bedrooms, and all reserved units must have at least one separate bedroom.

(d) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107, as amended, is not required. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
169.text:
SEC. S-169.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Environmental Performance Standards
169.text:
SEC. S-169.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Sustainable Design Features
169.text:
SEC. S-169.113. SUSTAINABLE DESIGN FEATURES.

(a) Electric vehicle charging. A minimum of 10 percent of required off-street parking spaces must service electric vehicles, with the required type of spaces as follows:

(1) A minimum of one percent of required off-street parking spaces must be EV installed parking spaces;

(2) A minimum of two percent of required off-street parking spaces must be EV ready; and

(3) A minimum of seven percent of all required off-street parking spaces must be EV capable.

(b) EV ready parking spaces. EV ready parking spaces must include a circuit that terminates in a suitable termination point such as a receptacle or junction box and be located in close proximity to the proposed location of the EV parking spaces.

(c) Micro-mobility charging and parking. Micro-mobility charging and parking for at least 10 vehicles must be provided along public streets and eight vehicles in the location marked open space on the development plan along the Katy Trail. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Landscaping
169.text:
SEC. S-169.114. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) An applicant for a building permit may request that the building official create a landscape phase area to satisfy the landscaping requirements of Part I of this article. Any landscape phase area created by the building official must: (1) wholly include the area on which the construction work is to be done; and (2) include the tree planting zone and sidewalk for new construction that is located within 60 feet of the nearest public street frontage. A landscape phase area need not be platted; however, it must be delineated on plans approved by the building official prior to the issuance of a building permit.

(c) Along the portion of the Knox Street frontage noted on the development plan as the area where the existing building walls will remain, the tree planting zone is that area parallel to and between zero and five feet from the back of the projected street curb, and may be paved. Required trees may be provided within tree grates within this area to satisfy the requirements of Section 51P-193.126(b)(5).

(d) All trees must have a minimum caliper of five inches, and street trees must be spaced no greater than 25 feet apart excluding driveways.

(e) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Signs
169.text:
SEC. S-169.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business districts in Article VII. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Additional Provisions
169.text:
SEC. S-169.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 32217)

169.title: Compliance With Conditions
169.text:
SEC. S-169.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32217)

172.title: Legislative History
172.text:
SEC. S-172.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 172 was established by Ordinance No. 32741, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 22, 2024.

172.title: Property Location And Size
172.text:
SEC. S-172.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 172 is established on property located on Inwood Road between Bordeaux Avenue and Lemmon Avenue. The size of PD Subdistrict 172 is approximately 3.035 acres.

172.title: Definitions And Interpretations
172.text:
SEC. S-172.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) ASSISTED LIVING FACILITY means a permanent residential facility, requiring an assisted living facility license from the State of Texas for all units, which furnishes (in single or multiple facilities) food, shelter, laundry, and other assistance, which may include memory care and in activities of daily living to five or more persons who are not related by blood, marriage, or adoption to the owner or proprietor of the establishment.

(2) OPEN SPACE means the portion of a building site that is principally open to the sky except for building overhangs or portions of the open space area underneath a portion of a building that provides shade above the open space.

(3) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district.

172.title: Exhibit
172.text:
SEC. S-172.105. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this division: Exhibit S-172A: assisted living facility development plan.

172.title: Development Plan
172.text:
SEC. S-172.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Assisted living facility. For an assisted living facility, development and use of the Property must comply with the assisted living facility development plan (Exhibit S-172A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the assisted living facility development plan, the text of this division controls.

(a) Other uses. For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply.

172.title: Main Uses Permitted
172.text:
SEC. S-172.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict only by specific use permit
(SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) The following additional main use is permitted by right:

-- Assisted living facility.

172.title: Accessory Uses
172.text:
SEC. S-172.108. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) In this section:

(1) ART STUDIO means a facility, within an assisted living facility and for the exclusive use of the residents, where art is displayed.

(2) CAFE OR FOOD STORE means a facility, within an assisted living facility and for the exclusive use of the residents, where food and beverages are sold to residents.

(3) DRUG FACILITY means a facility, within an assisted living facility and for the exclusive use of the residents, where drugs are dispensed.

(4) MOVIE THEATRE means a facility, within an assisted living facility and for the exclusive use of the residents, where motion pictures are shown.

(5) SALON means a facility, within an assisted living facility and for the exclusive use of the residents, where barber/beauty shop services are provided.

(b) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(c) The following accessory uses are permitted by right within this subdistrict but may not be open to the general public:

-- Art studio. -- Cafe or food store. -- Community center (private). -- Drug facility. -- Game court (private). -- Movie theatre. -- Salon. -- Swimming pool (private).

172.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
172.text:
SEC. S-172.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict apply.

(b) Assisted living facility.

(1) Front yard.

(i) Except as provided in this paragraph, minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(ii) An encroachment of an unenclosed structure less than 16 feet in height is permitted within the front setback along Inwood Road.

(iii) A screening fence with a maximum height of nine feet may be located within the front yards on La Foy Boulevard and Fairfax Avenue in front of the loading and service area.

(iv) Below grade parking structures may extend into the front yard.

(2) Side and rear yard.

(i) Minimum side yard is 10 feet.

(ii) Minimum rear yard is 10 feet.

(iii) Below grade parking structures may extend into the side and rear yards.

(3) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units and suites is 170.

(4) Lot area. No minimum lot area per dwelling unit or suite.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent. Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

172.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
172.text:
SEC. S-172.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Assisted living facility.

(1) A minimum of 0.7 space per dwelling unit or suite is required. No additional parking is required for a use that is accessory to an assisted living facility.

(2) All parking must be located underground. Only surface parking intended for short term pick-up and drop-off is permitted.

172.title: Environmental Performance Standards
172.text:
SEC. S-172.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI.

172.title: Landscaping
172.text:
SEC. S-172.112. LANDSCAPING.

Landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

172.title: Signs
172.text:
SEC. S-172.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

172.title: Urban Design Standards For An Assisted
172.text:
SEC. S-172.114. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS FOR AN ASSISTED LIVING FACILITY

(a) Pedestrian amenities. A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along each street frontage:

(1) Benches.

(2) Trash receptacles.

(3) Bicycle racks.

(b) Architectural elements. A minimum of one of the following architectural elements must be provided at all public entrances:

(1) Architecturally prominent public entrance.

(2) Canopy.

(3) Awning.

(4) Attached tower.

(5) Turret.

(c) Building articulation. Street-facing facades must contain articulation with a minimum depth of two feet of variation within the vertical plane for every 100 feet of facade length.

(d) Sidewalks.

(1) At each driveway and sidewalk intersection, crosswalks must be constructed of a material that differs in finish and color from that of vehicular ingress and egress driveways.

(2) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval of the director.

(3) A minimum six foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk with a minimum five-foot-wide buffer is required along all street frontages.

(e) Pedestrian lighting. Pedestrian scale lighting must be provided at regular intervals along all building facades facing a public street.

(f) Open space.

(i) Minimum required open space is 35,000 square feet.

(ii) Architectural elements such as colonnades, pergolas, and gazebos and structures supporting outdoor activities such as, but not limited to, shade structures, kiosks, or seating areas are allowed.

(iii) Open space may be located on top of a below grade parking structure.

(g) Ground level transparency. The following minimum transparency is required for street facing facades:

(i) Inwood Road. Minimum 15 percent.

(ii) Fairfax Avenue.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, minimum 20 percent.

(B) Between Lemmon Wood Plaza and La Foy Boulevard, minimum 15 percent.

(iv) Lemmon Wood Plaza. Minimum 12 percent.

172.title: Additional Provisions
172.text:
SEC. S-172.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) In general.

(1) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(2) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(3) Except as provided in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article.

(b) Retirement housing. Retirement housing may have a common dining facility.

(c) Assisted living facility. An assisted living facility may have centralized kitchens where food is prepared and centralized dining facilities. Individual dwelling units and suites may have kitchens.

172.title: Compliance With Conditions
172.text:
SEC. S-172.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

173.title: Legislative History
173.text:
SEC. S-173.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 173 was established by Ordinance No. 32780, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 26, 2024. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Property Location And Size
173.text:
SEC. S-173.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 173 is established on property located on McKinney Avenue and Central Expressway between Armstrong Avenue and Oliver Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 173 is approximately 3.251 acres. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Purpose
173.text:
SEC. S-173.103. PURPOSE.

The regulations in this division complement the development pattern in the area. The objectives of these regulations are as follows:

(1) To promote the health, safety, welfare, convenience, and enjoyment of the public.

(2) To achieve buildings more urban in form.

(3) To promote a pedestrian environment.

(4) To encourage underground off-street parking.

(5) To encourage development that complements nearby properties.

(6) To achieve buildings efficient in design and use of space while providing view corridors, light, and air to nearby properties.

(7) To achieve buildings that reduce natural resource consumption, enhance occupant comfort and health, lower utility consumption, minimize strain on local infrastructures, improve quality of life, and generally align with principles established in the Comprehensive Environmental and Climate Action Plan of the City of Dallas. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Definitions And Interpretations
173.text:
SEC. S-173.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) BLANK WALL means exterior ground floor walls of a building fronting a public street that does not include a window, door, building modulation, or other architectural fenestration.

(2) CONVALESCENT NURSING BUILDING means the building labeled as such on the development plan.

(3) GROUND LEVEL means the story of a building closest to and above grade along a public street or an internal street.

(4) HABITAT GARDEN means any planting areas that are native or native adaptive species to North Texas with low water or very low water consumption characteristics with the intention of attracting or providing habitat for bees, birds, butterflies, or other pollinators or a combination thereof. Turf and lawn areas are considered planting areas within this definition, provided however, that lawn and turf areas may use grasses that are not considered low or very low water consumption.

(5) LAST-MILE DELIVERY VEHICLES means vehicles for short term deliveries including, but not limited to, restaurant and food delivery and last-mile retail contract deliveries that are typically made in non-commercial vehicles that can safely park and maneuver within a standard parking space.

(6) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging micro-mobility vehicles such as e-scooters and e-bikes.

(7) MICRO-UNIT means an efficiency, studio, or one-bedroom unit less than 500 square feet in size.

(8) MULTIFAMILY BUILDING means the building labeled as such on the development plan for a project that qualifies for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116.

(9) OFFICE BUILDING means the building labeled as such on the development plan for a project that qualifies for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116.

(10) OPEN SPACE means an area not less than 10 feet in width or length that is unobstructed to the sky and containing no structures except for ordinary projections of cornices, balconies, building overhangs, eaves, pedestrian furniture, shade structures, or similar pedestrian amenities.

(11) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(12) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window opening, door opening, or other opening, expressed as a percentage of the total facade area by story.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Exhibits
173.text:
SEC. S-173.105. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-173A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-173B: landscape plan.

(3) Exhibit S-173C: height plan. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Development Plan
173.text:
SEC. S-173.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a project receiving a development bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-173A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Main Uses Permitted
173.text:
SEC. S-173.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) The only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this Subdistrict; etc.

(b) Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, related institution use, and retirement housing use may have a kitchen and a central dinning facility. Individual dwelling units and suites may have kitchens and a central dining facility. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Accessory Uses
173.text:
SEC. S-173.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
173.text:
SEC. S-173.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the LC Light Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Development bonus project. The following yard, lot, and space regulations apply to a project that complies with Sections S-173.110(b), S-173.112(b), S-173.113, S-173.114, and S-173.116.

(1) Front yard.

(A) McKinney Avenue and Armstrong Avenue.

(i) For portions of a structure less than 36 feet in height, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of a structure with a height of 36 feet or more, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(B) US-75 North Central Expressway.

(i) For portions of a structure less than 36 feet in height, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of a structure with a height of 36 feet or more, minimum front yard is 25 feet as shown on the development plan.

(C) Encroachments.

(i) Awnings or similar structures between 10 feet and 20 feet in height above grade may project up to 10 feet into the front yard.

(ii) Trellises, screens, awnings, balconies, and cantilevered roof eaves may project up to five feet into the front yard.

(iii) Retaining walls and planters with a maximum height of two feet may be located in the front yard.

(2) Side yard.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, minimum side yard is 10 feet.

(B) For the existing retail and restaurant building shown on the development plan, no required side yard.

(C) For the nursing convalescent building abutting a public alley, minimum side yard is 24 feet for the portion of the structure that is less than 60 feet in height and 30 feet for the portion of the structure that is 30 feet or more in height.

(3) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 7.9 to 1.

(4) Height.

(A) In general. Unless further restricted by the height shown on the height plan (Exhibit S-173C), maximum structure height is the following:

(i) Convalescent nursing building. Maximum structure height is 260 feet.

(ii) Office building. Maximum structure height is 295 feet.

(iii) Multifamily building. Maximum structure height is 399 feet.

(B) Parapet walls and railings. Parapet walls and railings may project up to four feet above the maximum structure heights.

(C) Other projections. The following may project a maximum of 10 feet above the maximum structure heights:

(i) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead;

(ii) Mechanical equipment;

(iii) Cooling tower;

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids;

(v) Skylights;

(vi) Visual screens surrounding roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(5) Lot coverage.

(A) For portions of a structure less than 36 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 55 percent.

(B) For portions of a structure 36 feet in height and up to 142 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 40 percent.

(C) For portions of a structure above 142 feet in height, maximum lot coverage is 37 percent.

(D) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking areas private drives, shade structures within open space, and underground parking structures are not. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
173.text:
SEC. S-173.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) For a project that qualifies for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116.

(1) All required parking must be located at grade and below grade.

(2) Four medium, three large, and four small loading spaces are required. Loading spaces may share maneuvering lanes, and separate buildings may share loading areas.

(3) For a retirement housing use, no additional parking is required for floor area outside of dwelling units.

(4) Maximum number of on-site surface parking spaces is 15.

(5) Two last-mile delivery vehicle parking spaces must be provided and clearly marked with a maximum of allowed time of 15 minutes. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Environmental Performance Standards
173.text:
SEC. S-173.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Landscaping
173.text:
SEC. S-173.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(b) For a project that qualifies for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-173B). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the landscape plan, the text of this division controls.

(2) Landscaping must consist of a habitat garden. The landscaping must be maintained with industry best practices to promote the healthy development and maintenance of pollinator habitats.

(3) The building official may allow for reduction or relocation of trees if necessary to avoid utility, driveway, or visibility triangle conflicts.

(c) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Sustainability Standards For A Development
173.text:
SEC. S-173.113. SUSTAINABILITY STANDARDS FOR A DEVELOPMENT BONUS PROJECT.

(a) Photovoltaic cells. A minimum of 1,000 square feet of photovoltaic cells for producing solar energy must be located on the roof of each building, with a total of 4,000 square feet required for the district.

(b) Micro-mobility charging and parking. Micro-mobility charging and parking for at least 12 micro-mobility vehicles must be provided along public streets.

(c) Bicycle parking.

(1) A minimum of one bicycle storage space for every three residential units is required onsite within the garage or residential building. Long-term bicycle storage spaces are not subject to the minimum size requirements for bicycle parking spaces in Division 51-4.330 and may be secured to wall or floor mounted storage racks.

(2) A minimum of 20 bicycle parking spaces must be provided for the office building within the garage or the office building, and if provided in the garage, such bicycle parking may be shared with the required bicycle parking for the residential building.

(d) No-smoking signs. No-smoking signs must be placed at all building entrances stating that smoking is prohibited within 25 feet of the building.

(e) Refrigerants. Zero CFC based refrigerants must be used on all HVAC equipment.

(f) Recycling. Locations for recycling paper, cardboard, glass, plastic, metal, mercury- containing lamps, batteries, and e-waste must be provided on site.

(g) Micro-units. A minimum of five percent of the dwelling units within the multifamily building must be micro-units. Micro-units may not be counted toward the percentage of units to qualify for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116(b).

(h) Drip irrigation. Drip irrigation must be utilized for maintenance of plantings.

(i) Irrigation.

(1) Condensate from base building HVAC cooling coils that are greater than five tons must be reused for cooling tower makeup or irrigation. Excess condensate must be discharged to a sanitary sewer if the amount of condensate wastewater exceeds the irrigation and cooling tower makeup water needs of the project.

(2) Detention and rainwater harvesting must be utilized for irrigation.

(j) Roofs. Light colored roof materials with an initial solar reflectance value of at least 0.80 that minimize cooling loads must be employed on all roofs. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Urban Design Standards For A Development Bonus
173.text:
SEC. S-173.114. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS FOR A DEVELOPMENT BONUS PROJECT.

(a) Pedestrian amenities. The following minimum pedestrian amenities are required along the McKinney Avenue and Armstrong Avenue frontages:

(1) Benches occupying at least 10 linear feet of frontage.

(2) A minimum of one trash receptacle and one recycling receptacle per street frontage.

(b) Ground level transparency.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, any facade along public streets must have a minimum transparency of 65 percent for the portion of the building at ground level between grade and 15 feet in height.

(2) Driveway and garage entrances are excluded in calculating facade area.

(c) Open space.

(1) A minimum of 14,000 square feet of open space must be provided.

(2) Paved areas such as sidewalks, walkways, courtyards, and plazas may be counted as part of open space area.

(3) A maximum of 60 percent of required open space may be impervious.

(4) Parking structures may be located below grade underneath pervious or impervious open space area.

(d) Shade. A minimum of 20 percent of the 14,000 square feet of open space area must be improved to provide shade, using trees, awnings, shade structures, building overhangs, or other means to provide users refuge from the elements.

(e) Sidewalks.

(1) A minimum 10-foot-wide unobstructed sidewalk is required along Armstrong Avenue and McKinney Avenue.

(2) At each driveway and sidewalk intersection, crosswalks must be constructed of a material that differs in finish and color from that of vehicular ingress and egress driveways.

(2) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval of the director.

(f) Screening of rooftop equipment. All mechanical and related equipment located on the rooftop of any building must be screened so as not to be visible from any adjacent public right- of-way.

(g) Pedestrian lighting.

(1) Pedestrian lighting must be provided at regular intervals along all building facades facing a public street or the internal way in order to provide suitable lighting on sidewalks, streets, or walkways, as applicable, to enhance pedestrian safety.

(2) Lighting must be directed downward and away from adjacent residential properties.

(3) Pedestrian scale lighting that provides a minimum maintained average illumination level of 1.5-foot candles must be provided along sidewalks, streets, or walkways, as applicable.

(h) Building lighting. Decorative lighting on the upper stories of buildings must be directed toward the building facade. Decorative light emitting diode bands not utilized for tenant signage are not permitted.

(i) Facade standards. The following design standards apply to facades:

(1) Facades must have a minimum transparency of 30 percent of the total area of each facade.

(2) Building entries must be architecturally prominent and clearly visible from the street or internal drives.

(3) Blank walls longer than 30 feet in length are prohibited. Where blank walls occur, horizontal or vertical articulation is required. A minimum of one change in plane is required for each 36 feet of horizontal or vertical articulation, such as an offset, reveal, recess, or projection. Changes in plane must have a width of no less than 12 inches and a depth of at least six inches and may include columns, planters, arches, niches, architectural details such as raised bands and cornices, architecturally prominent entrances, attached towers, awnings, or changes in material. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Signs
173.text:
SEC. S-173.115. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Development               Bonuses          For       Mixed-Income
173.text:
SEC. S-173.116. DEVELOPMENT BONUSES FOR MIXED-INCOME HOUSING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, as amended, is required to obtain the development bonuses in Section S-173.009.

(b) The height and floor area ratio development bonuses set forth in Section S-173.009 apply if a minimum two and one-half percent of the total dwelling units within the multifamily building are available to households earning between 81 percent and 100 percent of the area median family income.

(c) Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107, as amended, is not required. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Additional Provisions
173.text:
SEC. S-173.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) For uses that qualify for a bonus pursuant to Section S-173.116:

(1) Restaurant uses.

(a) Outdoor dining areas may not be operated after 11:00 p.m.

(b) Pollution control units must be provided to reduce odors from kitchen areas.

(2) Retail and personal service uses. Outdoor amplified sound systems may not be operated after 10:00 p.m. Amplified sound systems may not exceed 63 decibels.

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(d) Except as provided in this division, development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 32780)

173.title: Compliance With Conditions
173.text:
SEC. S-173.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32780)

174.title: Legislative History
174.text:
SEC. S-174.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 174 was established by Ordinance No. 32904, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 23, 2024. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Property Location And Size
174.text:
SEC. S-174.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 174 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Hall Street and Carlisle Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 174 is approximately 2.45 acres. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Definitions And Interpretations
174.text:
SEC. S-174.103 DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) HABITAT GARDEN means any planting areas that are native or native adaptive species to North Texas with low water or very low water consumption characteristics with the intention of attracting or providing habitat for bees, birds, butterflies, or other pollinators or a combination thereof.

(2) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging micro-mobility vehicles such as e-scooters and e-bikes.
(3) MICRO-UNIT means an efficiency, studio, or one-bedroom unit less than 475 square feet in size.

(4) OPEN SPACE means an area that is open to all occupants of a building on the same lot and is unobstructed to the sky without permanent structures, except structures supporting pedestrian activities, including colonnades, pergolas, and gazebos.

(5) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(6) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(7) TRANSPARENCY means the total area of window and door openings expressed as a percentage of the total street-level.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Exhibits
174.text:
SEC. S-174.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit S-174A: development plan.

(2) Exhibit S-174B: landscape plan. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Development Plan
174.text:
SEC. S-174.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For a project that qualifies for a development bonus in accordance with Section S- 174.114, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit S-174A). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the development plan, the text of this division controls.

(b) For all other uses, no development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51-4.702 regarding submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Main Uses Permitted
174.text:
SEC. S-174.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict only by specific use permit
(SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) For a project that qualifies for a development bonus in accordance with Section S- 174.114, the following additional main uses are also permitted in this subdistrict:

-- Restaurant without drive-in service [maximum 6,500 square feet]. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Accessory Uses
174.text:
SEC. S-174.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) Except as provided in this section, as a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due

to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Amateur communication tower. -- Open storage. -- Private stable. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
174.text:
SEC. S-174.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2 Multiple-Family Subdistrict apply.

(b) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 2.5 to 1.

(c) Development bonus project. The following yard, lot, and space regulations apply to a project that qualifies for a development bonus in accordance with Section S-174.114 and meets the requirements for a development bonus project in Sections S-174.110, S-174.112, S-174.113, and S-174.117.

(1) Front yard.

(A) Carlisle Place.

(i) For portions of structures 45 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of structures with a height greater than 45 feet, minimum front yard is 18 feet.

(B) Carlisle Street.

(i) For portions of structures 45 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(ii) For portions of structures with a height greater than 45 feet, minimum front yard is 35 feet.

(C) Hall Street.

(i) For portions of structures 45 feet in height or less, minimum front yard is 25 feet.

(ii) For portions of structures with a height greater than 45 feet but less than 65 feet, minimum front yard is 45 feet.

(iii) For portions of structures with a height greater than 65 feet, minimum front yard is 100 feet.

(D) Encroachments. Stoops, stairs, canopies, retaining walls, shade structures, planters, railings, and similar improvements may be located in the front yard.

(2) Side yard.

(A) Except as provided in this Paragraph, minimum side yard is 15 feet.

(B) For portions of structures with a height greater than 45 feet, minimum side yard is 120 feet.

(C) Stoops, stairs, canopies, retaining walls, shade structures, planters, railings, and similar improvements may be located in the side yard.

(3) Density. No minimum lot area per dwelling unit.

(4) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 5.8 to 1.

(5) Height.

(A) Except as provided in this Paragraph, maximum structure height is 360 feet.

(B) The following structures may project a maximum of 10 feet above the maximum structure height:

(i) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(ii) Mechanical equipment room and mechanical equipment.

(iii) Cooling tower.

(iv) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(v) Visual screens that surround roof-mounted mechanical equipment.

(vi) Chimney and vent stacks.

(C) Parapet walls may project a maximum of six feet above the maximum structure height.

(6) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 65 percent. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
174.text:
SEC. S-174.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult Part I of this article for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Urban Design Standards For A Project That
174.text:
SEC. S-174.110. URBAN DESIGN STANDARDS FOR A PROJECT THAT QUALIFIES FOR A DEVELOPMENT BONUS.

(a) In general. This section applies to a project that qualifies for a development bonus pursuant to Section S-174.114.

(b) Sidewalks.

(1) Sidewalks with a minimum unobstructed width of six feet are required along all street frontages.

(2) The minimum parkway width is five feet.

(3) The following buffering must be used where sidewalks abut any driving surface, off-street or on-street pedestrian loading zone, or parking surface:

(A) Landscaping plantings with a minimum height of 36 inches; or

(B) Bollards with a minimum height of 36 inches, spaced no more than six feet in distance from each other.

(4) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways, loading areas, and curb cuts, and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk subject to approval of the director.

(c) Driveways.

(1) Maximum number of driveways per street frontage is one.

(2) Maximum driveway width is 30 feet.

(3) At the intersection of each driveway with a sidewalk or pedestrian path, driveways must be clearly marked by colored concrete, patterned or stamped concrete, or brick pavers for pedestrian crossing.

(d) Pedestrian amenities.

(1) Street frontages. A minimum of two of each of the following pedestrian amenities must be provided along each street frontage:

(A) Benches.

(B) Trash and recycling receptacles.

(2) Katy Trail. At least one trash and recycling receptacle is required along the ground level pedestrian connection to the Katy Trail.

(e) Katy Trail-level pedestrian connection. At least one direct pedestrian connection from the Property to the Katy Trail is required. All uses located along the Katy Trail must have ground level access to the Katy Trail.

(f) Surface parking. Except for spaces intended for short term drop off and loading, surface parking that is not enclosed by a structure is prohibited.

(g) Screening. All rooftop mounted equipment must be screened.

(h) Crosswalk. Subject to review and approval of the director, a crosswalk demarked by signage, lighting, pavement markings, and traffic signaling must be provided from the property across Carlisle Street.

(i) Parking structures. Parking structures must be located primarily at or below grade with no more than a portion of a single level of parking structure above grade due to changes in topography across the Property. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Environmental Performance Standards
174.text:
SEC. S-174.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Sustainable Design Features For A Project
174.text:
SEC. S-174.112. SUSTAINABLE DESIGN FEATURES FOR A PROJECT THAT QUALIFIES FOR A DEVELOPMENT BONUS.

(a) Podium roof. A minimum of 30 percent of the podium roof area shown on the development plan must be covered with improvements that minimize heat production such as turf, synthetic turf, raised planters, photovoltaic cells, swimming pools, water features, or shade structures.

(b) Photovoltaic cells. At least 1,000 square feet of photovoltaic cells for producing solar energy must be located on a roof area of the main building.

(c) Irrigation.

(1) Except for lawn areas, drip irrigation is required for plant maintenance.

(2) If cooling coils are greater than five tons, condensate from main building HVAC must be reused for cooling tower makeup or irrigation. If excess condensate exceeds the irrigation and cooling tower makeup water needs of the project, it must be discharged to a sanitary sewer.

(3) Detention and rainwater harvesting must be utilized for irrigation.

(d) Recycling. Recycling containers must be available for residents and on-site workers.

(e) Micro-mobility charging and parking. Micro-mobility charging and parking for at least 10 vehicles must be provided within the front yard or along the Katy Trail.

(f) Bicycle parking. 20 total spaces for bicycle parking must be located along street frontages or along the Katy Trail.

(g) Facade lighting. Exterior lighting sources, if used, must be oriented down and onto the property they light and generally away from adjacent residential properties.

(h) Micro-units. A minimum of five percent of dwelling units must be micro-units. Micro-units do not count for purposes of qualifying for a mixed-income housing bonus pursuant to Section S-174.114(b). (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Landscaping
174.text:
SEC. S-174.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping and screening must be provided in accordance with Part I of this article.

(2) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Landscaping for a project that qualifies for a development bonus.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping must be provided as shown on the landscape plan (Exhibit S-174B). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the landscape plan, the text of this division controls.

(A) A minimum of 10 percent of the site area must be designated landscape site area.

(B) A minimum of 60 percent of the required front yard must be designated as landscape site area.

(C) A minimum of 12 percent of the required front yard must be designated as general planting area.

(D) A minimum of six percent of the required front yard must be designated special planting area.

(2) Landscaping must consist of a habitat garden.

(3) The chief arborist may allow for relocation of plantings at the time of permit, if necessary to allow for conflicts with utilities or driveways.

(4) The landscaping must be maintained with industry best practices to promote the healthy development and maintenance of pollinator habitats. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Development             Bonuses          For     Mixed-Income
174.text:
SEC. S-174.114. DEVELOPMENT BONUSES FOR MIXED-INCOME HOUSING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A- 4.1100, as amended, is required to obtain the development bonuses in Section S-174.108.

(b) Reserved units. The height and floor area ratio development bonuses set forth in Section S-174.108 apply if five percent of residential units are made available to households earning between 61 percent to 80 percent of area median family income.

(c) Development regulations. Except as provided in this subsection, compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is required.

(1) Architectural elements.

(A) Architectural elements, such as, architecturally prominent public entrances, canopies, awnings, building material variations, variations in building massing, increased transparency, and variations in fenestration must be provided adjacent to all building corners and at public entry points.

(B) Along the Katy Trail, Hall Street, Carlisle Place, and Carlisle Street, transparency is required for every 50 linear feet of continuous street-fronting and open-space- fronting facade.

(C) Building entries must be architecturally prominent and clearly visible from the street.

(D) Blank walls longer than 30 feet in length are prohibited. Where blank walls occur, horizontal or vertical articulation is required.

(2) Open space. Minimum open space is 20,000 square feet. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Signs
174.text:
SEC. S-174.115. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non- business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signs located above the third story may not be illuminated. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Infrastructure Improvements
174.text:
SEC. S-174.116. INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) The building official shall not issue a final certificate of occupancy for new construction unless the property owner provides evidence that an application has been made to the traffic engineer to install signs prohibiting parking on Hall Street between Carlisle Street and the Katy Trail in accordance with Section 28-26 of the Dallas City Code.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit for new construction until an apportionment determination has been made in accordance with Section 51A-1.109 for a traffic signal upgrade at the intersection of Carlisle Street and Hall Street.

(c) The building official shall not issue a building permit for new construction until a contract is entered into for the installation of detection equipment and an accessible pedestrian signal at the intersection of Carlisle Street and Hall Street. Any cost sharing for the installation must be documented in a cost sharing contract pursuant to Section 51A-8.614. (Ord. 32904)

174.title: Additional Provisions
174.text:
SEC. S-174.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) In general.

(1) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(2) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(3) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article.

(b) For a project that qualifies for a development bonus pursuant to Section S-174.114.

(1) Outdoor dining is prohibited after 11:00 p.m.

(2) Amplified outdoor noise may not exceed 63 decibels and may not be utilized after 10:00 p.m.

SEC. S-174-118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 32904)

175.title: Article heading
175.text: Division S-175. PD Subdistrict 175.

175.title: Legislative History
175.text:
SEC. S-175.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD Subdistrict 175 was established by Ordinance No. 33036, passed by the Dallas City Council on March 26, 2025. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Property Location And Size
175.text:
SEC. S-175.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD Subdistrict 175 is established on property bounded by Cedar Springs Road, Maple Avenue, McKinney Avenue, and Pearl Street. The size of PD Subdistrict 175 is approximately 9.9414 acres. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Definitions And Interpretations
175.text:
SEC. S-175.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51 and Part I of this article apply to this division. If there is a conflict, this division controls. If there is a conflict between Chapter 51 and Part I of this article, Part I of this article controls.

(b) In this division:

(1) HABITAT GARDEN means any planting areas that are native or native adaptive species to north Texas with low water or very low water consumption characteristics with the intention of attracting or providing habitat for bees, birds, butterflies, or other pollinators.

(2) MICRO-MOBILITY CHARGING SPACE means an electrical charging station or outlet available for charging a micro-mobility vehicle, such as an e-scooter or e-bike.

(3) NEW DRIVEWAY means a driveway that is constructed after March 26, 2025. For purposes of this definition, repairs that are necessary to maintain driveways constructed prior to March 26, 2025, are permitted and do not constitute a new driveway.

(4) NEW SIDEWALK means a sidewalk that is required to be constructed after March 26, 2025. For purposes of this definition, repairs that are necessary to maintain sidewalks constructed prior to March 26, 2025, are permitted and do not constitute a new sidewalk.

(5) SUBDISTRICT means a subdistrict of PD 193.

(c) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this division are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51.

(d) This subdistrict is considered to be a non-residential zoning district. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Exhibits
175.text:
SEC. S-175.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this division:

(1) Exhibit S-175A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit S-175B: Subarea A development plan.

(3) Exhibit S-175C: Subarea A landscape plan.

(4) Exhibit S-175D: Subarea B landscape plan.

(5) Exhibit S-175E: Environmental and sustainable design compliance scorecard. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Creation Of Subareas
175.text:
SEC. S-175.105. CREATION OF SUBAREAS.

This subdistrict is divided into two subareas: Subareas A and B, as shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit S-175A). (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Conceptual Plan
175.text:
SEC. S-175.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the conceptual plan, the text of this division controls. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Development Plan
175.text:
SEC. S-175.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Subarea A.

(1) Development and use of Subarea A must comply with the Subarea A development plan (Exhibit S-175B). If there is a conflict between the text of this division and the Subarea A development plan, the text of this division controls.

(2) The following are not required to be shown on the Subarea A development plan:

(A) Generators and equipment no taller than eight feet in height.

(B) Signs.

(b) Subarea B. No development plan is required, and the provisions of Section 51- 4.702 requiring submission of or amendments to a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, and development schedule do not apply. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Main Uses Permitted
175.text:
SEC. S-175.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted in this subdistrict are those main uses permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, subject to the same conditions applicable in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict, as set out in Part I of this article. For example, a use permitted in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict only by specific use permit
(SUP) is permitted in this subdistrict only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review
(DIR) in the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict is subject to DIR in this subdistrict; etc.

(b) The following use is permitted by right:

-- Helistop. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Accessory Uses
175.text:
SEC. S-175.109. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subdistrict in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51P-193.108. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51P-193.108. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
175.text:
SEC. S-175.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Part I of this article. If there is a conflict between this section and Part I of this article, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the HC Heavy Commercial Subdistrict apply.

(b) Floor area ratio. Maximum floor area ratio is 5.1:1.

(c) Height.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 285 feet.

(2) Subarea A. If compliant with Section S-175.117, maximum structure height is 415 feet.

(3) Projections. The following structures may project a maximum of 20 feet above the maximum structure height:

(A) Cooling tower.

(B) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(C) Mechanical equipment room and any visual screens which surround mechanical equipment.

(D) Skylights.

(E) Observation deck.

(F) Chimney and vent stacks.

(G) Parapet walls or guard rails.

(H) Helistop.

(d) Encroachments. The following additional items are permitted to be located within the required setbacks:

(1) Seat walls, retaining walls, stoops, porches, steps, unenclosed balconies, ramps, handrails, safety railings, and benches all not exceeding four feet in height and extending a maximum of five feet into the required setbacks.

(2) Landscape planters.

(3) Sculptures.

(4) Canopies or awnings.

(e) Front yard fences. A maximum four-foot-high fence with at least 75 percent transparency is allowed in the required front yard. A maximum four-foot-high handrail may be located on retaining walls in the required front yard. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
175.text:
SEC. S-175.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Off-street parking. For purposes of off-street parking, a minimum of 2,538 parking spaces must be provided for shared use by any use within this subdistrict. The specific off-street parking requirements for each use in Part I and Division 51-4.200 do not apply.

(b) Off-street loading.

(1) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult Part I of this article for the specific loading requirements for each use.

(2) Subarea A. If the increased development standard in Section S- 175.110(c)(2) is used, one medium size loading space is required, and the requirement in Section 51P-193.115(b)(2)(B), that one off-street loading space must be of large size, does not apply. The medium size loading space must be screened from the right-of-way.

(c) Passenger loading in Subarea A.

(1) A minimum of two off-street passenger loading spaces must be provided.

(2) A minimum of three on-street passenger loading spaces must be provided. The required on-street passenger loading zones must be constructed in compliance with the Architectural Barrier Act accessibility standards and must be approved by the director and by the director of transportation and public works. If the directors do not approve the passenger loading spaces, the on-street passenger loading spaces are not required. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Environmental Performance Standards
175.text:
SEC. S-175.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Landscaping
175.text:
SEC. S-175.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Subarea A. Landscaping must be provided as shown on the Subarea A landscape plan (Exhibit S-175C), and the following irrigation tools must be implemented:

(1) Drip irrigation must be used for landscaping and plantings.

(2) Condensate from mechanical equipment must be captured and reused for irrigation.

(3) Detention and rainwater harvesting must be used for irrigation.

(b) Subarea B. Landscaping must be provided as shown on the Subarea B landscape plan (Exhibit S-175D).

(c) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Subarea A Design Standards
175.text:
SEC. S-175.114. SUBAREA A DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) New sidewalks.

(1) Except for driveways and drop off areas, new sidewalks must provide a minimum unobstructed width of six feet at all times.

(2) A minimum five-foot-wide planting zone must be provided between the back of the curb and a new sidewalk.

(3) Subject to approval of the director, across all driveways and curb cuts, new sidewalks must be:

(A) continuous and level with the adjoining sidewalks;

(B) designed to be at the same grade as the adjoining sidewalk; and

(C) clearly marked by colored concrete, patterned or stamped concrete, or brick pavers to indicate pedestrian crossing.

(b) Pedestrian amenities. A minimum of one trash receptacle and a minimum of one pet refuse container must be provided along Cedar Springs Road and Maple Avenue.

(c) Building design.

(1) Transparency. A minimum 30 percent transparency must be provided for the street-facing facade, up to 30 feet in height.

(2) Facade articulation. Blank facades longer than 30 linear feet are prohibited. Where blank facades occur, a minimum of one of the following horizontal or vertical articulations is required:

(A) A minimum of one change in plane for each 30 feet of horizontal or vertical articulation, such as an offset, reveal, recess, or projection. Changes in plane must have a width of no less than 24 inches and depth of at least eight inches and may include columns, planters, arches, and niches.

(B) Architectural details, such as raised bands or cornices.

(C) Architecturally prominent entrances.

(D) Increased transparency.

(E) Attached tower or turret.

(F) Variations in fenestration or building massing.

(G) Canopies.

(H) Awnings.

(I) Balconies.

(J) Change in building materials.

(d) New driveways. A maximum of two new driveways are permitted, each with a maximum width of 24 feet.

(e) Pedestrian scale lighting. For a development greater than 20,000 square feet of floor area, pedestrian scale lighting that provides a minimum maintained average illumination level of 1.5 footcandles must be provided along public sidewalks and adjacent to public streets. The design and placement of both the standards and fixtures must be approved by the director of the department of transportation and public works.

(f) Exterior amplified sound. Use of exterior amplified sound is prohibited after 11:00 p.m., Monday through Sunday. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Environmental And Sustainable Design Test
175.text:
SEC. S-175.115. ENVIRONMENTAL AND SUSTAINABLE DESIGN TEST REQUIREMENTS.

(a) In general. This subdistrict must earn at least 200 points by providing any combination of the sustainable design features described in the environmental and sustainable design compliance scorecard (Exhibit S-175E).

(b) Determination of compliance. Documentation of how this subdistrict achieves 200 points on the environmental and sustainable design compliance scorecard must be submitted with an application for a building permit for new construction. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Signs
175.text:
SEC. S-175.116. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Mixed-Income Housing In Subarea A
175.text:
SEC. S-175.117. MIXED-INCOME HOUSING IN SUBAREA A.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, compliance with Division 51A- 4.1100 is required to obtain the height bonus in Section S-175.110(c)(2).

(b) Reserved dwelling units. Five percent of the total residential dwelling units must be made available to households earning between 81 percent to 100 percent of the area median family income.

(c) Design standards. Compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is not required. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Additional Provisions
175.text:
SEC. S-175.118. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with Part I of this article. (Ord. 33036)

175.title: Compliance With Conditions
175.text:
SEC. S-175.119. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this subdistrict until there has been full compliance with this division, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 33036)
